works.title: Engineering Vision: The Comparative Role of 3D Printing and 3D Bioprinting in Corneal Regeneration
works.abstract: Abstract Corneal blindness remains a major global cause of vision loss, and the limited availability of donor tissue has intensified efforts to engineer functional corneal substitutes with appropriate optical, mechanical, and biological performance. Advances in additive manufacturing have positioned 3D printing and 3D bioprinting as promising platforms for fabricating anatomically informed constructs that may recapitulate key aspects of the cornea's hierarchical architecture. This review provides a mechanistic comparison of these technologies with respect to material systems and (bio)ink formulation, processing strategies, scaffold architecture, cell incorporation, and biological integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the trade-off between high-fidelity 3D-printed scaffolds that can be seeded after fabrication and cell-laden bioprinted constructs that better capture early cell-matrix interactions but remain constrained by bioink rheology, resolution, mechanical integrity, and shape retention.The review further examines emerging strategies, including decellularized extracellular matrix bioinks, functionally graded hydrogels, and hybrid electrospun-printed constructs, for improving bioactivity, structural mimicry, collagen alignment, optical transmittance, and stromal-like extracellular matrix deposition. Persistent challenges include nanoscale and membrane-like architectural replication, longterm phenotype stability, reproducible manufacturing, surgical handling, storage, and regulatory classification of combination products. By integrating material science, fabrication physics, cellular responses, and translational considerations, this review delineates the complementary roles of 3D printing and 3D bioprinting and identifies the key design criteria required to advance printed corneal constructs toward clinically translatable regeneration.

works.title: A patient-derived, autologous component-integrated biomimetic hydrogel system for lung cancer organoid culture and recapitulation of immunotherapy response
works.abstract: Abstract Background: Matrigel-based culture of patient-derived lung cancer organoids (LCOs) is limited by undefined composition, batch-to-batch variability, and immunogenicity, which compromise experimental reproducibility and drug response readouts. Methods: We developed an autologous component-integrated hydrogel by incorporating patient-derived decellularized lung fiber fragments (1.25 μm diameter; 52.5 μm length) and optimized autologous plasma (56 °C, 30 min; 8,000×g, 5 min; 5% v/v) into a porous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) network. Five formulations—GelMA, GelMA+ fiber, GelMA + plasma, MC-GelMA (fibers + plasma) and Matrigel—were compared to dissect component contributions. LCOs were established from 8 patients, and PBMC co-culture experiments were performed with 3 samples (1 PD-L1-positive, 2 PD-L1-negative). Results: MC-GelMA exhibited uniform porosity and a Young’s modulus of 15.67 ± 0.86 kPa, closely matching native lung tumor tissue. Compared with Matrigel, LCOs cultured in MC-GelMA exhibited in vivo-like morphology, enhanced viability and metabolic activity, and preservation of key histological and genomic features.The platform supported stable long-term culture through passage 9 with maintained drug sensitivity. Component analysis revealed that fibers mainly provided structural and mechanical cues, while plasma supplied biochemical signals; their combination synergistically enhanced organoid growth and immune cell infiltration. In co-culture, MC-GelMA recapitulated anti-PD-L1 responses: PD-L1-positive organoids showed increased LDH release, whereas PD-L1-negative organoids did not respond. Conclusion: In conclusion, this autologous component-integrated biomimetic hydrogel serves as a highly reproducible biofabrication platform for stable LCO culture and reliable recapitulation of patient-specific immunotherapy response patterns. Further validation in larger cohorts is warranted to establish its predictive potential for clinical immunotherapy outcomes.

works.title: Optimized Vacuum-Sputtered Gold Nanoparticle-Modified Titanium Dioxide Nanotubes for Ultrasensitive Myocardial Infarction Multi-Biomarker Detection
works.abstract: Myocardial infarction, a sudden reduction in blood flow to the heart, requires rapid and sensitive detection of biomarkers reflecting different stages of cardiac injury and plaque destabilization. Herein, a universal electrochemical biosensing platform based on gold nanoparticle-modified titanium dioxide nanotubes (AuNPs/TNTs) was developed for the detection of cardiac troponin T (cTnT), heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A). Titanium dioxide nanotubes with a diameter of 50 ± 5 nm and a length of 1000 ± 100 nm, previously optimized for electrochemical and adsorption properties, were modified with AuNPs by vacuum sputtering at 20 mA for 10, 20, and 40 s. The influence of nanoparticle deposition on the morphology, phase composition, surface chemistry, wettability, and electrochemical properties of AuNPs/TNTs was systematically investigated. The AuNPs/TNTs sample prepared by Au sputtering for 10 s exhibited the most favorable physicochemical properties for biosensing applications. After nanocomposite functionalization, the platform enabled impedimetric detection of cTnT, H-FABP, and PAPP-A in clinically relevant concentration ranges. The obtained limits of detection for cTnT, H-FABP, and PAPP-A were 0.01, 0.23, and 0.008 ng/mL, respectively. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first AuNPs/TNTs-based electrochemical platform for the detection of cTnT, H-FABP, and PAPP-A. In addition, no AuNPs/TNTs electrochemical biosensor for PAPP-A determination has been reported to date.

works.title: Fabrication of Multiscale Porous Hydrogel Scaffold for Air–Liquid Interface Culture of Epithelial Cells Using Nebulized CaCl2-Assisted Three-Step Cross-Linking Three-Dimensional Printing
works.abstract: Creating thick tissue constructs that can enable air-liquid interface (ALI) culture is of great interest for the culture of epithelial cells. This paper presents a method of using nebulized calcium chloride (CaCl2)-assisted three-dimensional printing with a sacrificial polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) porogen component for the fabrication of a thick, multiscale porous scaffold for ALI cell culture. The ink used for scaffold fabrication is composed of gelatin microgels, PVA, sodium alginate, and a continuous gelatin solution. This fabrication approach utilizes ionic in situ cross-linking of sodium alginate using nebulized CaCl2, in addition to gelatin microgel jamming-based physical cross-linking during printing and enzymatic cross-linking of gelatin-based scaffolds post-printing, to create a robust structure, incorporating three different cross-linking steps. Exposure to the nebulized CaCl2 increases the storage modulus of the gel from 150 Pa to over 700 Pa and increases printing fidelity significantly. After cross-linking, the PVA component is leached from the scaffold, creating a network of pores to enhance transport. Printed scaffolds are able to transport 10 kDa molecules, roughly analogous to standard protein sizes. For applications in cell culture, the printing approach described here is used to fabricate a thick cylindrical scaffold with multiscale porosity, with printed macropores present in all but the solid top layer and micropores throughout the entire scaffold. Cells cultured on such porous scaffolds maintain a high degree of confluence, with an 88.1% surface coverage, while being exposed to air for multiple days. To demonstrate potential use of this approach to create drug screening platforms, cells grown on the scaffolds are exposed to the cancer drug Ulixertinib, delivered via scaffold transport. These results demonstrate that the presented fabrication method can be used to make porous scaffolds for the creation of an ALI culture environment, an important step towards biomimetic ALI models for biomedical applications, including therapeutic screening.

works.title: Supramolecular Tetrahydrocurcumin–Cyclodextrin for Enhanced Antioxidant, Anti-inflammatory, and Whitening Effects
works.abstract: Abstract Tetrahydrocurcumin (THC) is an active metabolite of curcumin with similar pharmacological activities, such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. However, the poor water solubility of THC results in low bioavailability and thus limits its application. We have developed a supramolecular encapsulation delivery system. Firstly, THC and citric acid (CA) were prepared into supramolecular THC-CA, and then hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) was added to prepare supramolecular THC-CA-CD. The supramolecular THC-CA-CD can self-assemble into spherical particles with a diameter of 156 nm in solution, achieving an encapsulation efficiency of 92.43%, aiming to improve its stability and bioavailability. Compared to free THC, the supramolecular THC-CA-CD exhibits stronger antioxidant capacity, anti-inflammatory effects (inhibiting IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1α), and the ability to inhibit tyrosinase activity. Additionally, the supramolecular THC-CA-CD was used as an active ingredient in a cosmetic cream for efficacy evaluation. The results showed that a 0.5% supramolecular THC-CA-CD skin cream increased the individual type angle (ITA°) value by 46.15%, decreased the melanin index (MI) value by 32.84%, and significantly increased the skin lightness (L) value by 44.06% within 4 weeks. In summary, the supramolecular THC-CA-CD exhibits whitening, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects.

works.title: Engineered microorganisms drive local metabolic reprogramming to Re-educate systemic immunity
works.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) features chronic synovial inflammation and systemic immune disorders. Current treatments mainly rely on systemic immunosuppression, raising risks of infection and long-term immune injury. Local therapies reduce such risks but struggle to regulate systemic immunity. Emerging studies show the synovial immunometabolic microenvironment links local inflammation to systemic responses. Here, we developed a strategy based on chemically attenuated photosynthetic bacteria that couples lactate metabolism with photo-driven hydrogen production to achieve local metabolic reprogramming and systemic immune re-education. We screened a photosynthetic bacterial strain with high lactate metabolic capacity, which also exhibited enhanced hydrogen production. To ensure safety, bacteria were PEGylated to mask immunogenic moieties while preserving metabolic activity. Intra-articular injection disrupted pathological crosstalk and restored the Treg/Th17 balance locally. Circulating IL-6 levels decreased, restoring the systemic regulatory role of Tregs, thereby alleviating distant joint inflammation. These results demonstrate that local synovial metabolic reprogramming by engineered bacteria can induce systemic immune re-education, offering a conceptually new therapeutic strategy for treating autoimmune arthritis.

works.title: Pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface coordinates infection control and osseointegration
works.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) compromises osseointegration through bacterial colonisation and dysregulated inflammation. Here, we pre-established a living biointerface by seeding immunity-and-matrix-regulatory cells (IMRCs) onto three-dimensional (3D)-printed titanium prostheses modified with silver (Ag) by plasma immersion ion implantation (Ag-PIII) before bacterial exposure, generating an IMRC-seeded Ag-PIII-modified titanium (TAM) construct. TAM was associated with reduced bacterial attachment. The Ag-PIII-modified substrate achieved antibacterial efficiencies above 99% against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli while supporting IMRC viability and attachment. TAM-conditioned medium favoured an M2-like macrophage profile, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. In the beagle PJI model, TAM reduced bacterial recovery and peri-implant inflammation and improved bone formation, fixation strength, and locomotor performance at 8 weeks. These findings provide preclinical support for pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface to alter the initial conditions of surface competition and integrate early infection control with subsequent osseointegration.

works.title: Engineered Milk‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles Integrate PCSK9 Silencing and Inflammation Modulation for Hyperlipidemia Therapy
works.abstract: Hyperlipidemia is a systemic metabolic disorder closely associated with chronic inflammation. Effective management requires integrated strategies that simultaneously lower lipid level and attenuate inflammation. Nucleic acid therapeutics, such as proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) siRNA, represent a breakthrough in lipid-lowering therapy. However, they either lack direct anti-inflammatory effects (GalNAc-siRNA) or are prone to triggering unintended inflammatory responses themselves such as lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Milk-derived extracellular vesicles (MDEs) emerge as naturally anti-inflammatory nanocarriers that suppress key pro-inflammatory cytokines by 30.0%-96.5% in vitro. However, MDEs predominantly undergo endocytic trafficking with substantial endosomal/lysosomal sequestration, which can limit productive cytosolic siRNA delivery. To address this, we developed engineered MDEs by incorporating 30.0% (w/w) probiotic-derived glycolipids into their membranes to facilitate early endosomal escape. When loaded with PCSK9 siRNA, the engineered MDEs achieved a remarkable silencing efficiency of 90.2 ± 0.2%, significantly outperforming both unmodified MDEs and conventional LNPs. In hyperlipidemic mice, systemic administration of engineered MDEs improved serum lipid profiles, reduced lipid accumulation and systemic inflammation, and showed a favorable safety profile under the conditions examined. Collectively, this work provides a promising nucleic acid delivery platform based on engineered MDEs for enhanced hyperlipidemia therapy through simultaneous lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory effects.

works.title: Establishment of a Responsive Tooth‐on‐a‐Chip Platform for the Assessment of Regenerative Factors in Dental Tissue Regeneration
works.abstract: Tooth formation relies on reciprocal signaling between embryological dental epithelial (DE) and mesenchymal (DM) cells, orchestrating the formation of enamel, dentin, and vascularized pulp. Current regenerative strategies aim to recreate DE-DM signaling, yet responsive in vitro platforms that faithfully reconstruct this interface and enable benchmarking of candidate cues are unavailable. Herein, a tooth-on-a-chip with a reconstructed DE-DM interface was tested for cue-specific tissue maturation in vitro. The platform comprises a polydimethylsiloxane microfluidic device integrating a fibrin-based mesenchymal compartment with an overlying epithelial layer. The system was exposed to two developmental inducers, sequential fibroblast growth factor 10 (FGF10) and bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4), and BMP2, as well as the clinically used enamel matrix derivative Emdogain, to emulate distinct inductive environments. The platform robustly supported interface formation and revealed cue-specific maturation trajectories with high experimental reproducibility. Notably, Emdogain induced enamel organ-like structural maturation, revealing a previously unrecognized pro-enamel (amelogenic) activity of a biomaterial that has been used clinically for over three decades. Together, these findings validated the tooth-on-a-chip system as a biologically relevant in vitro test platform, providing a translational framework for benchmarking regenerative cues and guiding the development of dental regenerative therapies.

works.title: A Novel 3D Model Co‐Culturing Breast Cancer Cells in Direct Contact with Patient‐Derived Mature Adipocytes Demonstrates Cell‐Type Specific Alterations in Phenotype and Chemosensitivity
works.abstract: Mature adipocytes within the breast tumour microenvironment contribute a significant role in malignant progression. At the invasive front of breast tumours, mature adipocytes undergo morphological and phenotypic changes and may provide metabolic support to fuel tumour growth and spread. However, investigations into mature adipocyte-breast cancer interactions have been limited by the lack of suitable in vitro models. Here, we developed an innovative 3D in vitro co-culture system allowing direct contact between patient-derived mature breast adipocytes and breast cancer cell lines, to systematically examine cell-cell interactions over 21 days. In co-culture with triple negative breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-231), mature adipocytes exhibited loss of Perilipin 1 (PLIN1) expression and were associated with reduced chemotherapy responsiveness and increased Major Vault Protein (MVP) abundance. In contrast, Luminal A (MCF7) breast cancer cells displayed increased expression of mesenchymal markers (N-cadherin and Vimentin), consistent with a partial epithelial to mesenchymal transition. The direct 3D co-culture model developed by this work provides a novel platform to study breast cancer subtype-specific interactions between mature adipocytes and cancer cells, revealing interactions associated with chemotherapy responsiveness and malignant progression.

works.title: Adaptive MSC@ECM/PRP Matrix Sustains Transplanted Stem Cells and Restores Endometrial Regeneration
works.abstract: Stem cell-based therapy holds promise for endometrial regeneration but suffers from rapid cell loss in the oxidative and cytokine-deficient uterine niche. We developed a biomimetic decellularized extracellular matrix integrated with platelet-rich plasma (ECM/PRP) that serves as a bioactive cytokine reservoir designed to construct a supportive local microenvironment capable of retaining cytokines and maintaining transplanted cell viability. The ECM binds PRP-derived cytokines, stabilizing their bioactivity and converting burst release into sustained signaling. Adhered human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (HUC-MSCs) respond to these anchored cues, with changes in mitochondrial electron transport activity correlating with enhanced cellular antioxidant capacity. This ECM/PRP composite improves HUC-MSC survival, alleviating intracellular ROS, sustain their paracrine secretion under the IUA pathological microenvironment, and elevate the number of surviving transplanted HUC-MSCs in vivo. In a murine intrauterine adhesion (IUA) model, MSC@ECM/PRP enhanced endometrial proliferation and microvessel density while reducing collagen deposition. These coordinated changes facilitate reconstruction of physiological endometrial structure and produce a marked improvement in fertility relative to the untreated IUA group. Collectively, the adaptive MSC@ECM/PRP scaffold protects transplanted HUC-MSCs against oxidative stress in the IUA microenvironment, facilitates endometrial structural repair and angiogenesis, suppresses excessive fibrosis, and achieves satisfactory therapeutic and fertility-restoring effects in IUA.

works.title: Sequential Modeling of Fibrotic and Mineralizing Osteoarthritis‐Like Remodeling in hDPSC‐Derived Cartilage Microtissues
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) involves alterations in cartilage mechanics, matrix composition, and mineralization, yet in vitro models that resolve remodeling transitions remain limited. Scaffold-free cartilage microtissues derived from human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) are subjected to sequential dynamic rocking culture and triiodothyronine (T3) treatment. Dynamic rocking produces superficial Col I-positive fibrotic and matrix-degrading changes, whereas T3 induces proteoglycan loss, increased Col I and MMP13, irregular mineral deposition, and altered nanomechanical properties, defining a mixed terminal catabolic and mineralizing OA-like state. Transcriptomic profiling shows stage-associated reorganization rather than uniform pathway activation. In T3-treated microtissues, ATF6-associated ER-stress abnormalities include ER cisternal dilation and increased ATF6 signal. Targeted ATF6 knockdown reduces ATF6 signal, ER dilation, extracellular-matrix disorganization, and ER-stress/proteostasis and inflammatory/catabolic transcriptional module scores, supporting ATF6-associated signaling as a functionally relevant component of this degenerative state. In mouse temporomandibular joint and knee OA models, intra-articular Ad-shATF6 is associated with partial cartilage preservation and subchondral-bone indices shifted toward control ranges.

works.title: Dynamically Repairable Hydration‐Lubricating Microspheres for Osteoarthritis Therapy
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) progression is closely associated with the deterioration of joint lubrication. Although surface-grafted lubrication coatings can reduce friction, they are susceptible to mechanical damage under repetitive shear stress, resulting in rapid lubrication failure. Therefore, constructing a dynamically reconfigurable lubrication interface capable of continuous restoration under friction is critical for long-term joint protection. Herein, a dynamically self-repairing hydration lubrication microsphere system (HMs-CD@Ad-PMPC) is developed based on host-guest interactions. β-Cyclodextrin (β-CD)-functionalized silk fibroin microspheres dynamically recruit adamantane (Ad)-terminated poly(2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC) brushes through supramolecular host-guest recognition, thereby establishing a robust yet reversible hydration lubrication interface. Under shear stress during joint motion, partial dissociation of Ad-PMPC chains induces transient lubrication attenuation, while spontaneous molecular reassembly rapidly restores the lubrication interface upon stress release, thereby enabling dynamic self-repairing lubrication. In vitro, HMs-CD@Ad-PMPC maintains a stable low coefficient of friction (COF, 0.03-0.04) under cyclic shear conditions, exhibiting excellent wear resistance and long-term lubrication stability. In vivo, the system effectively reduces joint wear, preserves cartilage integrity, and significantly delays OA progression. This work establishes a dynamic lubrication strategy capable of restoring interfacial functionality under mechanical stress, providing a promising platform for long-term joint lubrication and OA therapy.

works.title: Author Correction: A HO-1 gene knockout using a NanoCRISPR scaffold suppresses metastasis in mouse models
ROS-responsive Se@HSC-DIA enables local drug delivery and modulates CD44high inflammatory nucleus pulposus cell states in intervertebral disc degeneration
works.abstract: Low back pain is closely associated with structural abnormalities of the spine, yet how altered mechanical loading drives persistent disc inflammation and pain remains unclear. Here, we investigated the cellular mechanisms linking structural disturbance to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) and developed a mechanism-guided local therapy. Human disc specimens from patients with lumbar spondylolysis (LS), integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets, primary nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs), pharmacological perturbation, and an in vivo IVDD model were analyzed. LS-associated discs showed increased NOX4 and CD44 expression with enhanced oxidative stress and inflammation. Single-cell analysis identified a CD44 high inflammatory NP population (Inflamed NP) that expanded with degeneration severity. Oxidative stress promoted this state, whereas IL-1β-IL-1R1 signaling and canonical NF-κB activation sustained its inflammatory and matrix-catabolic phenotype. Drug screening identified diacerein (DIA) as an effective inhibitor of this axis. We therefore developed Se@HSC-DIA, an injectable hydrogel that responds to reactive oxygen species (ROS) and integrates CD44 affinity, ROS-triggered DIA release, and selenium nanoparticle-mediated antioxidant activity. Se@HSC-DIA reduced ROS, NF-κB activation, inflammatory mediators, and matrix catabolism in NPCs. In vivo, it preserved disc structure, restored matrix homeostasis, alleviated pain-related behavior, and shifted the degenerative transcriptome toward homeostasis without evident systemic toxicity. These findings define a ROS-IL-1β/IL-1R1-NF-κB axis linking structural stress to an inflammatory NP state and support microenvironment-responsive biomaterials for IVDD therapy.

works.title: PSMA-targeted nanoparticles delivering ATR and Src/Bcr-Abl inhibitors to stimulate STING and reprogram senescence-associated secretory phenotype for enhancing immunotherapy in prostate cancer
works.abstract: Significant increases in the proportion of senescent cells were observed in prostate cancer following endocrine therapy. Although treatment-induced senescence (TIS) effectively suppresses cancer cell proliferation, the long-term accumulation of the immunosuppressive senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) promotes immune evasion, leading to the failure of immunotherapy. Herein, a liposomal nanoparticle (T-Lipo@Das/Ber) encapsulating the ATR inhibitor Berzosertib and the Src/Bcr-Abl inhibitor Dasatinib was designed, which can target prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). T-Lipo@Das/Ber efficiently enters cells via PSMA-mediated endocytosis. On the one hand, Berzosertib inhibits ATR, increases DNA damage, and induces the release of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory factors via the cGAS-STING pathway, ultimately enhancing tumor immunogenicity. On the other hand, by inhibiting the Src/Bcr-Abl pathway, Dasatinib reprograms the SASP, reducing the secretion of immunosuppressive factors while promoting the exposure of calreticulin (CRT) and the release of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), thereby synergistically recruiting and activating immune cells. With the stimulation of both innate and adaptive immune responses, “immune cold tumor” is transformed into “immune hot tumor”. When combined with αPD-1, it not only effectively inhibits the growth of the primary tumor, but also induces long-term immune memory to prevent tumor recurrence.

works.title: Constructing functionalized cartilage organoids by preserving mitochondrial homeostasis to accelerate cartilage repair
works.abstract: Due to the lack of blood vessels and nerves in cartilage tissue, its regeneration and repair has always been a clinical challenge. Cartilage organoids (COs) are miniature cartilage tissues cultivated using stem cells or chondrocytes, which have a broad application prospect in the field of cartilage regeneration and repair. However, prolonged scaffold-based culture of COs is often accompanied by chondrocyte hypertrophy and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which may compromise the maintenance of a stable cartilage phenotype. In this study, transcriptomic analysis of COs cultured for up to 8 weeks revealed stage-dependent changes in stress- and matrix-related programs and suggested that altered mitochondrial homeostasis may be associated with phenotypic deterioration. To address this problem, this study constructed a MnO 2 -Melatonin@DNA-SF hydrogel (Mn-Me@DSH) bioink matrix by loading MnO 2 nanoparticles and Melatonin on DNA-SF hydrogels. Subsequently, we bioprinted BMSCs with Mn-Me@DSH using a DLP system to produce a functionalized COs that could maintain mitochondrial homeostasis. These engineered COs effectively repaired cartilage defects in rats within 6 weeks. This study breaks through the limitations of the traditional COs in the oxidative stress microenvironment through the ROS scavenging, and provides a new solution for the construction of functionalized COs and cartilage regeneration.

works.title: An i-Motif-gated DNA-based nanoassembly enables pH-responsive biofilm control and enamel remineralization for initial caries therapy
works.abstract: Dental caries is a biofilm-mediated disease characterized by acidogenic microbial dysbiosis and enamel demineralization. Current antibacterial and remineralization strategies are often limited by poor penetration into cariogenic biofilms, nonselective antimicrobial activity, and the acid instability of mineral precursors. Here, we developed an i-Motif-gated DNA-based nanoassembly that integrates biofilm penetration, pH-responsive biofilm control, and biomimetic enamel regeneration for initial caries therapy. The nanoassembly was constructed by co-assembling i-Motif-forming DNA strands, DNA-templated silver nanoclusters and amorphous calcium phosphate precursors. In a validated three-species streptococcal biofilm model, the nanoassembly exhibited efficient penetration throughout the biofilm matrix. Under acidic cariogenic conditions, folding of the i-Motif structure promoted the release of silver-containing species, resulting in enhanced antibacterial activity against cariogenic-state biofilms while exerting minimal effects under relatively non-cariogenic conditions. Simultaneously, protonation of the DNA scaffold stabilized the amorphous calcium phosphate against acid dissolution down to pH 4.0, facilitating the regeneration of densely packed enamel-like crystals. In a rat caries model, topical treatment effectively suppressed cariogenic bacterial colonization and minimized lesion development without disrupting oral microbial diversity. These findings demonstrate that programmable DNA nanoassemblies can couple pH-responsive antibacterial activation with biomimetic mineralization, providing a promising strategy for precise management of initial caries.

works.title: Bioadhesive calcium phosphate cement with nano-whitlockite for vascularized bone regeneration
works.abstract: Calcium phosphate cements are widely used in bone repair but are limited by inadequate mechanical strength, weak bone adhesion, slow resorption, and limited angiogenic activity. Here, we developed a multifunctional bone cement based on tetracalcium phosphate and phosphoserine, incorporating poly(methyl vinyl ether-alt-maleic acid) (PMVE-MA) and Mg-containing nano-whitlockite (nWH). The optimized formulation, C-PM15-W20, exhibited significantly enhanced compressive and adhesive strength compared with a commercial hydroxyapatite-forming cement. It also demonstrated favorable handling characteristics, aqueous stability, and gradual degradation under both physiological and mildly acidic conditions. In a synthetic osteoporotic bone model, C-PM15-W20 achieved pedicle screw pull-out strength comparable to commercial PMMA and hydroxyapatite-forming cement controls. In vitro, nWH incorporation promoted HUVEC migration and tube formation while enhancing osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization, whereas PMVE-MA-containing formulations reduced LPS-stimulated IL-1β and TNF-α expression, indicating modulation of selected pro-inflammatory responses. In vivo, C-PM15-W20 enhanced bone regeneration in rat calvarial and rabbit iliac defect models, with increased new bone formation. Specifically, the rat calvarial model showed increased new bone formation and vascularization, while rabbit iliac model showed increased new bone formation and bone-material contact. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that C-PM15-W20 integrates improved mechanical performance, bone adhesion, degradability, angiogenic activity, and osteogenic potential, supporting its potential as a multifunctional bone cement for regenerative bone repair.

works.title: Genetically engineered extracellular vesicles with chimeric antigen receptors of human stem cell-derived neutrophils targeting fibroblast activation protein to modulate tumor microenvironment
works.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most commonly occurring central nervous system tumor, accounting for over 50% of gliomas, with a poor survival rate. A primary driver of GBM progression is the fibrotic stroma, where excess extracellular matrix deposition creates a dense network that excludes immune cells and chemotherapeutic agents. While targeting tumor-associated fibroblasts (TAFs) via fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cells is a promising strategy, off-target toxicities limit the clinical utility of the treatment. To address these safety concerns, extracellular vesicles (EVs) of FAP-CAR-engineered neutrophils differentiated from human pluripotent stem cells were isolated and characterized, including proteomic profile, microRNA content, in vitro bioactivity, and in vivo biodistribution in this study. Multi-omic profiling revealed that CAR engineering enriched EVs with proinflammatory proteins, iron-transferring proteins, and proliferation regulators, and a significant upregulation of miRNAs targeting FAP and proliferation-regulating genes was observed. Functional in vitro assays demonstrated that these EVs are selectively cytotoxic to TAFs, reducing the expression of BCL-2 and RAS-MAPK-ERK signaling pathway genes. These EVs also demonstrated cytotoxicity to patient-derived GBM spheroids. Furthermore, in vivo biodistribution results confirmed that FAP-CAR EVs are capable of systemic circulation and payload delivery, showing a significant increase in accumulation within the liver and spleen compared to free Cy5.5. These findings suggest that CAR engineering enhances the ability of FAP-CAR EVs to inhibit TAF proliferation and induce apoptosis. FAP-targeting CAR EVs are positioned as a targeted bioengineered delivery platform with the potential for remodeling the tumor microenvironment and slowing the progression of desmoplasia in GBM.

works.title: Atomically dispersed nanoactivators drive innate mitochondrial biogenesis for active neuroprotection in ischemic stroke
works.abstract: Mitigating mitochondrial bioenergetic failure is a pivotal yet formidable neuroprotective goal in treating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues. RMV comprises atomically dispersed ruthenium sites anchored within an oxygen-deficient manganese hydroxide matrix via synergistic Ru–O–Mn bridges. Benefiting from its intrinsic mitochondriotropic properties, RMV effectively intercepts aberrant electron leakage and breaks the self-amplifying cycle of ROS-induced ROS release through cascade multi-enzyme mimetic activities. Importantly, transcriptomic profiling and ultrastructural analysis reveal that RMV transcends passive antioxidant defense by functioning as a bioactive switch. It revives the suppressed SIRT1–PGC1α–TFAM signaling axis, fundamentally driving mitochondrial biogenesis and the reconstruction of functionally intact respiratory chains. In a murine stroke model, RMV treatment induces a 1.52-fold expansion of the neuronal mitochondrial biomass under ischemic stress, thereby suppressing neuronal apoptosis, reducing infarct volumes, and favorably reshaping an M2-polarized neuroimmune microenvironment. These integrated effects yield robust and sustained neurofunctional recovery. Our study shifts the neuroprotective paradigm from reactive damage control to active mitochondrial biogenesis, offering an atomically engineered strategy for ischemic stroke management.

works.title: Bioinspired Buffered Microenvironment Enables Highly Crystalline 3D COF Gels With Controllable Structures for Exceptional Molecular Adsorption
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling long‐range crystallinity with macroscopic network formation remains a central challenge in constructing three‐dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF) gels. Inspired by biomineralization and tofu coagulation, we propose a synergistic buffered system with salt bridges for direct assembly of crystalline 3D COF gels via imine condensation. Ten metal salts were selected to regulate stable and buffered pH microenvironment. Comparing various salts revealed a correlation between pH microenvironment and the formation state and crystallinity of COFs. NaAc emerges as representative regulator for multiple roles: (i) forming AcO − /AcOH buffer to maintain a stable weakly acidic microenvironment and promote disorder‐to‐order transition, (ii) regulating kinetics, defect healing, and COF topology, and (iii) Na + as salt bridges stabilizing the 3D gel network. Pore topology can be switched between two crystalline phases by varying side substituents and salt addition sequence, as seen by XRD peak shift from 8.9° to 6.6°. The gels have low density (0.028–0.042 g/cm 3 ), high compressive strength, CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 140, organic solvent uptake up to 80 times their weight, and over 90% capacity retention after 20 cycles. Overall, this work establishes a paradigm from microenvironment engineering and ion selection to topology regulation and adsorption, providing a blueprint for functional 3D COF gels.

works.title: Lewis Acid‐Activated High‐Entropy Layered Double Hydroxide for Superior Seawater Electrolysis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater electrolysis has been identified as a sustainable approach for the industrialization of green hydrogen. However, this process is hindered by two significant factors: the sluggish anodic kinetics and chloride‐induced corrosion. In this study, we introduce Zn 2+ as a Lewis acid site into high‐entropy layered double hydroxide (LDH) to modulate both the interfacial microenvironment and the bulk electronic structure. The resulting catalyst requires overpotentials of 35 and 160 mV for the hydrogen/oxygen evolution reactions at 10 mA cm −2 , respectively, accompanied by small Tafel slopes. Furthermore, an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer demonstrates operational stability over a duration of 900 h at 1.5 A cm −2 . Theoretical and in situ analyses reveal that Zn 2+ exhibits a preference for adsorbing OH − , thereby repelling Cl − . Concurrently, this process induces oxygen vacancies and optimizes the d‑band centers of Fe/Co sites, establishing a interfacial/bulk dual regulation. This work offers a novel paradigm for the design of robust high‑entropy catalysts via Lewis acid doping for practical applications in harsh environments.

works.title: Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High‐Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure
works.abstract: Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities-such as metal-dielectric-metal nanopatch antennas-offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP-positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.

works.title: Mutual Waxing and Waning—A Novel Nano‐Biocomposite Harnesses the Lactate Gradient to Enhance Cuproptosis and Anti‐Tumor Immunity
works.abstract: Modifying the lactate gradient in tumors can induce acidosis and improve the immunosuppressive microenvironment. However, the therapeutic benefit is offset by compensatory metabolic adaptations and the inability of small-molecule drugs to regulate the gradient throughout the tumor tissue. This study developed a novel nano-biocomposite (LOB@CDSH) that combines cuproptosis to damage mitochondria and cut off energy supply, thereby improving the therapeutic outcome of acidosis induction. Simultaneously, it utilizes the invasive and tumor-colonizing capabilities of engineered bacteria to efficiently reduce lactate levels within tumor tissues. The MCT4 inhibitor syrosingopine (Syro) was loaded into a reactive oxygen species-responsive copper-based metal-organic framework (Cu-DTA) and coated with hyaluronic acid (HA) to form Cu-DTA@Syro@HA (CDSH). Syro inhibits lactate efflux, leading to intracellular lactate accumulation and acidosis. This promotes mitochondrial metabolism and induces lactylation modification of methyltransferase-like 16 (METTL16), thereby upregulating the expression of ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) to enhance cuproptosis. Lactate oxidase (LOX)-engineered Escherichia coli BL21 (LOB) serves as a carrier to deliver CDSH to the tumor site, where it proliferates, disseminates, and continuously expresses LOX to deplete lactate in the tumor microenvironment, thereby alleviating lactate-mediated immunosuppression. The aforementioned nano-biocomposite provides a reciprocally modulating strategy for lactate metabolism, offering a novel approach for tumor immunotherapy.

works.title: A 3D‐Printed Model of Human Lactation
works.abstract: Engineering physiologically relevant breast in vitro models remains challenging due to the gland's complex three-dimensional microanatomy, together with the need for epithelial polarity and hormone responsiveness. To overcome these challenges, fabrication methods are needed that rapidly create alveoli-scale structures with efficient diffusion and sustained hormonal stimulation. Here, Filamented Light (FLight) biofabrication is leveraged to print highly porous, ECM-based hydrogel scaffolds directly within standard Transwell inserts with separate apical and basal access. FLight's speckle-patterned laser generates multiscale scaffold architectures that integrate FLight channels (∼15 µm) to promote diffusion with alveoli-inspired cylindrical microwell arrays (Ø100, Ø150, and Ø200 µm) that impose geometric constraints to guide epithelial organization. Each insert is printed in <10 s and incorporates slow-release prolactin microcrystals to provide lactogenic stimulation in situ. Primary human milk-derived mammary epithelial cells (milk MECs) were seeded onto the constructs. There, milk MECs line the printed microwells, establish zona occludens-1-positive tight junctions, and express lactation-associated markers (prolactin receptor and β-casein), alongside milk fat globules and intracellular lipid droplets. Collectively, this rapidly reconfigurable FLight platform enables high-throughput generation of hormone-responsive human mammary microtissues for lactation-focused studies and is adaptable to other lumen-forming epithelia.

works.title: Influence of Microsphere‐to‐Hydrogel Matrix Composition on Long‐Term Volume Retention and Host Tissue Remodeling of Injectable Composite Collagen Hydrogels
works.abstract: The most commonly used materials for soft tissue augmentation, including autologous fat and hyaluronic acid, remain limited by inconsistent graft survival or repeated application to maintain volume. Composite collagen hydrogels (CCH) containing high-density crosslinked collagen microspheres embedded within a low-density collagen hydrogel, have demonstrated significantly enhanced vascularization, enabling simultaneous skin grafting and neodermis formation in one surgical step in preclinical models. Herein we evaluated an injectable form of the CCH (iCCH) to determine its long-term volume retention, host tissue integration, and remodeling following subcutaneous implantation. One percent collagen microspheres were mixed with 0.3% collagen hydrogel at microsphere-to-hydrogel ratios of 70:30 (MS70), 50:50 (MS50), and 30:70 (MS30). A microsphere-only formulation (MS-Only; 70:30 microsphere:PBS) and a 1% hyaluronic acid (HA) vehicle were included as controls. Each wild-type mouse received two 0.5 mL dorsal subcutaneous administrations of the assigned material. The iCCH formulations demonstrated cellular infiltration, neovascularization, and progressive inter-microsphere tissue remodeling, while MS70 showed near-complete construct volume retention at 12 months. Across the iCCH formulations, a mild and transient inflammatory response without evidence of an adverse foreign body reaction was observed. Overall, these findings support the potential of iCCH as a durable collagen scaffold for soft tissue augmentation.

works.title: Route‐Gated Lymphatic Delivery of Antigen‐Only Gliadin Nanoparticles for Celiac Disease‐Oriented Immune Modulation
works.abstract: Celiac disease (CeD) lacks approved pharmacologic therapy. Targeted delivery of antigens to immune inductive sites may provide a means to modulate pathogenic immune responses, yet practical delivery remains challenging. We show that minimal, adjuvant-free, self-assembled gliadin nanoparticles (L@GNP) attenuated antibody boosting after exploratory intravenous (i.v.) pre-exposure. Both soluble gliadin and L@GNP attenuated subsequent anti-gliadin antibody boosting under the tested i.v. conditions, with L@GNP providing a particulate antigen format with a controlled surface antigen positive rate. Rather than i.v. dosing, subcutaneous (s.c.) administration of L@GNP preferentially accessed draining lymphoid tissues and exhibited temporally coordinated uptake by multiple antigen-presenting cell (APC) populations, characterized by early CD11b+ myeloid-cell capture, transient B220+ cell involvement, and sustained enrichment in CD11c+ APCs at later time points. In a short-term CeD-like mouse model, L@GNP preserved villus architecture as indicated by higher V/C and reduced intestinal inflammation by lowering Transglutaminase 2 (TGM2) and key cytokines, rebalanced Th1/Th2, and increased Foxp3 expression, whereas a rapamycin-loaded counterpart (R/L@GNP) did not confer additional benefit at matched antigen doses. These data highlight route-gated lymphatic access and antigen-only simplicity as materials design principles for immunomodulatory nanomedicines.

works.title: Functional Construction Strategies and Multidimensional Applications of Kidney Organoids
works.abstract: Kidney diseases represent a major global health burden, highlighting the need for advanced human-relevant models to investigate disease mechanisms and develop therapeutic strategies. Stem cell-derived kidney organoids have emerged as powerful human-relevant platforms that recapitulate key aspects of kidney development and enable the modeling of renal diseases. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in kidney organoid construction and characterization and highlights key bioengineering strategies for improving their structural and functional properties. These strategies include decellularized extracellular matrix scaffolds, 3D bioprinting, genetic engineering, vascularization, and organoid-on-a-chip technologies. Their broad biomedical applications in disease modeling, drug screening, toxicity assessment, and regenerative medicine are further discussed. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are addressed, with emphasis on improving reproducibility, maturation, and functional relevance to advance the translational potential of kidney organoids.

works.title: On-Demand Fabrication of Nanofiber Mats with a Handheld Electrospinning Device for Flexible Postoperative Adhesion Barriers
works.abstract: Postoperative adhesions remain a major clinical challenge because currently available barrier materials often show limited conformability, insufficient mechanical robustness, and suboptimal performance under moist physiological conditions. Here, we investigated an on-demand strategy for the intraoperative fabrication of antiadhesion barriers using polyurethane dispersion (PUD) and poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) nanofiber (NF) mats fabricated by a handheld electrospinning device. The physicochemical properties, mechanical performance, degradation behavior, and cytocompatibility of the fabricated NF mats were characterized in vitro. PUD NF mat had superior wet-state mechanical stability, slower degradation, and stronger inhibition of fibroblast migration. Meanwhile, both materials showed favorable cytocompatibility. Antiadhesion efficacy was evaluated in a rat peritoneal ischemic button model, with assessment of gross adhesion formation, histological findings, and immunohistochemical and immunofluorescence markers of α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), Ki67, and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1). In situ electrospun NF mats reduced postoperative adhesion formation relative to controls. PUD showed the greatest reduction in adhesion incidence, tenacity, and histological fibrosis. PUD NF mats demonstrated antiadhesion efficacy comparable to that of Mediclore. The rapid PEO dissolution limited sustained barrier function despite partial macroscopic benefit. A handheld electrospinning device as a portable platform designed for on-demand antiadhesion barrier fabrication was successfully developed. PUD NF mats were identified as a promising candidate for preventing postoperative adhesions.

works.title: Defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerfaces enable ultrasound-amplified built-in electric fields for bacterial envelope destabilization and implant infection control
works.abstract: Built-in electric fields (BIEFs) at piezoelectric heterointerfaces are widely invoked to assist charge separation, but their contribution to antibacterial activity under ultrasound remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerface strategy to investigate BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects. Density functional theory (DFT)-guided screening identifies a dual-vacancy piezoelectric heterojunction (BTO 3-X /MoS 2-X ) with enhanced interfacial polarization. Under ultrasound, BTO 3-X /MoS 2-X efficiently kills Staphylococcus aureus , accompanied by pronounced bacterial envelope destabilization. This response is accompanied by membrane lipid perturbation, increased permeability, respiratory inhibition, and intracellular ROS accumulation. GROMACS simulations show that a model lipid bilayer destabilizes only under a sufficiently strong applied electric field. In infected implant models, ultrasound activated BTO 3-X /MoS 2-X reduces early peri-implant bacterial burden and promotes a repair-favorable inflammatory microenvironment. These findings highlight the potential contribution of BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects to ultrasound responsive antibacterial activity and offer a defect-engineering strategy for implant infection control.

works.title: Pathophysiology-guided design of injectable hydrogels for myocardial infarction repair
works.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a temporally evolving cascade of ischemic injury, inflammation, extracellular matrix degradation, fibrosis, and adverse ventricular remodeling. This temporal heterogeneity places distinct, and sometimes competing, demands on biomaterial intervention at different stages of myocardial repair. This review examines injectable hydrogels according to how their material properties and therapeutic functions address the evolving pathology of MI. This review discusses injectable hydrogels in the context of MI progression. The biological features and treatment priorities of the main post-infarction stages are summarized, followed by recent advances in in situ-forming hydrogels, shear-thinning materials, reversible covalent and supramolecular networks, and systems designed for stimulus-responsive or sequential delivery. The distinctions among multifunctional, stimulus-responsive, and programmable hydrogels are clarified, with particular attention to the timing and sequence of therapeutic action. Challenges associated with catheter delivery, myocardial retention, degradation, biosafety, large-animal validation, manufacturing, and clinical translation are also discussed. A disease-stage-based perspective may guide the development of injectable hydrogels that better match the changing needs of post-infarction myocardial repair.

works.title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π‐Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro‐Crosslinking‐Network for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable fully π‐conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic‐deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft‐micro‐crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p ‐ n FπCPs (P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI) films with a recoverable‐deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three‐dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro‐crosslinked network formed by oxime‐urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro‐crosslinked p ‐ n FπCPs free‐standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm −2 . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro‐crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m −2 , revealed the excellent cycle‐deformation‐stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro‐crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long‐term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

works.title: Polymer‐Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template‐Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single‐Crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer‐directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template‐free synthesis of mesoporous single‐crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3 (MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 ). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn 2+ ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single‐crystalline MnBO 2 OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 . As an anode active material for lithium‐ion batteries, MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , more than twice that of bulk Mn 2 OBO 3 . Notably, this polymer‐directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single‐crystalline materials for energy storage.

works.title: Determining Composition–Structure–Property Relationships in Quaternary Perovskitoids Through Megalibraries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how composition governs structure and function is essential for designing functional materials, however, establishing these relationships remains prohibitively slow for materials with massive and tunable compositional spaces, such as Bi and Sb‐based perovskitoids. Here, a novel megalibrary‐based synthetic methodology has been developed and used to rapidly identify and characterize quaternary perovskite derivatives across an expansive compositional space. Parylene templates were used to synthesize one million compositionally distinct, positionally encoded Cs 3 Sb 2−x Bi x Br 9−y I y microcrystals on 2 × 2 cm 2 chips with 20 µm periodicity. These megalibraries enabled the systematic investigation of structural and optoelectronic evolution across this compositional space using micro‐area x‐ray diffraction, position‐resolved absorbance spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and confocal fluorescence microscopy. An unusual non‐monotonic bandgap shift was observed with increasing Br content, reaching a minimum at 33% Br. This behavior is attributed to the formation of halide‐segregated heterostructures, consisting of low‐dimensional, I‐rich shells surrounding Br‐rich layered cores. Phase separation was most pronounced in Sb‐rich compositions, which were found to stabilize heterostructure formation. This study demonstrates how megalibraries enable the simultaneous evaluation of key optoelectronic parameters, including bandgap and phase purity, revealing complex, composition‐dependent structure‐function relationships in perovskitoids and providing a versatile platform for accelerating the discovery of optoelectronic‐relevant materials.

works.title: An Engineered Thio‐Amino Polymer Achieves Potent, Safe, and Broad Cell Type Delivery in the Lung Mapped by Spatial Transcriptomics
works.abstract: Efficient delivery of nucleic acids to the lung has the potential to impact future respiratory treatments. Current formulations exhibit significant limitations, including insufficient potency, single-cell delivery characterizations, efficacy demonstrations in disease models, and toxicology assessments. Here we describe polymer 81 (P81), which, when used with hypotonic solvents, is 34.1- to 77.8-fold more potent than previous polymers with various cargos for lung transfection by nebulized mRNA. Through the exploration of multiple routes of administration, P81 demonstrated a wide of range of cell-type delivery, including bronchial airway epithelial cells, tracheal basal stem cells, and 54% of all cells in the distal lung, assessed via single-cell spatial transcriptomics. Robust expression of mRNA-encoded antibodies in the lung by P81 enabled quantification of target protein and successful suppression of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The toxicology assessments of multiple doses of P81 polyplexes via nebulization in rodents were unremarkable. Overall, P81 represents a step forward for inhaled nucleic acid delivery to the respiratory tract, positioning itself as an efficient, safe, and translatable delivery formulation.

works.title: Intranasal Pathogenesis‐Adaptive Nanotherapeutics Reinstate Regenerative Competence for Post‐Stroke Neural Repair
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Poststroke neurorehabilitation is limited by the poor regenerative capacity of adult neurons. Although neural stem cells (NSCs) can generate new neurons, their reparative potential is constrained by inefficient delivery to cerebral lesions and a hostile regenerative niche. Here, analysis of a single‐nucleus transcriptomic dataset revealed pronounced dysfunction and intercellular crosstalk among neurons, microglia, and NSCs, highlighting redox imbalance and impaired nitric oxide (NO) signaling as potential therapeutic targets. Guided by these findings, we develop FCeO 2 @GLp, a pathogenesis‐adaptive nanotherapeutic integrating reactive oxygen species scavenging, NO replenishment and immune modulation within cerebral ischemic microenvironment. Following intranasal administration, FCeO 2 @GLp actively adheres to the olfactory epithelium (OE), reaches infarcted brain regions, releases cerium oxide (CeO 2 ) nanozyme, fingolimod, and a NO donor in response to local acidity. This coordinated strategy alleviates oxidative stress, reprograms microglia, protects neurons, and enhances NSC proliferation and neuronal differentiation. Consequently, FCeO 2 @GLp effectively reduces infarct volume and cerebral edema during the acute phase, and improves long‐term neurological function and survival, establishing a lesion‐responsive strategy for poststroke neural repair.

works.title: Scalable Hydrogel‐Programmed Porous Photonic Cement for Passive Daytime Cooling
works.abstract: Cement is among the most widely produced materials on Earth, yet its strong solar absorption causes building envelopes to act as heat sources, increasing cooling energy demand. Here, we structurally program cement hydration to transform conventional cementitious materials into passive cooling interfaces. Through hydrogel-confined mineralization of cement clinker, we construct a robust, hierarchically porous calcium-silicate-hydrate (C-S-H) network that integrates broadband light scattering, vapor transport and thermal insulation. By regulating the composition and crystallinity of the hydrates, the material achieves ∼95% solar reflectance and ∼98% infrared emissivity without the use of additional photonic fillers. The hygroscopic nature of the network further enables sustained evaporative cooling under humid or cloudy conditions where radiative cooling alone becomes inefficient. Life-cycle analysis indicates that this strategy provides a pathway to transform high-emission cement into carbon-mitigating materials integrated within opaque building envelopes, enabling the scalable deployment of daytime radiative cooling across the built environment.

works.title: A Janus Bilayer Portland Cement‐Based Moisture‐Electricity Generator via Hydrogen‐Bonding Network Regulation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The ubiquitous interaction between ambient moisture and built environments presents a compelling opportunity for continuous energy harvesting through moisture‐electricity generation (MEG). However, current MEG materials fail to satisfy high‐power demands in buildings because hydrogen bonds, indispensable for the structural integrity of soft carbon‐chain networks, severely restrict water diffusion, and thus bottleneck MEG performance. Hydrated Portland cement, featuring a robust silicate backbone, allows aggressive modulation of the water hydrogen‐bonding network (HBN), emerging as an ideal platform for higher performance. Here, we developed a Portland cement‐based moisture‐electricity generator (CMEG) via a facile asymmetric acid etching strategy, extending MEG to cementitious material systems. The resulting CMEG presents a Janus bilayer architecture with a stark gradient in hygroscopicity across the layers to drive the unidirectional diffusion of water molecules. Mechanistically, the etching process induces the breakage of HBN, which unlocks ultrafast water diffusion throughout the top layer and thus accelerates selective ion transport toward the bottom layer. Remarkably, CMEG delivers an extremely high short‐circuit current density of 723 µA/cm 2 and output power density of 112.5 µW/cm 2 . Furthermore, CMEG demonstrates exceptional scalability, modular integration capabilities and nearly identical mechanical strength to that before acid etching, proving its giant potential for future self‐powered buildings and infrastructures.

works.title: In Situ Topological Dealloying Enables Atomically Coupled Metal‐Oxide Heterostructures
works.abstract: Metal-oxide heterostructures are central to energy conversion and electronic devices because interfaces can modulate the configuration coupling among charge, spin, and orbit. However, conventional synthesis routes suffer from structural incompatibility and weak coupling, which hinder the universal construction of atomically coupled metal-oxide heterointerfaces. Here, we develop an in situ topological dealloying strategy to construct metal-oxide heterostructures with atomically interconnected interfaces. This strategy can be broadly applied to perovskite, spinel, columbite, and vanadate oxides, which enables the spontaneous formation of high-density magnetic nanoalloys embedded within dielectric oxide matrices. Direct nanoscale visualizations of electric and magnetic fields reveal the coexistence of interfacial charge polarization and vortex-like spin textures. These emergent dielectric and magnetic behaviors arise from atomically interfacial hybridization that mediates strong charge-spin interactions. When integrated into flexible architectures, these heterostructures exhibit broadband GHz-frequency absorption (effective absorption bandwidth up to 6.6 GHz at 3.0 mm), high efficiency, and rapid electromagnetic-to-thermal energy conversion under microwave irradiation. This work establishes a general route to engineer metal-oxide heterostructures for functional applications.

works.title: Bridge‐Level Electronic Compensation in Prussian White Cathodes: Charge‐Transfer Kinetic Regimes and Design Principles
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Prussian White (PW) cathodes are promising sodium–ion battery materials because of their open framework, low cost, and high structural reversibility. However, polarization and capacity loss under high‐rate or low‐temperature operation arise from coupled ionic, structural, interfacial, and electronic processes that are not fully captured by Na + diffusion or average structural evolution alone. This perspective introduces a bridge‐level electronic‐compensation framework in which the Fe─C≡N─TM bridge is treated as a local unit for describing local charge redistribution. Using Marcus‐type descriptors together with concepts of metal‐to‐metal charge transfer, intervalence charge transfer, and metal–ligand interactions, three physical contributions are emphasized: the local charge‐state free‐energy difference ( ΔG° ), cyanide‐mediated electronic coupling ( H ab ), and structure‐coupled reorganization energy ( λ ). Local bridge states are organized into descriptor‐based kinetic regimes based on the balance among energetic mismatch, electronic coupling, and structural reorganization, with transition‐metal chemistries serving as representative mechanistic cases. These descriptors are further translated into design principles involving redox‐level alignment, cyanide‐mediated coupling and network connectivity, and control of local structural reorganization. This perspective provides a physical basis for interpreting bridge‐level electronic compensation and considering how local energetic alignment, coupling, and structural reorganization can be regulated in PW cathodes.

works.title: Staged Network Evolution Enables In Situ Strengthening and On‐Demand Recyclability of Polyurethanes via Dynamic Sulfilimine–Urea Bonds
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Cross‐linked polymers exhibit exceptional mechanical robustness, dimensional stability, and chemical resistance arising from permanent covalent networks. However, it remains challenging to tune mechanical properties after curing and to decouple on‐demand recyclability from in‐use stability. Herein, we report a staged network evolution strategy based on dynamic sulfilimine–urea bonds to address these demands. The rapid room‐temperature addition of isocyanates to sulfilimines forms dynamic sulfilimine–urea linkages, affording a solvent‐resistant initial polyurethane (SUP‐S1). Subsequent thermal treatment of SUP‐S1 induces dissociation of the sulfilimine–urea linkages, regenerating the sulfilimine motifs and releasing isocyanates that are captured in situ by backbone hydroxyl groups to form thermodynamically stable urethane bonds. The tensile strength and toughness of the obtained polyurethane (SUP‐S2) are significantly enhanced, increasing from 17 to 42 MPa and from 55 to 158 MJ m −3 , respectively, while the Young's modulus is retained. Moreover, the photoclip of sulfilimine motifs facilitates on‐demand recyclability by reducing the cross‐link density. The resulting recyclable polyurethane (SUP‐S3) exhibits excellent multi‐recyclability, retaining over 96% of its mechanical properties after five recycling cycles. This staged network evolution design reconciles the enhancement of mechanical properties with end‐of‐life recyclability within a single material platform, providing a robust pathway for the development of next‐generation sustainable cross‐linked polymeric materials.

works.title: Synergistic Dual‐Site Regulation in a Tailored Imine‐COF for Enhanced Hydrogen Peroxide Photosynthesis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) emerge as promising candidates for the photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). However, precise modulation of the chemical environment of active sites in COFs remains a significant challenge. Based on a molecular engineering strategy, this study focuses on hierarchical regulation of nitrogen coordination environments for efficient photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production through the 2e − ORR. Intrinsic nitrogen configurations (triazine vs. pyridine) are first tailored to construct two types of COFs. The pyridyl‐imine TAPT‐BTPA ( 4 ) optimizes charge carrier separation and extends visible‐light absorption, leading to an enhanced H 2 O 2 production rate of 8.12 mmol g −1 h −1 in aqueous solution containing isopropanol as a sacrificial agent under an O 2 atmosphere. Main‐group metals (In, Sn, and Sb) are then anchored at the pyridine‐imine sites to modulate local electron density further and steer reaction pathways. Structural characterization and activity tests reveal that Sb‐coordinated TAPT‐BTPA‐Sb ( 10 ) induces a unique synergistic effect, redirecting the ORR toward a more favorable stepwise 1e − route. This significant pathway regulation ultimately boosts the H 2 O 2 production rate to 15.3 mmol g −1 h −1 under the same conditions. This work clarifies the decisive role of coordination environment engineering and establishes a molecular‐level design paradigm for advanced H 2 O 2 synthesis photocatalysts.

works.title: A Coaxial Bioprinted Hydrogel With Semipermeable Sheath and Pro‐Chondrogenic Core for Articular Cartilage Repair
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Stem cell‐laden hydrogels represent a promising strategy for the functional repair of articular cartilage defects. However, the pathological joint microenvironment is often characterized by persistently elevated levels of pro‐inflammatory cytokines, which severely compromise transplanted cell survival and impair their chondrogenic differentiation potential. Inspired by the hierarchical mechanical gradient of native cartilage, we developed a sheath‐core biomimetic hydrogel (SC GAE ) via embedded coaxial bioprinting, featuring a robust poly(ethylene glycol)‐alginate (PA) sheath that spatially integrates mechanical support and immunoprotection around a soft, bioactive gelatin methacryloyl‐alginate‐decellularized extracellular matrix (GAE) core. The dense PA sheath provides immediate mechanical support and functions as a size‐selective diffusion barrier, permitting nutrient and oxygen permeation while effectively blocking inflammatory cytokines (>40 kDa). This protective niche enables the pericellular matrix‐mimicking GAE core to maintain stem cell viability >89% under pro‐inflammatory conditions and support robust chondrogenic differentiation. In a rabbit osteochondral defect model, bone marrow stromal cell‐laden SC GAE constructs promoted substantial cartilage repair, achieving defect filling, host integration, and regeneration of glycosaminoglycan‐rich hyaline‐like cartilage. This sheath‐core architecture design spatially integrates structural, mechanical, and immunoprotection functions, presenting a promising platform for the regeneration of load‐bearing articular cartilage.

works.title: Deciphering Roles of Interfacial Tunable Primer for High Active Material Contents Pure Silicon Electrodes
works.abstract: While pure silicon (Si) is a highly attractive anode material for next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries, its practical implementation is limited by severe volumetric fluctuations during cycling. This intrinsic instability inevitably induces continuous structural degradation, strictly restricting the maximum allowable active material fraction within the electrode. To address this critical challenge, we design an interfacial tunable functional primer (fp) that serves as an effective multi-component bridging agent. By optimizing the mechanical resilience and electrochemical cohesion among electrode components, the fp layer dissipates interfacial stress and secures continuous electron conduction pathways. Furthermore, the unique ionophoric properties of the benzoxazine framework directly regulate the interfacial solvation structure and enhance ion flux. Driven by these integrated effects, the fp-modified Si anode achieves remarkable electrochemical reversibility even at a nearly binder-free composition containing 99 wt% active material content. This strategy completely averts the rapid physical degradation typically observed in standard binder networks under such extreme formulations. Furthermore, fp-modified Si demonstrates practical viability by assembling double-stacked pouch cells paired with NCM90 cathodes, which exhibit long-term cycle durability. This study provides a highly effective paradigm for electrode-component regulation and molecular-level engineering in pure Si anode interfacial modification strategies.

works.title: Constructing Low‐Friction Ion Transport Pathways in Crosslinked Polymer Electrolyte for Practical Quasi‐Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Quasi‐solid‐state polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with high energy density, but still suffer from sacrificed ionic conductivity caused by electrolyte solidification. Here, by tuning monomer structures with different Li + ‐affinity, we investigate the decisive role of the segmental solvation ability of the polymer matrix in cation transport. Owing to the overly strong affinity for cations, conventional ether segments significantly decrease the Li + relaxation rate, and the resulting “sticky” polymer chains impede Li + migration. In contrast, the weakly coordinating segments such as fluorinated ether could effectively minimize coupling with Li + ions, thereby constructing “low‐friction” cation transport pathways in crosslinked polymer electrolytes, as reflected by the nearly unchanged Li + relaxation kinetics and high ionic conductivity. Therefore, the industrial Li metal pouch cells achieve excellent comprehensive electrochemical performance under harsh lean‐electrolyte conditions, with electrolyte dosage even as low as 1.3 g Ah −1 . The 2 Ah NCM811/Li cell exhibits an extended lifespan beyond 520 cycles and maintains stable operation across a wide temperature range from −50°C to +90°C. The 8.7 Ah NCM955/Li cell delivers 550 Wh kg −1 energy density and demonstrates impressive cycling stability over 260 cycles. This work could inspire fundamental understanding and further development toward practical LMBs.

works.title: FGF2-engineered extracellular vesicles loaded in an ECM-mimetic hydrogel promote wound healing and attenuate scar formation via immunomodulation and enhanced neurovascular responses

Aligned Basement Membrane-Modified Collagen Scaffolds for Skeletal Muscle Tissue Engineering
works.abstract: Biomaterial scaffolds for repairing traumatic muscle injuries require restoration of both the anisotropic architecture and basement membrane extracellular matrix cues critical to normal muscle function. To address this need, we establish a collagen-glycosaminoglycan (CG) scaffold platform pairing an aligned pore microstructure, produced via directional freeze-drying, with basement membrane protein functionalization via carbodiimide cross-linking. Laminin and/or collagen IV are successfully tethered and retained within CG scaffolds over 7 days without significantly altering pore size or alignment, confirming stable protein functionalization and preservation of scaffold architecture. Human muscle progenitor cells show excellent viability and metabolic activity in all scaffold groups, with collagen IV functionalization significantly enhancing myotube number and fusion index. Toward establishing scaffold compatibility with nonmyogenic support cells, we show that neural stem cells remain viable and metabolically active across all scaffold conditions. Overall, these findings highlight the combination of aligned scaffold architecture and collagen IV functionalization as potentially impactful for skeletal muscle tissue engineering.

pH‐Responsive Synthetic Cells for Programmable In Situ Protein Synthesis and Release
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid membrane‐bound synthetic cells provide programmable, cell‐like compartments for on‐demand biomolecule production. However, most cell‐free gene expression systems in synthetic cells are regulated by user‐imposed cues rather than signals associated with environmental or physiological states. Here, we present an acidity‐transducing synthetic cell that converts external pH changes into nucleic acid information to drive in situ protein synthesis. The system integrates gramicidin A proton channels for pH sensing, triplex‐forming single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) that releases a trigger ssDNA upon acidification, and a toehold switch RNA that activates translation in response to the released trigger ssDNA. This work further reveals that tuning the annealing length between the pH‐responsive and trigger ssDNAs controls the trigger‐release pH, which is critical for enabling acid‐triggered protein synthesis. The synthetic cells retain their pH‐responsive activity when embedded in alginate hydrogels, creating acidity‐responsive materials that synthesize proteins in situ rather than release preloaded cargo. Cell‐penetrating peptide tagging further enables selective protein release and target‐specific binding. This work establishes a molecular transduction strategy for programming synthetic cell materials to sense environmentally relevant acidity and generates functional biomolecules on demand.

works.title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10 H ‐Pyrido[1,2‐ a ]‐5‐indolium Salts
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Next‐generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent‐free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation‐caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion–π + interactions. Specifically, a rigid N‐doped fluorene (10 H ‐pyrido[1,2‐ a ]‐5‐indolium, PIn + ) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent‐free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization.
