These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

works.title: High‐Density Pixelated Metasurfaces for Terahertz Hyperspectral Imaging
works.abstract: Metasurface-enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high-throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade-off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction-enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high-quality-factor resonances. By embedding bound-state-in-the-continuum metapixels within a bandgap-engineered heterostructure, we simultaneously suppress lateral leakage and control vertical radiation, enabling effective three-dimensional photon confinement in finite metasurfaces. This mechanism overcomes the conventional dependence of resonance quality on pixel size, yielding enhanced quality factors and figure of merit without increasing the device footprint, and enabling metapixels with lateral dimensions of ∼2λ that retain high spectral fidelity and signal-to-noise ratio. Leveraging this capability, we realize a 3 × 3 pixelated metasurface supporting nine independently addressable resonances, all retrieved in a single-shot broadband terahertz measurement. The resulting spectral-spatial encoding strategy establishes a direct one-to-one mapping between resonance signatures and spatial pixels, enabling hyperspectral imaging with a single-pixel detector and a THz pulse, without raster scanning or algorithmic inversion. These results provide a scalable route toward real-time terahertz imaging and integrated photonic sensing.

works.title: Bismuth‐Mediated Zinc Extraction‐Induced Carbon Defects Boost Fe Single‐Atom Catalysis for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Fe single‐atom catalysts with Fe‐N 4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi‐mediated Fe‐adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe‐N 4 moieties on ZIF‐8‐derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe‐N‐pC d catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half‐wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi‐solid‐state Zn‐air battery using Fe‐N‐pC d as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at −40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe‐N 4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH‐bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect‐modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d‐band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe‐*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential‐limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring‐template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.

works.title: Discovery of Small‐Molecule Cryoprotectants Using Pretrained Language Model Representations
works.abstract: Cryopreservation supports cell therapy, transfusion medicine, and tissue banking, but cryoprotectant selection remains constrained by empirical screening, toxicity, and ice recrystallization. We used pretrained language models as SMILES sequence encoders to prioritize small-molecule cryoprotectants for experimental testing. Hierarchical representations were coupled to descriptor reconstruction, gated fusion, and downstream prediction of normalized mean grain size and thresholded labels. Splat-cooling measurements assessed candidate ice recrystallization inhibition, followed by compatibility and cryopreservation experiments in red blood cells, human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells and rat abdominal aortas. Selected additives improved recovery or preservation endpoints within the tested formulations. This representation-based screening workflow connects molecular property prediction with experimental cryobiology across ice, cellular, and tissue endpoints.

works.title: Upcycling Piezoelectric Single‐Crystal Debris Into High‐Performance Flexible 0–3 Composites
works.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐value piezoelectric single‐crystal debris remains an untapped resource for flexible electromechanical materials. Although relaxor‐based ferroelectric single crystals offer exceptional piezoelectric properties, off‐cuts inevitably generated during precision processing are typically discarded because their irregular geometries prevent direct device integration. Here, we report a recycling‐to‐device upcycling strategy that converts industrial Pb(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3 –PbTiO 3 (PMN–PT) single‐crystal debris into high‐performance flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites and energy harvesters through material–structure–mechanics co‐design. A ball‐milling‐based particle refinement procedure converts the debris into dispersible particulate fillers, while dielectrophoresis (DEP)‐assisted curing reorganizes randomly dispersed particles in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix into vertically connected quasi‐1–3‐like networks. The polymer matrix provides mechanical tunability, allowing flexibility and dynamic stress transfer to the aligned single‐crystal network to be jointly optimized. The optimized composite achieves a d 33 of 118.5 pC N −1 while retaining mechanical flexibility, placing it among the highest‐performing flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites. Comparative experiments and finite‐element simulations reveal that single‐crystal‐derived fillers exhibit stronger DEP‐induced enhancement than polycrystalline counterparts owing to more coherent intraparticle electromechanical conversion. Integrated into flexible energy harvesters, the optimized composite delivers a peak areal power density of 284.2 µW cm − 2 . This work establishes a scalable upcycling pathway for reutilizing high‐value functional crystal waste in flexible self‐powered electromechanical systems.

works.title: Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial‐ and Mesenchymal‐Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC‐Derived Intestinal Organoids
works.abstract: Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill-defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG- and Matrigel-cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation-associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM-remodelling and integrin-associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2-positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

works.title: Ion–Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision
works.abstract: A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single-channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion-electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual-channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic-light-guided closed-loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This "single device enabled, distinguishable dual-channel readouts" principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

works.title: Ultralow Loading Iridium Doped Hollandite Manganese Oxide Nanowires for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are critical for hydrogen production but remain limited by reliance on scarce iridium (Ir). We present an ultralow‐loading Ir catalyst (3 at%, <16 µgIr cm − 2 ) integrated within a hollandite MnO 2 framework, which lowers the overpotential at 10 mA cm − 2 from 580 mV (undoped α‐MnO 2 ) to 303 mV and delivers an Ir mass activity an order of magnitude higher than commercial IrO x . Varying pH and potential, we combine ICP‐MS dissolution measurements with x‐ray absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, and 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy. Dissolution is modest, with at least 79% of the Ir and 76% of the Mn remaining after 6 h under applied potential, and Ir remains oxidized and associated with the hollandite framework. Mn, in contrast, undergoes pH‐ and potential‐dependent reduction and local structural disorder. Notably, the strongest Mn reconstruction (pH 0, 1.65 V) coincides with moderate dissolution, whereas the greatest Ir and Mn loss (pH 0, 1.60 V) occurs where the residual material is less reconstructed. Net dissolution therefore does not report on local structural change, highlighting the need to evaluate dissolution, reconstruction, and oxidation state together when designing and assessing Ir‐efficient mixed‐metal oxide catalysts.

works.title: Sustainable Soft Electronic Devices by High‐Performance Recyclable Elastomers and Conductors
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft electronics have driven emerging advancements, which are expected to have wide‐range and large‐scale applications in health management, electronic skins, soft robotics, and interactive human‐machine interfaces. However, existing strategies mainly focus on isolated components, and system‐level soft electronic devices combining sustainable fabrication, robust performance, and versatile integrated functions have rarely been explored. Herein, we develop a recyclable soft electronic system enabled with multifunctional poly thioctic acid (TA) elastomer and high‐performance elastic metallic conductors. The multifunctional TA elastomer exhibits an exceptional combination of stretchability (435% strain), fracture energy (5.5 kJ/m 2 ), apparent adhesion energy on Cu (10.7 kJ/m 2 ), and thermal conductivity (0.69 W/m·K). These properties enable robust mechanical and electronic interfacing with different electronic components for sustainable soft circuits, while also endowing the electronic systems with outstanding self‐healing and recycling capabilities. Furthermore, by integrating with printable and recyclable elastic conductors based on eutectic liquid metals, the sustainable soft electronic systems can fully restore circuit functionality after complete mechanical rupture with the selfhealing capability of the composite elastomer and the elastic conductor. The system can be reprocessed to achieve full functionality restoration. The materials strategy developed in this study renders a promising solution for the development of soft and sustainable electronic devices.

works.title: A Dual‐Locked and H 2 S‐NO Tandem‐Activatable NIR‐II Nanoagent for Colon Cancer Theranostics
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Dual‐locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual‐locked systems only restricted to enzyme‐responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker‐responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual‐locked and gas tandem‐activatable NIR‐II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water‐dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid‐responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN‐NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible‐NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN‐NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H 2 S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR‐II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN‐NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type‐I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR‐II fluorescence imaging‐guided efficient photo‐elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual‐locked and H 2 S‐NO tandem‐activatable nanoagents with gas‐responsive and NIR‐II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.

works.title: Fluoride‐Mediated Host‐Activator Engineering in Homogeneous Lithium Glass Scintillators for Thermal‐Neutron Detection and Imaging
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous lithium‐aluminosilicate‐glass scintillators offer transparency, scalable fabrication, and compositional flexibility, but their neutron response is limited by defect trapping and activator loading concentration. Here, fluoride‐mediated host‐activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce 3+ ‐activated lithium aluminosilicate glasses. F − preferentially coordinates with Li + and Mg 2+ , preserving the primary Si/Al─O tetrahedral units while reorganizing inter‐tetrahedral linkages. The resulting host‐network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect‐mediated trapping, modulates medium‐range Ce‐centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce‐concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO 2 (twice that of GS20). After 6 Li enrichment, it delivers 8003 photons neutron −1 , an energy resolution of 6.8%, a decay time of 85.06 ns, and a neutron peak‐to‐trough ratio of 77:1. To the best of our knowledge, these values represent the highest light yield and best energy resolution reported for a homogeneous transparent 6 Li‐enriched glass scintillator, achieving single‐digit neutron energy resolution for the first time and approaching the performance of 3 He proportional counters and high‐performance crystalline scintillators. A transparent plate exceeding 2 inches further enables proof‐of‐concept two‐dimensional thermal‐neutron imaging with a system‐level spatial resolution of 1.35 mm, demonstrating the scalability of the glass for position‐sensitive neutron imaging.

works.title: Dynamic, Wet‐Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair
works.abstract: Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self-repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial-based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet-adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid-covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff-base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine-containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self-healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane-derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host-graft integration, and cartilage-like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet-adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial-cartilage interface healing in fluid-rich joint environments.

works.title: Rate Capability of Lithium‐Rich Manganese‐Based Oxide Cathodes: Charge–Discharge Kinetics, Multiscale Bottlenecks, and Dynamic Rate‐Determining Steps
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials deliver a reversible specific capacity exceeding 250 mAh g −1 through synergistic anionic and cationic redox, promising for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries, yet their poor rate capability remains a critical barrier to practical deployment, particularly for fast‐charging applications. This review deconstructs rate‐limiting mechanisms at three levels, namely direct charge‐transport impediments, kinetic sluggishness of anionic redox, and degradation cascade of phase transformations, voltage decay, and microcracking that exacerbates kinetics. A central insight is that the rate‐determining step (RDS) shifts from electron‐transfer to ion‐diffusion dominance, governed by the exchange current density ( j 0 ) and the limiting current density ( j d ). Modification strategies are classified into two threads, kinetic enhancement by shortening diffusion paths and lowering migration barriers, and structural stabilization by reinforcing bonds and suppressing oxygen release. Importantly, the often‐overlooked charging kinetics are critically assessed, as the asymmetric nature of anionic redox imposes a more severe bottleneck for fast charging than for high‐rate discharging. Methodological limitations in cross‐study C‐rate comparisons, arising from variations in electrode loading and testing protocols, are also examined to enable more rigorous evaluation of reported performance. This review ultimately provides a theoretical foundation for rational design of high‐rate LRMO cathodes toward practical energy storage applications.

works.title: Designing a Thermochemically Active Hydrogel With In Situ‐Formed Ceramic–Carbon Hybrid Barrier for Suppressing Thermal Runaway Propagation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water‐rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm‐shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross‐linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual‐mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm − 3 ) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame‐inhibiting SO 2 release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic–carbon hybrid barrier. Post‐test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO 4 ) maximizes covalent B─O─C bonds that chemically “weld” B 2 O 3 to carbon. This trend in BO 4 fraction with BA loading quantitatively explains the exceptional TRP suppression, reducing the adjacent cell's peak temperature by over 500°C. Beyond a high‐performance material, this work establishes a general design principle: employing reactive fillers that orchestrate both multi‐stage energy management and tailored barrier synthesis, paving the way for next‐generation battery safety materials.

works.title: Sensitive, Broadband, and Stable Short‐Wave Infrared Photodetection and Imaging in Mixed‐Dimensional Organic/Inorganic Heterostructures
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors confront cost disadvantages and fabrication complexity, whereas two‐dimensional (2D) van der Waals devices exhibit inherent performance limitations. Mixed‐dimensional organic/inorganic heterostructures offer a promising strategy for SWIR photodetection, synergizing strong optical absorption and tunability of organic semiconductors with high charge mobility and stability of inorganics. However, critical challenges remain in architecture design, including optimal carrier‐collection geometry, material selection, and interface engineering for boosting devices’ performance. Herein, a type‐II band‐aligned PTF/WSe 2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure is reported for high‐performance broadband SWIR photodetection via heterostructure synergy and rational Schottky barrier engineering. The Cr/ p ‐WSe 2 /PTF configuration (∼ 0.28 eV barrier) achieves superior performance, while Cr/ n ‐WSe 2 /PTF suffers from a higher barrier (∼ 1.18 eV). The optimized device achieves broad spectral photoresponsivity (∼ 10 3 A/W, 1060–1470 nm) and exceptional performance at 1310 nm: ultrahigh photoresponsivity ( R = 2894 A/W), robust specific detectivity ( D * = 1.0×10 12 Jones), and excellent long‐term ambient stability. Versus standalone PTF, it delivers 17‐fold higher photoresponsivity and 96% lower bias voltage. High‐resolution SWIR image‐pattern reconstruction, together with concurrent performance improvements after six months of controlled storage, validates this PTF/WSe 2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure's potential for advancing next‐generation high‐performance SWIR detectors.

works.title: Preserving Polymorphic Crystalline Structures in Bulk Heterojunctions for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The crystal structure of a material profoundly influences its physical, optical, and electronic properties. However, precise control over polymorph formation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) in bulk heterojunction active layers remains challenging for optimizing organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Here, we employ a non‐halogenated mixed‐solvent system comprising carbon disulfide (CS 2 ) and o‐xylene (OXY) to selectively regulate the crystallization of the high‐performance acceptor BTP‐eC9. A specific polymorph (Form II) is preferentially induced and consistently identified in powder, neat‐film, and bulk heterojunction samples by correlating wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (WAXS) and grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) patterns with simulations derived from the corresponding single‐crystal structures. Compared with Form I, Form II exhibits improved optoelectronic properties, including extended exciton diffusion length, balanced charge mobility, and suppressed non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, Form II‐based devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.61% with a fill factor of 82.85%, representing a 27.0% relative improvement over Form I devices (PCE = 16.23%). Moreover, this method enables scalable manufacturing, with flexible OSCs (1 cm 2 active area) fabricated by slot‐die coating achieving a PCE of 17.93%. This work establishes a practical pathway for solution‐processed polymorph control and reveals the relationship among single‐crystal packing, acceptor molecular packing, and device performance.

works.title: Pd Single‐Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self‐Decoupled Temperature‐Humidity Dual‐Mode Sensors
works.abstract: The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high-fidelity multi-modal temperature-humidity sensing without inter-channel cross-talk and computational post-processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron-ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self-decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single-atom anchoring and heterogeneous-nucleation-driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus-response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra-fast quasi-2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy-driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross-talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low-temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi-modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed-loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on-demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next-generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.

works.title: Correction to “Colorful Electrochromic Displays With High Visual Quality Based on Porous Metamaterials”
Skunk Cabbage‐Inspired AIEgen Photoactuators With Multiwavelength Response, Ultrafast Actuation, and Multicolor Fluorescence
works.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR)-responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade-offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra-fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR-responsive actuators by integrating aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus-structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra-low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi-donor-π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor-acceptor interactions and molecular motion-facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding. Programmable motions are implemented under different wavelengths through sequential, penetrative, and heat-transfer actuation. This work provides guidelines for smart materials requiring precise 980 nm actuation with maintained mechanical robustness.

works.title: Chiral Materials for the Recognition and Inhibition of Amyloid‐β Aggregation
works.abstract: Abnormal aggregation of amyloid-β (Aβ) peptides is a central pathological event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), closely associated with neurotoxicity and disease progression. The development of molecules or materials with high selectivity and affinity toward Aβ aggregates constitutes an essential component for the early diagnosis and intervention of AD. Aβ peptides, composed of homochiral amino acids, undergo intermolecular β-sheet assembly to form supramolecular chiral aggregates, providing a structural basis for chirality-sensitive recognition. Therefore, chiral materials have attracted significant attention in Aβ aggregates recognition and regulation. Previous reviews have examined different types of chiral materials for the inhibition of Aβ aggregation, including chiral small molecules, amino acids, peptides, and various chiral interfaces or nanomaterials. The present review organizes reported chiral materials according to three intervention strategies for modulating Aβ aggregation: conformation-locking, self-assembly-induced remodeling, and multifunctional intervention. We summarize representative materials in each category, along with the corresponding design principles and modulation performance toward Aβ aggregation. Current challenges and potential directions for the development of chiral therapeutics for AD are also discussed.

works.title: An Iron Disulfide‐Decorated Polymeric Carbon Nitride Integrated Photocatalytic Irrigation System Promotes Cartilage Repair via Transient H 2 O 2 ‐Mediated Immune Regulation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Acute inflammation and necrosis in the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) hinder cartilage repair by disrupting immune–chondrocyte crosstalk and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. Photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) offers a promising approach for reconstituting the local microenvironment by debriding and healing damaged tissue. However, achieving high catalytic activity and selectivity for efficient and controllable ROS regulation remains challenging. Herein, we developed an iron disulfide (FeS 2 )‐decorated polymeric carbon nitride (PCN‐FeS 2 ) composite as an efficient visible‐light–driven photocatalyst for controlled H 2 O 2 generation. The optimized PCN‐FeS 2 exhibited an H 2 O 2 production rate of 1657 µmol·L − 1 ·h − 1 , representing an 8.3‐fold enhancement over pristine PCN, owing to improved charge separation and efficient conversion of toxic superoxide radical (·O 2 − ) intermediates. This catalytic system was designed for transient intra‐articular lavage under acute inflammatory stress, providing controlled, light‐triggered H 2 O 2 generation to promote a reparative microenvironment while minimizing material retention. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a rat model of lipopolysaccharide‐induced acute TMJ arthritis, in which PCN‐FeS 2 was administered through transient low‐pressure intermittent intra‐articular irrigation. Moreover, the oxidation signal contributed to the differentiation of IL10 + regulatory B cells (Bregs) to facilitate chondrocyte recovery. Overall, this study provides a translationally feasible strategy that integrates catalytic chemistry with endogenous immunocommunication for acute TMJ pathology.

works.title: Pagoda‐Inspired Microneedles for Multiphase Coverage Wound Healing
works.abstract: Microneedle patches are considered as an attractive technology for wound treatment. Current researches are devoted to enhancing the structure and functionality of microneedles to cover multiphase for wound healing. Here, we present a desired quaternized chitosan-coated pagoda-inspired microneedle (QPDMN) patch loaded with diverse drugs to treat wounds. The QPDMN tips are comprised of a bottom layer loading vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and a top layer containing antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), as well as with the outer surface coated with quaternized chitosan (QCS). When applied, QCS could firstly contact wounds and rapidly promote blood clotting. Subsequently, AMPs released from top needles could remarkably inhibit bacterium growth, while VEGF released from bottom tips effectively facilitate tissue regeneration. Animal experiments have further proved that the QPDMN system has rapid hemostasis, enhanced angiogenesis, anti-inflammation and collagen deposition performances, coordinating the different phases of wound healing. Thus, we believe that the pagoda-like microneedles could be an excellent multiphase-coverage therapeutic agent in clinic wound healing.

works.title: Synergistic Sulfur‐Atom Positioning and Acceptor Engineering Enable Preferential Type‐I Photodynamic Therapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Less oxygen‐independent Type‐I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by photosensitizers offer distinct advantages for tumor photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, most conventional photosensitizers activate nonselective mixed ROS pathways, significantly hindering the advancement of PDT. In this study, we propose a synergistic molecular design strategy that integrates sulfur‐atom positioning and acceptor engineering to achieve preferential Type‐I ROS generation. We identified a novel near‐infrared Type‐I photosensitizer NS4 . Combined theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations demonstrate that sulfur substitution enhances the S 1 ‐T 1 intersystem crossing, while acceptor engineering promotes a pronounced twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT). This TICT effect lowers the energy of the S 1 state and stabilizes the T 1 state, thereby synergistically enabling the preferential production of Type‐I ROS. Both free NS4 derivative and NS‐NPs , self‐assembled from NS4 and F‐127, can generate substantial amounts of Type‐I ROS under 660 nm laser irradiation, effectively triggering tumor cell apoptosis. In vivo assessments confirm that a single dose of NS‐NPs significantly suppresses tumor growth with negligible systemic toxicity. This work establishes theoretical and structural guidelines for the rational design of high‐performance Type‐I photosensitizers and facilitates the further translation of PDT.

works.title: A Two‐Stage Strategy to Reprogram Cyanine Photosensitizers as Controllable‐Pyroptosis Inducers for Anticancer Phototherapy
works.abstract: Pyroptosis, a lytic and inflammatory form of programmed cell death, provides a promising strategy for antitumor immunotherapy. However, controllable modulation of pyroptosis using phototherapeutic agents remains challenging. In this study, we report a two-stage molecular reprogramming method to rationally design cyanine photosensitizers with tunable pyroptosis-inducing activity. We first reprogram IR808 into a novel photosensitizer T808, by integrating a tetraphenylethylene unit with IR808, which consequently enhances excited - state features related to intersystem crossing (ISC) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation capability, accompanied by inducing pyroptosis under irradiation. In the second process, T808 is conjugated with poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) chains of varying lengths (M.W. 550, 1000, and 2000 Da) to finely modulate the pyroptotic efficacy. The relationship of PEG chain length with pyroptosis-inducing activity is in the order of PT550 > T808 > PT1000 >> PT2000. Cellular and in vivo studies show that T808, PT550, and PT1000 treatments suppress tumor growth and induce pyroptosis with occurrence of immunogenic cell death (ICD). Even under a lower intratumoral injection dose (25 µM), T808 and PT550 therapies exhibit remarkable antitumor efficacy with measurable pyroptosis features. This work provides a new insight into reprogramming cyanine photosensitizers into pyroptosis-active molecules, and proposes possible structural association of PEGylated cyanines with the pyroptosis activity.

works.title: Artemisinin‐Loaded Core‐Shell Microspheres Modulate Histone Lactylation to Remodel the Microenvironment for Cartilage Protection in Rheumatoid Arthritis
works.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves persistent inflammation and metabolic dysregulation that jointly drive cartilage damage. Although lactate accumulates in arthritic joints, the role of lactate-induced histone lactylation in cartilage progenitor cell (CPC) dysfunction remains unclear. Here, we developed an injectable, tissue-adhesive core-shell microsphere (ART@PLGA@GH-A) for sustained intra-articular delivery of artemisinin (ART). CUT&Tag sequencing identified a pathological lactate-H4K16la-Ccnb2 axis in RA-derived CPCs, in which lactate accumulation enhanced H4K16la enrichment at the Ccnb2 promoter, promoting mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and extracellular matrix degradation. ART@PLGA@GH-A suppressed H4K16la deposition at the Ccnb2 locus and more effectively inhibited CPC senescence and glycolytic lactate production than ART-loaded hydrogel microspheres (ART@GH). Mechanistically, ART@PLGA@GH-A promoted macrophage polarization from pro-inflammatory M1 toward anti-inflammatory M2, reduced intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, restored mitochondrial membrane potential and dynamics, enhanced chondrogenic markers (COL II, Aggrecan, and SOX9), and reduced matrix-degrading enzymes (MMP13 and ADAMTS5). In collagen-induced arthritis rats, a single intra-articular injection of ART@PLGA@GH-A reduced subchondral bone erosion and proteoglycan loss and improved hindlimb gait function, outperforming free ART and non-adhesive microspheres. Therefore, ART@PLGA@GH-A targets the lactate-dependent H4K16la-Ccnb2 axis and restores joint homeostasis, thereby achieving synergistic anti-inflammatory, anti-senescent, and chondroprotective effects and providing a clinically translatable local therapeutic strategy for RA.

works.title: Quantum Saturation of the Electro‐Optic Effect
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Future quantum computing architectures require electro‐optic materials that maintain a strong, stable performance at cryogenic temperatures. In conventional electro‐optic materials, large electro‐optic coefficients are often confined to narrow temperature windows near structural phase transitions, where small changes in temperature lead to large changes in the electro‐optic response. Using thermodynamic analysis, phase‐field simulations, experimental growth, and cryogenic optical measurements, we show that quantum fluctuations can be harnessed to overcome this trade‐off. By tuning the ferroelectric phase boundaries down to 0 K, quantum fluctuations induce a saturation regime in which a large electro‐optic response becomes nearly temperature‐independent below 25 K. We demonstrate that the phase boundaries can be tuned through either strain in BaTiO 3 or through chemical composition in Ba 1‐ x Ca x TiO 3 , leading to a large, temperature‐insensitive, cryogenic electro‐optic response, r eff = 2850 pm V −1 (experiment) and r 51 = 2900 pm V −1 (theory) for BaTiO 3 on GdScO 3 and r 51 = 1898 pm V −1 (theory) for Ba 0.77 Ca 0.23 TiO 3 . These values exceed the room temperature performance of bulk BaTiO 3 r 51 = 1600 pm V −1 and surpass the cryogenic performance of BaTiO 3 ‐on‐Si, r eff = 200 pm V −1 , by over an order of magnitude. These findings establish a general design principle for engineering high‐performance electro‐optic materials for cryogenic applications.

works.title: First use of a woven allogeneic vascular graft made of cell-assembled extracellular matrix (CAM) as an arteriovenous shunt in sheep: a pilot study
An All‐Natural Multifunctional Hydrogel Incorporating Carrier‐Free Self‐Assembled Microparticles for the Treatment of S. aureus ‐Infected Wounds
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional wound dressings combining antibacterial activity and tissue regeneration are highly desirable for infected wound management. In this study, a multifunctional chitosan‐gelatin hydrogel incorporating carrier‐free self‐assembled anisaldehyde‐tannic acid‐Zn 2 + (AA‐TA‐Zn 2 + ) bioactive microparticles is developed. These microparticles are fabricated through non‐covalent self‐assembly and metal‐phenolic coordination without additional polymeric carriers or surfactants. Anisaldehyde (AA) serves as both an antibacterial agent and a hydrophobic structural building block, while tannic acid (TA) and Zn 2 + provide complementary antioxidant and coordination functions. Incorporation of these microparticles into the chitosan‐gelatin matrix enhances the structural integrity and multifunctionality of the resulting composite hydrogel through dynamic intermolecular interactions. The hydrogel exhibits excellent injectability, self‐healing capability, tissue adhesion, and sustained release with pH‐responsive behavior. In vitro experiments demonstrate the antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti‐inflammatory activities of the microparticles and composite hydrogel, including their ability to alleviate oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, as well as the hydrogel's effectiveness in disrupting established Staphylococcus aureus biofilms. In a murine model of S. aureus ‐infected wounds, the hydrogel significantly accelerates wound closure and enhances collagen deposition and tissue restoration. This study presents a promising strategy for integrating carrier‐free bioactive microparticles into a natural biopolymer hydrogel matrix, offering a multifunctional platform for infected wound management.

works.title: Shelf‐Stable Human‐Derived Granular Extracellular Matrix (gECM) Hydrogel Wafers as 2.5D Substrates for Microphysiological Modeling
works.abstract: Understanding disease pathology and evaluating emerging therapeutics require in vitro models that accurately recapitulate human tissue environments. However, existing microphysiological systems often compromise either biomimicry or ease-of-use, limiting widespread adoption and scalability. Here, we present lyophilized granular extracellular matrix (gECM) hydrogel wafers as shelf-stable, humanized 2.5D substrates that enable physiologically relevant modeling while simplifying integration into experimental workflows. Derived from decellularized human cartilage and bone, our gECM hydrogel wafers retain tissue-specific architecture while introducing microporosity and surface topography through lyophilization. These wafers maintain swelling behavior, structural integrity, and mechanical properties over three months of room-temperature storage, allowing pre-fabrication and on-demand use without loss of function. gECM hydrogel wafers support direct cell seeding without encapsulation and sustain viability and proliferation of human adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells over 21 days. Furthermore, wafers can be readily integrated into proof-of-concept on-chip fabrication with in situ hydration and transport of large biomolecules. Together, this platform bridges the gap between conventional 2D culture ease-of-use and 3D biomaterial biomimicry, providing a scalable, physiologically-relevant, and humanized in vitro model approach that shows potential for future high-throughput disease studies and therapeutic screening.

works.title: Exploring the Organization of Uncalcified Vertebral Shark Cartilage
works.abstract: Elasmobranch vertebral cartilage is a sophisticated hierarchical composite, integrating a collagenous organic framework with bioapatite mineral, proteoglycans, and a complex suite of non-collagenous proteins. While the mineralized skeletal tissues have been characterized, the structural motifs and biomechanical contributions of the unmineralized regions remain poorly understood. This study investigates the micro- and nanoscale architecture of unmineralized nurse shark (Ginglymostoma cirratum) cartilage to infer the structure-property relationships governing its biological function. By combining synchrotron nearfield X-ray holotomography (nanoCT), synchrotron X-ray fluorescence (XRF) microscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and polarized light microscopy (PLM), we develop an in-depth understanding of the soft-hard tissue interfaces and 3D collagenous organization. The unmineralized phase consists of a dense extracellular matrix (ECM), distinct collagen structures, and graded organic-inorganic interfaces. NanoCT imaging revealed a complex network of cartilage channels and plate-like collagenous lamellae. Quantitative analysis by AI-assisted machine learning segmentation identified differences in fiber directionality, exhibiting both collinear and perpendicular orientations relative to the mineralized front. PLM intensity profiles corroborated optical anisotropy across extended regions. Ultrastructural analysis via TEM confirmed highly oriented type-II collagen fibers with distinct d-banding periodicity, supporting the structural motifs observed in 3D nanoCT volumes. Elemental XRF mappings identified a heterogeneous distribution of mineral species within the ECM and collagenous domains, highlighting localized intensity gradients that define the transition between phases. This structural hierarchy, characterized by tailored stiffness gradients and lamellar reinforcement, suggests an evolutionary optimization for mechanical load distribution, serving as a blueprint for the design of advanced, bio-inspired composites and biomimetic joint replacement materials.

works.title: Mechanobiology-instructed biomaterials for osteoarthritis: Bridging mechanotransduction and disease modification
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a whole-joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and subchondral bone remodeling. Disrupted mechanical homeostasis contributes to these interconnected changes by altering load distribution, tissue deformation, and cellular responses to mechanical stimuli. Inflammation, aging, and matrix remodeling further modify cellular mechanosensitivity, allowing similar mechanical inputs to produce distinct biological outcomes. Conventional biomaterials have largely emphasized defect filling, structural support, and matching the mechanical properties of native cartilage. However, reproducing tissue stiffness does not necessarily restore the dynamic mechanical microenvironment experienced by cells, underscoring the need to regulate pathological mechanical information rather than static material properties alone. This review examines the multiscale mechanical pathology of OA and the mechanosensing and mechanotransduction processes that connect local physical cues with disease progression. It synthesizes biomaterial design strategies involving spatially regulated mechanics, viscoelastic adaptation, mechanical energy conversion, external physical actuation, and mechanically coupled therapeutic delivery. These approaches are discussed in relation to chondrocyte homeostasis, stem cell fate, synovial immune responses, osteochondral remodeling, and aging-associated dysfunction. A phenotype-guided framework is proposed to align material functions with priority mechanical abnormalities across different disease stages and patient-specific pathological contexts, while recognizing that multiple pathological features often coexist and evolve within individual joints. We further identifies requirements for disease-modifying evaluation, including causal mechanistic evidence, physiologically relevant dynamic testing, whole-joint functional outcomes, and durability after material degradation or treatment withdrawal. Together, these perspectives connect mechanobiological principles with rational material design and outline a path toward sustained OA intervention.

works.title: Percolation-tunable conductive MXene–hydrogel multi-channel conduits promote integrin-mediated peripheral nerve regeneration
works.abstract: A B S T R A C T Peripheral nerve repair is severely hindered by the lack of biomimetic conductive scaffolds that recapitulate native conductive microenvironments to coordinate neuronal differentiation and myelination. Here, we fabricate a multi-channel polyacrylamide/chitosan/MXene hydrogel nerve conduit with concentration-programmable percolative conductivity. A critical percolation threshold at 600 μg/mL establishes an optimal conductive microenvironment, which significantly enhances Schwann cell viability, neurite outgrowth, and neurotrophic factor secretion. Mechanistically, the MXene-mediated conductive cue upregulates myelination- and neuronal differentiation-related genes via activating integrin-dependent PI3K-Akt mechanotransduction and axon guidance signaling pathways. In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, the optimized conduit significantly promotes axonal regeneration and remyelination, with 12-week functional and electrophysiological recovery indicators showing no significant statistical difference from those of autologous nerve grafts. This work demonstrates that percolation-tunable conductive engineering is a reliable strategy to construct biomimetic neural microenvironments, providing a feasible translational scaffold for advanced peripheral nerve regeneration.

works.title: A composite lymph node-targeting nanoadjuvant NA@DCM integrates TLR9 and mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming for enhanced hepatitis B vaccination
works.abstract: : Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global public health concern. Although hepatitis B subunit vaccines are safe and effective, improved adjuvants may further enhance their immunogenicity. We developed NA@DCM, an aluminum-based composite nanoadjuvant in which DSPE-PEG 2000 nanomicelles incorporating a covalently conjugated DSPE-PEG–CpG 1018 (DC) conjugate are interfacially assembled with nano-aluminum (NA). We evaluated draining lymph node (dLN) biodistribution, immunogenicity, and biosafety in murine models, and examined B-cell activation mechanisms by transcriptomic, Western blot, and pharmacological inhibition analyses. NA@DCM enhanced CpG-associated accumulation in dLNs at 6 h versus free CpG, with sustained retention and component colocalization over 48 h. Compared with its individual components and their physical mixture, NA@DCM increased antigen-specific IgG titers, the IgG2c/IgG1 ratio, IFN-γ + /TNF-α + / IL-2 + /IL-4 + CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, and germinal center responses, and matched an AS04-like reference formulation in total IgG. These features are consistent with a Th1-biased antibody profile. Mechanistically, NA@DCM enhanced Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9)–NF-κB signaling and mitochondrial function, with increased superoxide-associated fluorescence, ATP production, and respiratory chain complex activities . Oligomycin A inhibition of ATP synthase attenuated bioenergetic responses and CD69/CD86 upregulation in human Namalwa and primary murine B cells, indicating mitochondrial ATP synthesis is required for NA@DCM-induced B-cell activation. NA@DCM showed favorable hemocompatibility in vitro and no overt acute toxicity in vivo ; repeated immunization induced early cytokine responses and local infiltration without detectable hepatic or renal abnormalities. Collectively, NA@DCM integrates lymph node-targeted delivery, TLR9-associated signaling, and mitochondrial bioenergetic modulation, supporting further preclinical development as a hepatitis B vaccine adjuvant.

works.title: Formulation‐Driven Design of Antimicrobial Hydrogel Wound Patches 3D‐Printed by Digital Light Processing: Mapping Polysaccharide and Nanoparticle Effects
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Wound dressings must balance antimicrobial efficacy with the printability limits imposed by nanoparticle‐mediated ultraviolet attenuation during digital light processing 3D printing. Here, we develop process–structure–property relationships for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA)‐based hydrogel wound patches containing Ag/ZnO‐derived antimicrobial phases and polysaccharide/cellulose modifiers (cellulose nanofibrils, chitosan, or alginate). Beer–Lambert analysis shows that nanoparticle loading reduces optical penetration depth at 405 nm to 1.04‐1.28 mm, narrowing the usable curing margin so that radiant exposure exceeds the critical energy by only 4%–5%. Flory–Rehner analysis of swelling reveals formulation‐dependent crosslink density: alginate lowers effective crosslink density by 45% vs. neat PEGDA and increases mesh size from 0.42 to 0.60 nm. This network loosening drives 1.5× variation in water vapor transmission rate (WVTR; 346–518 g·m − 2 ·day − 1 ) and a 7× range in wettability (11.5°–81.1°). Two‐way factorial analysis identifies polysaccharide type as the dominant driver of swelling (87.5% of variance) and antimicrobial efficacy (>50%), while nanoparticle type controls contact angle (60.1%) and WVTR (76.9%). The Ag + chitosan formulation (S5) achieves 23–24 mm inhibition zones against Escherichia coli and Bacillus sp. via chitosan‐facilitated Ag + diffusion plus intrinsic contact‐killing. Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy confirms cumulative Ag + release (32.7 mg·L − 1 over 14 days), while Zn 2 + remains immobilized below detection.

works.title: Redefining Post-detoxification with Novel Surface Coatings: Proteomic Insights into the Early Host Response
works.abstract: Conventional peri-implantitis treatments often rely on detoxification protocols to reduce surface-associated biofilms. However, biofilm removal alone may be insufficient, as successful outcomes ultimately depend on subsequent cellular and molecular responses that support tissue healing. Cellular interactions after detoxification are influenced by proteins at the implant-tissue interface, and strategies to engineer a proregenerative protein profile following detoxification remain unexplored. This study investigated the potential of antimicrobial and lubricative dicatonic imidazolium-based ionic liquid (IL) coating to modulate protein adsorption following clinically relevant detoxification protocols. The interfacial proteome on titanium (Ti) surfaces was evaluated at 24 h using a subcutaneous rat model after exposure to a mixed-species oral biofilm, detoxification, and subsequent IL application. Experimental groups included implants detoxified with citric acid (CA 40%), chlorhexidine (CHX 1%), or saline (SA 0.9%), as well as combination groups with IL (CAIL, CHXIL, and SAIL). Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analysis recovered 318,659 peptides representing 5084 proteins. Detoxification monotherapies (CA, CHX, and SA) were associated with distinct interfacial proteomic profiles, including patterns with pro-inflammatory signaling. To directly evaluate the effect of IL after each detoxification treatment, we compared CAIL vs CA, CHXIL vs CHX, and SAIL vs SA. The strongest direct protein-level IL-associated effect was observed following CA treatment, whereas no proteins met the pre-specified significance criteria of |log2FC| > 0.58 and false-discovery rate < 0.05 for CHXIL vs CHX or SAIL vs SA. Pathway analysis showed a treatment-dependent pattern consistent with NRF2-mediated cytoprotective signaling, Th2-associated immune modulation, tissue repair, cell adhesion, and inflammatory responses; we interpreted these pathway findings as predicted molecular associations rather than direct evidence of pathway activation or suppression. Altogether, these results suggest that post-detoxification IL application may further modify the early interfacial proteomic response in a treatment-dependent manner, supporting further investigation of IL coating as a strategy to improve biomaterial-host interactions following implant-surface detoxification.

works.title: Engineering copper homeostasis for microenvironment-adaptive therapy in inflammation-driven disorders
works.abstract: Inflammation-driven disorders (IDDs) arise from distinct initiating events, yet many persist because immune activation, oxidative and metabolic stress, regulated cell death, and tissue remodeling form self-reinforcing local niches. Copper connects these processes through its roles as a cuproenzyme cofactor, redox-active species and dynamically trafficked regulatory metal. Its therapeutic significance, however, is determined by disease stage, cell type, subcellular distribution and chemical state. Copper deficiency, excess or mislocalization may therefore be adaptive, protective or pathogenic in different contexts. This review develops a disease- and copper-state-specific framework that links copper homeostasis to therapeutic platform design. We first examine inflammation-associated remodeling of copper trafficking and compare representative copper states in autoimmune joint disease, metabolic inflammation, fibrosis, inflammation-associated cancer and infection-associated tissue repair. We then critically evaluate copper-dependent and copper-sensitive mechanisms governing inflammatory mediator availability, immune-cell programming and checkpoint regulation, regulated cell death, angiogenesis and stromal remodeling, while distinguishing direct mechanistic evidence from model-dependent inference. Building on this analysis, we compare pharmacological modulators with nanocarriers, copper-containing active materials and local copper-sequestering platforms that implement copper chelation or sequestration, controlled copper delivery or release, intracellular redistribution, and catalytic activation or nanozyme-like redox regulation. We further outline how pathological copper pools, activation cues, release kinetics, speciation, biodistribution and target engagement should be measured so that precision is demonstrated rather than inferred from material composition. This framework positions copper modulation as a context-specific complement to existing therapy and defines the mechanistic, analytical and translational evidence required for microenvironment-adaptive treatment of IDDs.

works.title: Staged photothermal hydrogel containing manganese-doped bioactive glass nanoparticles promotes infected bone regeneration by engaging Schwann cell PI3K/AKT signaling and neuro-osteogenic coupling
works.abstract: Infected bone lesions are characterized by concurrent bacterial infection, persistent inflammatory infiltration, peripheral nerve damage, and impaired osteogenesis. However, most biomaterials address only antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, or osteogenic functions while overlooking nerve-bone crosstalk during tissue repair. Here, we engineered QOMB, an injectable photothermal hydrogel responsive to near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, by embedding manganese-doped bioactive glass nanoparticles (Mn-BGN) within a dynamically crosslinked network of gallic acid-grafted quaternized chitosan (QCSG) and oxidized sodium alginate (OSA). QOMB exerts synergistic photothermal antibacterial effects and promotes anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage polarization within inflammatory microenvironments. More importantly, ions released from Mn-BGN stimulate Schwann cells (SCs) to secrete abundant neurotrophic factors, thereby establishing a pro-regenerative paracrine niche that promotes osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation demonstrated that stimulation with Mn-BGN-derived ionic cues activates PI3K/AKT signaling and enhances neurotrophic factor secretion by SCs. In a rat model of infected femoral condylar defects, QOMB administration combined with sequential NIR irradiation markedly suppressed local bacterial colonization, attenuated chronic inflammation, enhanced neurotrophic signaling, and accelerated de novo bone formation. These results support a material-Schwann cell-bone regulatory pathway that coordinates staged infection control and immune reprogramming with neuro-osteogenic repair.

works.title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing
works.abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define ‘benchmark-ready’ organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

works.title: Retinal neuroprotection and microglia M1/M2 polarization modulation of triamcinolone acetonide and basic fibroblast growth factor co-delivered in liposomes after optic nerve injury
works.abstract: Optic nerve diseases can result in the degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons, ultimately causing irreversible blindness. Current conventional treatments are limited by inconsistent efficacy, adverse effects or poor tolerability, underscoring the urgent need for more effective therapeutic approaches. Triamcinolone acetonide (TA) and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) have been identified as neuroprotective agents; however, investigations into their combined effects remain scarce. The present study describes a PEG-modified liposome co-encapsulating TA and bFGF, administered via intravitreal injection in a murine model of optic nerve crush (ONC). This co-delivery system demonstrates superior effects in protecting RGCs, promoting axonal regeneration, and modulating microglia M1/M2 shift compared to the monotherapies. RNA sequencing analysis and molecular experiments revealed that TA/bFGF@Lipo was involved in the NF-κB/p65 signaling pathway and PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Notably, the expression of tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases-1 (TIMP1) was significantly upregulated following the liposomes treatment and exhibited a strong correlation with the expression of microglia M2 biomarkers. Subsequent experiments demonstrated that rmTIMP1 promoted BV2 microglia M1/M2 shift in a dose-dependent manner, and TIMP1 knockdown significantly decreased the RGCs survival and M2 polarization of retinal microglia induced by TA/bFGF@Lipo. Collectively, this research establishes TA/bFGF@Lipo as an effective therapeutic strategy for optic nerve injury, and highlights the essential role of TIMP1 in RGCs protection and microglia M2 polarization, offering novel insights for the treatment of optic nerve diseases.

works.title: Atomic‐Scale Design, Performance Degradation Mechanisms, and System Integration of Multi‐Principal Element Hydrogen Storage Materials
works.abstract: Solid-state metal hydrides offer high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety for hydrogen storage, yet their practical application is severely hindered by poor room-temperature thermodynamics, sluggish kinetics, impurity gas poisoning, difficult activation, and cycling degradation. Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) have recently emerged as promising candidates to overcome these bottlenecks through their vast compositional space, severe lattice distortion, and synergistic cocktail effect. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MPEAs for solid-state hydrogen storage, bridging atomic-scale design to system-level performance. A unified composition-process-structure-property framework is established that integrates engineering-driven design rules, post-processing techniques, multi-scale computations, machine learning (ML), and high-throughput experiments. Using advanced in situ and ex situ characterization, the atomic-scale origins and cross-scale evolution of surface poisoning, hydrogen-induced amorphization (HIA), disproportionation, pulverization, and defect accumulation. A theoretical framework linking electronic structure to heat and mass transport is further developed, and hydrogen storage bed design, device integration, fuel-cell coupling, manufacturing scalability, and cost analysis are discussed. Finally, key scientific and engineering challenges and future research directions are outlined. This review provides scientific guidance for designing MPEA-based solid-state hydrogen storage systems with high capacity, long cycle life, high poisoning tolerance, fast de-/hydrogenation kinetics, and low cost.

works.title: Engineering High‐Performance Flexible Electronics Through Scalable Manufacturing: Interplay of Materials, Processing, and Morphology
works.abstract: Flexible electronics have garnered extensive attention in recent years considering their promising applications across diverse fields such as communications, energy, display, healthcare, and wearable devices. Unlike laboratory-scale fabrication and integration, the transition of flexible electronics toward commercial applications demands scalable manufacturing that ensures high performance, large-area reproducibility, high yield, and throughput. However, achieving scalable manufacturing while maintaining device performance remains challenging, as fabrication scale-up often induces variations in material assembly, morphology evolution, and device integration, which may compromise functional reliability achieved at the laboratory scale. Generally, current flexible electronic devices can be divided into two categories: planar-type and fiber-type devices, representing two complementary platforms for realizing large-scale and highly integrated systems. In this review, scalable fabrication strategies tailored for each category and the latest advances are systematically summarized. In particular, the interplay among material design, scalable processing, morphology evolution, and device integration is highlighted, with emphasis on strategies that preserve device performance during manufacturing scale-up. Representative planar-type and fiber-type flexible electronic systems are further discussed to demonstrate how the synergistic optimization of material design and scalable manufacturing approaches enables high-performance devices for diverse applications. Finally, we outline remaining challenges and future directions to inform future developments in scalable flexible electronics.

works.title: Coupling Iodine Conversion and Zinc Ion Transport via Molecular Catalysis for Long‐Life Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries are attractive for low‐cost and scalable energy storage owing to their rapid iodine redox and high theoretical capacity. However, their practical application is severely limited by polyiodide shuttling and interfacial mass‐transport imbalance, where polyiodide immobilization and Zn 2+ accessibility are difficult to reconcile for continuous redox compensation, especially under high‐rate conditions. Here, we address this adsorption–transport conflict by screening a series of metalated tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl) porphyrin molecular catalysts and identifying iron (III) meso‐tetrakis (4‐carboxyphenyl) porphyrin (Fe–TCPP) as a unified interfacial regulator catalyst. The Fe–N 4 center provides moderate polyiodide binding, thereby stabilizing iodide intermediates without inducing interfacial passivation. Meanwhile, peripheral carboxyphenyl groups create a zincophilic microenvironment that promotes Zn 2+ accessibility and local ion compensation. This coordinated regulation synchronizes electron transfer and ion redistribution, thereby sustaining reversible iodine redox while avoiding transport blockage. As a result, the Fe–TCPP‐regulated iodine cathode delivers a specific capacity of 178 mAh g −1 and sustains 50 000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Moreover, a pouch cell with a high iodine loading of 22 mg cm −2 operates stably for more than 1300 cycles. This work establishes a molecular‐catalytic framework for the simultaneous regulation of redox‐intermediate adsorption–conversion and ionic transport in aqueous batteries involving soluble redox species.

works.title: Spin‐Selective Hydrogen Utilization Enables Efficient Electrochemical CO 2 ‐to‐CH 4 Conversion in Ag‐Modified Chiral Cu Catalysts for Unassisted Solar Fuel Production
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Although electrochemical CO 2 ‐to‐CH 4 conversion offers a viable pathway to sustainable fuel synthesis, its efficiency is limited by the difficulty of balancing the availability of reactive hydrogen species for multistep CO 2 hydrogenation against the suppression of the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we establish a spin‐selective catalytic strategy using Ag‐modified chiral Cu electrocatalysts to overcome this intrinsic trade‐off. Structural chirality in the Cu framework induces chirality‐induced spin selectivity, which disfavors spin‐singlet H 2 formation, thereby mitigating the HER and favoring productive hydrogen utilization toward CO 2 hydrogenation. Ag modification facilitates the supply of *CO intermediates on adjacent Cu sites. Thus, the chiral Ag/Cu catalyst selectively drives CO 2 reduction toward CH 4 , delivering a CH 4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 67.0% at −0.7 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode while suppressing the HER. When coupled with perovskite‐based photoelectrochemical electrodes, the chiral catalyst enables unassisted solar‐driven CO 2 ‐to‐CH 4 conversion with an FE CH4 of 54.1% and a solar‐to‐fuel efficiency of 5.86%. These results suggest spin‐selective hydrogen utilization as an effective approach to selective hydrocarbon synthesis and bias‐free solar CO 2 ‐to‐fuel conversion.

works.title: Ferroionic‐Assisted, Charge‐Driven Polymorphic Phase Engineering for Multilevel Memristive Devices
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Memristive device operation can arise from diverse microscopic mechanisms, including charge polarization and trapping, magnetic ordering, ionic migration, and structural phase transitions. Among these, crystalline–crystalline phase transitions in polymorphic materials offer a unique platform for nonvolatile resistance modulation but are often hindered by large energy barriers and limited endurance. Here, we demonstrate a multimodal, charge‐driven phase modulation in an atomically thin polymorphic material, Mo 0.92 W 0.08 Te 2 , enabled by electrostatic coupling to a ferroionic substrate, CuInP 2 S 6 . The polymorphic channel exhibits reversible switching between semiconducting and metallic phases via electrostatically accumulated charges, reflecting the intrinsically low energy barrier between its competing polymorphs. Integration with the ferroionic substrate enables spatially localized, nonvolatile charge accumulation in the channel, which provides distinct, programmable phase‐control pathways under a two‐terminal bias configuration. The phase‐induced resistance modulation through field‐driven ionic processes is governed by the evolution of a phase‐dependent Schottky junction at the electrode–channel interface, yielding multiple, stable conductance states under pulsed electrical excitation. Leveraging these experimentally derived synaptic characteristics, we conducted an MNIST inference simulation with a convolutional neural network, achieving 98.45% accuracy. This ferroionic‐assisted phase‐engineering strategy offers new opportunities beyond traditional phase‐change devices for adaptive electronic and neuromorphic material platforms.

works.title: Breaking the Capacity‐Reversibility Linear Trade‐Off in Li–O 2 Batteries via Amorphous Non‐Precious High‐Entropy Alloy Catalysts
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries suffer from sluggish reaction kinetics and rely on precious metal‐based catalysts to facilitate the reaction process. Despite being effective, these costly catalysts would inevitably introduce a critical trade‐off between capacity and reversibility, compromising the high energy density advantage of Li–O 2 batteries. In this study, we have designed an amorphous non‐precious MnFeCoNiCu high‐entropy alloy (A‐HEA) catalyst via a mild liquid‐phase reduction strategy to break the above inherent linear trade‐off. The amorphous and porous structure of A‐HEA could provide a large electrochemical active surface area, diluting the local current density to promote the solution‐mediated discharge pathway. This enables the growth of large‐sized Li 2 O 2 to deliver a discharge capacity reaching 10.8 mAh cm −2 . Additionally, the multielemental synergistic electron redistribution of A‐HEA optimizes the d ‐band center to strengthen the LiO 2 adsorption and weaken the O─O bonding, reducing the overpotential to 0.75 V and extending the battery lifetime by 4−5 times compared to the crystalline counterparts. Importantly, the A‐HEA can be produced at a scale of over 100 g and works well in Li–O 2 pouch cells with a rate capability up to 400 mA and an energy density of 754 Wh kg −1 (560 Wh kg −1 even at −30°C).

works.title: Engineering hypoactivated platelet-derived coating to decouple thrombosis for vascular regeneration
Spatial bridges of hierarchical scaffolds orchestrate MSCs/SCs interaction for bone regeneration
Bioprinted Stiffness‑Tunable Pancreatic Microniches to Decode Early Tumor Initiation Mechanisms
works.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest human cancers, driven in 90% of cases by KRAS mutations and characterized by an intense desmoplastic reaction, early metastasis, and therapy resistance. The mechanisms driving PDAC initiation, however, remain poorly understood because early acinar transformation is difficult to model in a controlled microenvironment. Here, we introduce a microvalve-bioprinted 3D pancreatic cancer initiation niche that supports culture of primary acini from wild-type and Kras-mutant mice, up to 14 days, within gelatin-methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogels. Our printing strategy enables tuning of hydrogel stiffness to cover the range reported for healthy murine pancreas and early stages of desmoplastic remodelling. In this system, wild-type acini retain a predominantly acinar phenotype, whereas intermediate GelMA conditions cooperate with pre-existing oncogenic Kras to promote acinar-to-ductal metaplasia and proliferative programs associated with early neoplastic reprogramming. Multimodal readouts revealed a stiffness-permissive window in which mechanical cues cooperated with oncogenic Kras to promote acinar transdifferenciation, proliferation and distinct stiffness-dependent secretory programs, including inflammatory and stromal-associated factors with previously reported relevance to PDAC biology. The deterministic droplet geometry supported reproducible, high-throughput, and longitudinal analysis under conditions inaccessible to conventional extrusion or laser‑assisted bioprinting, providing an experimental framework to study early Kras-driven acinar reprogramming.

works.title: A ROS‐Responsive Injectable Hydrogel Platform Reprograms the Diabetic Wound Microenvironment to Enable Exosome Therapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Diabetic wounds persist because excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) sustain chronic inflammation and disrupt the regenerative microenvironment, impairing the stability and function of bioactive therapeutic components, including stem cells and extracellular vesicles (EVs). Here, an injectable hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogel integrates microenvironment modulation with regenerative cue delivery by co‐encapsulating ROS‐responsive cerium oxide nanozymes (CeO 2 NPs) and mesenchymal stem cell‐derived exosomes (EXOs). In this system, CeO 2 NPs act as antioxidant regulators that respond to oxidative stress, while EXOs provide regenerative signals for tissue repair. CeO 2 NPs are packaged within a thioketal‐linked PLGA‐PEG shell, enabling ROS‐triggered degradation and on‐demand activation, whereas the in situ crosslinked HA network serves as a localized matrix that protects components and synchronizes their sustained co‐release. Under high‐glucose conditions, the composite hydrogel reduces intracellular ROS, restores mitochondrial membrane potential, and enhances proliferation, migration, and angiogenic activity of endothelial cells and fibroblasts. In a diabetic mouse wound model, the hydrogel accelerates wound closure, accompanied by attenuated oxidative stress and inflammation, enhanced neovascularization and re‐epithelialization, organized collagen remodeling, and a shift of macrophages toward a pro‐regenerative M2 phenotype. This pathology‐responsive antioxidant–regenerative coupling strategy establishes a rational, modular platform for overcoming microenvironmental constraints in exosome‐based regenerative therapies.

works.title: A Biocatalytic Cascade‐Based Cu‐GMP Self‐Assembly Nanozyme for Accelerating Infected Diabetic Wound Healing
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanozymes with multi‐enzyme catalytic properties have emerged as promising multifunctional materials for biosensing and antimicrobial applications. Herein, a copper‐guanosine monophosphate (Cu‐GMP) nanozyme was synthesized via a simple one‐pot method. Its supramolecular network serves as a multifunctional carrier, enabling the encapsulation of functional guest biomolecules and retaining their inherent activity simultaneously. As a proof‐of‐concept, glucose oxidase (GOx) was incorporated to construct a glucose‐responsive cascade catalytic system (GOx@Cu‐GMP). In this system, GOx catalyzes glucose oxidation to produce hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) and gluconic acid. The latter creates a localized acidic microenvironment, which combined with in situ generated H 2 O 2 , effectively activates the peroxidase (POD)‐like activity of Cu‐GMP and further generates hydroxyl radicals (•OH). Leveraging this cascade reaction, GOx@Cu‐GMP was developed as a sensitive colorimetric platform for glucose detection. Furthermore, Cu‐GMP exhibits oxidase (OXD)‐, laccase (LAC)‐, and glutathione peroxidase (GPx)‐like activities, facilitating the generation of various reactive oxygen species. Benefiting from multi‑enzyme synergy, it achieves broad‑spectrum antibacterial performance. Moreover, GOx@Cu‐GMP can eliminate bacterial infections and accelerate wound healing in a diabetic mouse skin wound model. This work provides a multifunctional nanozyme‐based platform for glucose detection and diabetic wound antimicrobial therapy, offering new insights for the development of integrated biosensing and therapeutic materials.

works.title: A Mitochondrial Autophagy‐Synthesis Dynamic Equilibrium Liposome for the Repair of Energy Metabolism in Acute Kidney Injury
works.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a clinical syndrome primarily attributed to mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by disrupted mitochondrial balance. Impaired biogenesis leads to insufficient energy supply, while defective autophagy results in the accumulation of damaged mitochondria-both of which exacerbate injury to renal tubular epithelial cells.
