In this study, we developed melatonin/pioglitazone liposomes (MP@Lip) for AKI therapy via restoration of mitochondrial dynamic balance. When melatonin and pioglitazone was jointly delivered to damaged renal tubules, they activated mitochondrial autophagy and biogenesis, thereby bidirectionally restoring mitochondrial network homeostasis. Mechanistically, AMPK/SIRT3/PGC-1α-related signaling may be involved in the mitochondrial protection of MP@Lip. Upon AMPK phosphorylation, SIRT1/SIRT3 deacetylase activity is upregulated, the ratio of LC3B-II/LC3B-I increases, p62/SQSTM1 decreases, and autophagy is enhanced. PGC-1α enhances transcriptional activity and promotes the expression of mitochondrial biogenic markers (TOM20). This complementary degradation-synthesis loop gradually restores mitochondrial dynamic balance. In vitro experiments confirmed that MP@Lip reduces ROS production and apoptosis while restoring mitochondrial membrane potential. In vivo studies demonstrated improvement in renal function indicators, alleviation of inflammatory responses and histopathological damage, and no systemic toxicity. This strategy shifts AKI treatment from symptomatic support to ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction, providing a targeted, complementary and relatively safe approach that may be applicable to other mitochondrial functional-related diseases.

works.title: Inhibiting Lactylation‐Mediated Metabolic‐Epigenetic Reprogramming to Potentiate Tumor Photo‐Immunotherapy
works.abstract: Cancer immunotherapies face limitations in treating "cold" tumors due to immune suppression driven by metabolic dysregulation within the tumor microenvironment. Research has revealed that tumor cells produce excess lactate via hypoxia-induced glycolysis, promoting histone lactylation and establishing immunosuppression-associated metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming. Here, a near-infrared (NIR)-triggered nanoplatform (RgA-L-I/P/R) has been developed to fundamentally dismantle the immunosuppression via the metabolic-epigenetic axis. Upon NIR excitation, the platform released oxygen from perfluoropentane (PFP) ("oxygen unlocking chamber") in the tumor through dual targeting of AS1411 and Rg3 ("nano-warhead"), liberating the IR-1048 and the CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) ("NIR immune trigger" and "metabolic nanolock"). IR-1048 induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) to trigger dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, while CRISPR/Cas9 RNP induced LDHA (lactate dehydrogenase A) gene knockdown that locked the lactate supply and reprogrammed metabolism and epigenetics. These changes reduced histone lactylation and IL-10 expression, promoting the conversion of tumor-associated macrophages to the M1 type and synergistically downregulating hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression upon oxygen release. This nanoplatform enables synergistic photothermal immunostimulation with CRISPR-mediated metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. Rather than merely countering mild downstream immune regulation by ICD, it seeks to fundamentally eliminate the immunosuppression, offering novel therapeutic strategies through the metabolic-epigenetic pathway for poorly immunoresponsive tumors.

works.title: Antimicrobial living double-layer skin dressing for inflammation reduction and skin barrier restoration to alleviate Malassezia -induced skin damage
works.abstract: Abstract Microecological imbalance associated with Malassezia overgrowth is closely related to the pathogenesis of diverse cutaneous disorders. However, conventional antifungal therapies face critical challenges, including pathogen resistance induction and inflammation exacerbation. To address these, developing safe and effective biological therapies is crucial for managing Malassezia -associated dermatitis. Here, a double-layer skin dressing is designed to efficiently inhibit Malassezia and mitigate Malassezia -induced skin inflammation in mice. The lower layer comprises Paenibacillus polymyxa JWYB12, which inhibits M. restricta , and the upper layer is a hydrogel composed of Pluronic F-127, polydopamine (PDA), anti-inflammatory exopolysaccharide EPS1, and oxygen-producing Spirulina (SP). Temperature elevation from 4°C to 37°C triggers rapid gelation and robust skin adhesion of the upper layer. SP-mediated oxygen production significantly upregulates energy metabolism genes, thereby enhancing JWYB12 proliferation, while EPS1 exerts a synergistic growthpromoting effect. Collectively, the upper layer markedly augments JWYB12 abundance and its inhibitory activity against M. restricta . In murine models, the dressing significantly reduces dermatitis scores and epidermal thickness, alleviates inflammation via cytokine downregulation, and restores skin barrier function by upregulating barrier proteins, thus effectively controlling M. restricta -induced inflammation. These properties make this double-layer skin dressing an effective clinical treatment for Malassezia -induced dermatitis, presenting a promising biological therapy strategy for pathogen-associated dermatoses.

works.title: Hybrid Chitosan–BSA Bioinks for DLP Biofabrication and DLP-Assisted Molding of 3D Hydrogel Constructs with Embedded Branched Structures
works.abstract: Digital light processing (DLP) bioprinting enables rapid fabrication of high-resolution three-dimensional constructs, but its broader application remains limited by the availability of bioinks that combine structural stability with biological functionality. Here, we present a hybrid chitosan methacrylate-bovine serum albumin methacrylate (ChiMA-BSA-MA) bioink that integrates the structural support of methacrylated chitosan with the biologically favorable properties of methacrylated bovine serum albumin for DLP biofabrication. The hybrid formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior, rapid photocrosslinking under 405 nm light exposure, and composition-dependent rheological and mechanical properties suitable for vat photopolymerization. Selected formulations enabled fabrication of free-standing constructs exceeding 10 mm in height while maintaining preserved microscale features. Representative complex geometries and embedded branched structures were successfully fabricated using direct DLP printing together with a complementary DLP-assisted molding strategy. Unlike many existing approaches that rely on extrusion-based bioprinting, support-bath printing, sacrificial templates, coaxial nozzles, or other multistep fabrication procedures, the proposed workflow combines direct DLP printing with a simple secondary molding step using a conventional DLP printer. Biological evaluation demonstrated sustained metabolic activity and cell viability over 14 days. Under chondrogenic differentiation conditions, RT-qPCR showed increased expression of SOX9, COL2A1, ACAN, ELN, COL10A1, and MMP13, indicating induction of chondrogenic and hypertrophy-associated marker expression. Overall, the ChiMA-BSA-MA hybrid bioink provides a versatile platform for DLP biofabrication of tissue models with embedded branched structures, expanding the range of photocurable bioinks available for advanced in vitro tissue engineering applications.

works.title: A fluorinated poly(amino acid) nanovaccine with spatiotemporally encoded innate priming and antigen cross-presentation for tumor immunotherapy
works.abstract: The efficacy of cancer vaccines depends on spatiotemporally coordinated innate immune priming and antigen cross-presentation, but this hierarchy remains difficult to control with existing delivery platforms. Here, we report a fluorinated diethylenetriamine-modified poly(aspartic acid) nanovaccine platform, termed DET-F, and identify DET-F30 as the optimized formulation for antigen delivery and immune activation. Perfluorooctyl side chains promote early endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) associated innate immune signaling and dendritic cell maturation, whereas the pH-responsive polymer backbone facilitates subsequent endosomal escape and cytosolic antigen release. This chemically encoded sequence enables delayed yet enhanced antigen cross-presentation in mature dendritic cells. DET-F30/antigen nanoparticles display efficient antigen loading and cellular uptake, activate TLR3-related innate immune pathways, and elicit robust antigen-specific CD8 + T cell immunity. In multiple tumor models, DET-F30-based vaccination suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, prolongs survival, and enhances post-surgical anti-PD-1 therapy. This work establishes fluorinated poly(amino acid)s as minimalist self-adjuvant nanovaccine vectors and demonstrates that precise polymer-architecture encoding can orchestrate sequential innate immune activation and antigen processing for improved cancer immunotherapy.

works.title: Heterostructure Design in Two‐Dimensional Perovskites by Sequential Recrystallization
works.abstract: Low-dimensional metal halide perovskites provide exciting opportunities to fabricate new semiconductor materials. Semiconductor technology relies on electronic heterojunctions, and cost-efficient and flexible approaches to realize functional heterostructures are of fundamental importance. Lateral heterostructures define the energy landscape in the plane of the semiconducting lattice in 2D perovskite materials, representing an ideal platform to tailor energy barriers and to control charge carrier flow. Here, we demonstrate a versatile one-pot synthesis to fabricate a large variety of 2D perovskite heterostructures based on different halides and/or metal cations. Exploiting sequential crystallization of different 2D perovskites and tuning the composition and injection events of the materials, enables the design of diverse heterostructure architectures, including multiple heterojunctions. We obtain heterostructures with high crystalline quality, multicolor emission, and optical coupling between the different heterostructure regions. We foresee that the design freedom of our method will stimulate the development of novel optoelectronic devices where electronic band engineering is crucial.

works.title: A Noninvasive Approach to Study Localized Forces in 3D Epithelia
works.abstract: Epithelial tissue integrity and remodeling rely on mechanical coupling between cytoskeletal organization and adhesion complexes, but their orchestration in three-dimensional (3D) epithelia remains unresolved. Here, we introduced a noninvasive strategy to locally probe forces within 3D epithelial tissues. We engineered elastic polyacrylamide (PAAm) microbeads with cell-like size and mechanical properties, enabling their integration into tissues. PAAm microbeads were spontaneously engulfed by the tissue, establishing an intrinsic interface. This allowed bead deformation to be directly correlated with local cytoskeletal architecture and adhesion organization, visualized through high-resolution imaging and quantitative 3D computational reconstruction. Using this approach, we demonstrated that localized mechanical perturbations trigger cytoskeletal remodeling while preserving tissue polarity. We further identified extracellular matrix composition as a key determinant of bead-tissue interactions. At the bead-cell interface, cells assembled tension-bearing focal adhesions and actin stress fibers. Quantitative analysis of bead deformation revealed sub-cellular scale patterns of cell-bead interaction forces, which correlated with the localization of cytoskeletal elements. Our findings extend previous traction force microscopy observations to 3D, revealing coordinated, spatially heterogeneous forces specifically at the cell-bead interface. Taken together, this enabled us to dissect the interplay between cellular processes and tissue mechanics in a noninvasive way in 3D model systems.

works.title: Twistsonics: Engineering Acoustic Topological Textures in Moiré Sound Lattices
works.abstract: Moiré superlattices formed by twisting periodic systems provide a powerful platform for emergent topological phenomena, but their use for programming real-space topology in acoustic wave fields remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a phase-controlled spoof surface acoustic wave platform for constructing moiré topological textures in the acoustic particle-velocity field. On a perforated acoustic metasurface, two twisted skyrmion lattices are synthesized and superposed, yielding acoustic skyrmion bags with controllable topological numbers and geometries. The twist angle and rotation center control the scale and configuration of the bags, enabling deterministic reshaping of the composite texture. We further introduce controlled defects to assess the defect tolerance of the moiré skyrmion bags. The skyrmion bags retain their composite topology over a finite range of defect fractions, and comparison with an untwisted single-layer skyrmion lattice suggests enhanced stability of the enclosed skyrmion cluster relative to the single-layer reference at higher defect fractions. The same programmable platform also supports transitions from skyrmion lattices to meron lattices and enables twist-induced meron clusters. These findings establish acoustic moiré superlattices as a reconfigurable platform for engineering robust real-space topological textures, with potential applications in topology-guided acoustic manipulation and information encoding.

works.title: Buried CdSe Sacrificial Layer Driving Phase Evolution and Crystallization Kinetics Enables 14.78%‐Efficient DMF‐Based Kesterite Solar Cells
works.abstract: ABSTRACT During selenization, the inherent transport lag of Se from the film surface to the buried Mo/precursor interface causes early‐stage Se deficiency in the bottom region, creating a depth‐dependent crystallization lag that limits the homogeneity of Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 (CZTSSe) absorbers. Here, we evaporate an ultrathin CdSe sacrificial layer at the Mo/precursor interface of N,N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF)‐derived CZTSSe absorbers. This layer is rapidly consumed at the onset of selenization, providing an in‐situ Se supply at the buried interface and effectively bypassing the intrinsic transport delay from the surface. The locally supplied Se initiates early‐stage bottom selenization and promotes the conversion of Cu 2 SnSe 3 ‐related intermediates toward CZTSSe while suppressing their persistent accumulation, enabling rear‐side nucleation and grain growth to commence substantially earlier than in the conventional surface‐dominated process. Meanwhile, the redistributed Cd 2+ partially substitutes Zn 2+ sites, reducing defect‐assisted recombination and enhancing carrier transport and extraction. The optimized device achieves a champion efficiency of 14.78% with a certified efficiency of 14.30%, establishing a new benchmark for DMF‐derived kesterite solar cells. This work demonstrates that prepositioning a sacrificial Se‐containing component at the buried interface to enable in situ release of Se offers a viable pathway for coordinating phase evolution and improving multinary chalcogenide absorber quality.

works.title: Coordination Bridges in Confined‐Water Domains Enable Partially Desolvated Zn 2 + Transport in Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc‐ion batteries (ZIBs), owing to their intrinsic safety and cost competitiveness, are attracting significant interest as next‐generation energy storage system (ESS) technologies. However, their commercialization is severely hindered by poor cycle stability, primarily originating from dendritic Zn growth and parasitic hydrogen evolution. To address these challenges simultaneously, we design and integrate a multifunctional polymeric protective layer incorporating amide and imidazolium functional groups. The zincophilic amide groups facilitate ion transport by providing stable Zn 2+ binding sites, whereas the hygroscopic imidazolium groups establish a confined‐water domain that regulates local solvation dynamics. Within this domain, water molecules transiently stabilize Zn 2+ and act as a coordination bridge during ion migration, yet their mobility toward the electrode surface is restricted. This dual functionality increases the Zn 2+ single‐ion conductivity 6.55‐fold and reduces the hydrogen evolution rate by 79.1%. Consequently, Zn//Zn symmetric cells exhibit markedly extended cycling lifetimes of up to 2200 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . When applied to Zn–I 2 full cells, the protective layer enables stable operation over 4000 cycles with >85% capacity retention, even under a practical areal capacity of 3.6 mAh cm −2 . These findings highlight a robust interfacial strategy to realize long‐duration, high‐capacity aqueous ZIBs for grid‐scale energy storage.

works.title: Non‐Selective Suppression of Cation and Anion Crosstalk from an Anode Perspective
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal fluoride and sulfur cathodes are appealing for their abundance and high capacity but are plagued by severe electrode crosstalk. This occurs when transition metal cations or polysulfide anions dissolve and shuttle to the anode, causing corrosion and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose an anode‐centric mechanism utilizing a Na‐rich nanoalloy (Na x Sn) anode that achieves simultaneous kinetic regulation and physical shielding, suppressing cation and anion crosstalk at both the source and destination. The ultrafast kinetics of the Na x Sn alloy elevate the Damköhler number (Da), a descriptor quantifying the competition between conversion and diffusion, thereby ensuring these species are rapidly reduced at the cathode prior to outward diffusion. Concurrently, this nanoalloy induces the formation of an ultrathin, robust Na 2 O‐rich solid electrolyte interphase that non‐selectively blocks residual cation and anion crossovers. This mechanism enables an FeF 2 ||Na x Sn full cell to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.93% over 200 cycles. Additionally, the S/C||Na x Sn system supports extreme rate capabilities (630 mAh g −1 at 20C) and transitions to practical pouch cell configurations, yielding an excellent capacity retention of 91.95% after 1000 cycles at 0.5C. Ultimately, Na‐rich nanoalloy anodes offer a compelling pathway toward high‐energy, sustainable batteries by transforming electrode crosstalk into a spatiotemporally synergistic anode‐cathode coupling.

works.title: Bio-orthogonally functionalized biomimetic nanoreactors suppress lung cancer stem-like cells by triggering a self-amplifying endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria stress loop
Editorial Board
Heptamethine cyanines serve as photocaged Michael electrophiles for spatiotemporal GPX4 inhibition and ferroptosis immunotherapy
Programmed Gut–Liver‐Targeted Oral Delivery of Peptide‐Probiotic Nano‐Microsystem for Metabolic Complications of Hyperglycemia and Hyperuricemia
authors: WANG Xiao-gang 1,  CHEN Yi-feng 2,  LU Bo 3,  WANG Yu-jie 1,  XU Wei-ya 4,  YANG Qiang 5,  ZHANG Xi-wei 6
works.abstract: Hyperglycemia and hyperuricemia are highly prevalent metabolic comorbidities characterized by systemic metabolic disturbances and complex multi-organ pathogenesis, urgently requiring synergistic multi-organ-targeted therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a programmed gut-liver-targeted oral peptide-probiotic nano-microsystem for metabolic complications of hyperglycemia and hyperuricemia treatment. The xanthine oxidase (XOD)-inhibitory peptide PPKNW (P1) was loaded in a layer-by-layer reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticle (P1NPs), followed by engineering on the surface of probiotic Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk), resulting in a peptide-probiotic nano-microsystem (P1NPs@Akk). After oral administration, P1NPs@Akk remained stable during gastric passage. Upon reaching intestinal environment, CS and HA layers were progressively removed, exposing the P1-loaded polymersomes, which were transported across the intestinal epithelium via PAT-1-mediated transcytosis. In the liver, P1 was released in response to ROS-mediated disulfide bond cleavage to inhibit XOD and reduce uric acid synthesis. Meanwhile, Akk was delivered to and colonized in the intestine to regulate glucose metabolism. In a mouse model of combined hyperglycemia and hyperuricemia, P1NPs@Akk promoted hepatic accumulation of P1 and intestinal enrichment of Akk, resulting in significant reductions in blood glucose and uric acid levels. This work presents a programmed gut-liver-targeted oral platform that integrates peptide therapy and probiotic intervention for multi-organ regulation of metabolic disorders.

works.title: NIR‐Activated Ag 2 S Quantum Dots for Synergistic Immunomodulation and Precision Therapy of Refractory Osteomyelitis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) is a predominant clinical pathogen responsible for a wide range of infections. By forming biofilms during infection, S. aureus evades conventional therapies, leading to persistent infections and treatment failure. To address this challenge, we employed silver sulfide quantum dots (Ag 2 S QDs) for near‐infrared (NIR) phototherapy. In vitro, the nanoagent achieved >99.99% killing of S. aureus within 10 minutes and reduced biofilm biomass by >58%. In a murine osteomyelitis model, a single NIR treatment reduced bacterial loads by 71.83% on implants and 59.18% in bone tissue, while also suppressing key inflammatory cytokines, with local macrophage polarization shifting from an M1‐dominant to an M2‐dominant phenotype. Histopathological and micro‐CT analyses indicated attenuated bone destruction. The nanoagent showed favorable biosafety, with no systemic toxicity in major organs and osteoblast viability >75% at therapeutic concentrations. Together, these results demonstrate a phototherapeutic strategy with combined antibacterial and anti‐biofilm effects, supporting its potential as an adjuvant approach for managing refractory osteomyelitis.

works.title: Digital cell factories for biomanufacturing
Spatially Resolved Cell-Fate Engineering through Nanoneedle-Mediated Optoporation
works.abstract: The development of advanced tissue models demands spatially resolved control over cell fate to provide deeper insights into complex biological processes, yet precise intracellular manipulation remains a critical bottleneck in cellular engineering strategies. Current approaches for gene delivery struggle in achieving the required localized resolution to control individual cell fate, while optogenetic approaches are constrained by the requirement for complex genetic engineering and limited modes of gene regulation. Here, we show that nanoneedle-mediated optoporation enables spatially resolved intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, locally directing cell fate. Through computational modeling and experimental validation, we investigated the dependence of electromagnetic field enhancement on wavelength, nanoneedle geometry, and porosity. We demonstrated the importance of surface chemistry for optoporation efficiency, achieving optimal transfection performance through thermal carbonization. This approach achieves efficient delivery for propidium iodide, 500 kDa dextran, and siRNA, alongside a 72% mRNA transfection efficiency, resulting in sustained protein expression after 24 h. Selective SNAIL1 mRNA transfection demonstrated localized cell-fate engineering, inducing a targeted epithelial to mesenchymal transition. This porous nanoneedle system presents a versatile and flexible approach for precise genetic manipulation through electromagnetic field tunability, offering new possibilities for studying complex biological processes and disease progression through spatially resolved control of cell fate.

works.title: Nanotechnology-enabled construction of bispecific and multispecific antibody platforms for enhanced antitumor therapy
works.abstract: Refractory solid tumors are characterized by pronounced antigen heterogeneity, dense tissue barriers, and immunosuppressive microenvironments, which limit the tumor coverage and durable immune clearance achieved with conventional monospecific antibodies. Bispecific and multispecific antibodies (BsAbs and MsAbs) can recognize two or more antigens or epitopes, thereby integrating tumor targeting, immune-cell recruitment, and regulation of multiple signaling pathways within a single therapeutic system. However, soluble BsAbs and MsAbs remain limited by suboptimal circulatory stability, inadequate penetration and accumulation in solid tumors, limited control over antibody stoichiometry and spatial organization, and toxicities associated with systemic immune activation. Nanotechnology provides an engineering framework for addressing these limitations. Through chemical conjugation, affinity-tag-mediated assembly, anti-mPEG/mPEG anchoring, or Fc-mediated binding, nanocarriers can integrate multiple antibodies and therapeutic modules on a single platform while enabling multivalent display, oriented immobilization, and control over component ratios. Pharmacokinetics and tumor exposure can also be improved by nanoparticles; multivalent binding and immune-cell-tumor-cell bridging can be strengthened, and localized activation and combination therapy can be enabled through valency control, stimuli-responsive release, and co-delivery of therapeutic payloads. This review summarizes the principal construction strategies for nanotechnology-enabled BsAbs and MsAbs. It examines how these systems enhance binding avidity, improve in vivo delivery, increase therapeutic safety, and potentiate multimodal antitumor activity. Translational considerations, including quality control, immunogenicity, and scalable manufacturing, are discussed in the context of approved bispecific antibodies and early-phase clinical studies.

works.title: Sustained intestinal hydrogen delivery enhances exercise endurance in mice with coordinated gut-liver-muscle metabolic responses
works.abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) exerts unique metabolic-modulating effects, yet its clinical translation is hindered by a fundamental pharmacokinetic challenge. Rapid systemic diffusion and short intestinal residence time require frequent dosing regimens to maintain sustained tissue exposure. Here, we demonstrate that sustained intestinal H 2 delivery improves exercise endurance and correlates with coordinated metabolic responses across the intestine, liver, and skeletal muscle. Mechanistically, continuous intestinal H 2 exposure is associated with reduced intestinal inflammatory and oxidative alterations, increased hepatic FOXO1 and gluconeogenesis-related protein abundance, as well as altered expression of glycolysis- and lactate-handling components in skeletal muscle. These observations support a working model in which sustained intestinal H 2 exposure is associated with coordinated gut-liver-muscle metabolic responses during strenuous exercise. Although these coordinated metabolic changes were initially observed using a high-frequency hydrogen-rich water (HRW) gavage protocol, this approach is limited by repeated-administration requirements. To address this translational barrier and prolong H 2 exposure duration, we engineered Mg@SiO 2 @ES, an orally deliverable, intestine-targeted hydrogen-generating micro-reactor. This formulation is designed to resist gastric degradation and enable sustained H 2 release selectively within the intestinal lumen. It recapitulates multiple metabolic and exercise-related phenotypes observed with repeated HRW gavage. In murine acute exhaustive-exercise models, a single pre-exercise gavage of Mg@SiO 2 @ES enhanced exercise performance. This improvement was accompanied by attenuated oxidative stress, lower blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels, and better preservation of circulating glucose and intramuscular glycogen stores. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of sustained intestinal H 2 delivery to elicit systemic metabolic responses. They also demonstrate bioengineered gas-releasing micro-reactors as a promising strategy for further exploration of targeted H 2 delivery in metabolic and exercise-related research.

works.title: Neutrophil-tropic APL@Mn3O4 nanozymes alleviate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury through redox regulation
works.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is driven by coupled oxidative and inflammatory amplification after reperfusion, with activated neutrophils acting as early upstream effectors that propagate secondary cardiomyocyte injury. Strategies limited to downstream oxidative damage may therefore be insufficient to interrupt this reinforcing cascade. We developed an agglutinated-protein liposome formulation encapsulating Mn 3 O 4 nanozymes (APL@Mn 3 O 4 ), designed to integrate delivery directed toward activated neutrophils with catalytic redox regulation. The agglutinated-protein liposomal surface supported complement-associated tropism toward activated neutrophils under inflammatory conditions, whereas the Mn 3 O 4 core retained catalytic antioxidant activity for reactive oxygen species (ROS) regulation. In vitro , APL@Mn 3 O 4 reduced neutrophil oxidative and inflammatory responses without measurably impairing migratory capacity under the tested conditions. In a neutrophil-cardiomyocyte co-culture system, APL@Mn 3 O 4 attenuated oxidative stress and apoptosis in injured cardiomyocytes. In vivo , APL@Mn 3 O 4 preferentially associated with circulating neutrophils, attenuated oxidative and inflammatory myocardial injury, and improved post-reperfusion cardiac remodeling and function. These findings support APL@Mn 3 O 4 as a neutrophil-tropic nanozyme platform for alleviating MIRI by attenuating pathological neutrophil-associated oxidative and inflammatory activity and reducing secondary cardiomyocyte injury.

works.title: Does simvastatin-adenosine-loaded nanostructured lipid carrier counteract the pathophysiology of diabetic wounds? Evidence from 3D skin models
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic wounds, such as diabetic foot ulcers, represent a clinical challenge due to impaired healing processes. Traditional two-dimensional cell cultures fail to replicate the complexity of human skin, limiting therapeutic predictability. We previously developed nanostructured lipid carrier co-loaded with simvastatin and adenosine (NLC-SA), which enhanced keratinocyte proliferation and skin drug retention. Herein, we advanced to physiologically relevant three-dimensional human skin equivalents (HSEs) and reconstructed human epidermis (RHEs) to model chronic diabetic wounds and evaluate the therapeutic potential of NLC-SA. RHE generated from primary human keratinocytes (NHEK) exhibited superior epidermal architecture and barrier properties compared with HaCat-based constructs and was selected for subsequent studies. Full-thickness HSEs were developed using NHEK and primary human dermal fibroblasts (NHDF). Chronic wound-like conditions were induced by exposure to high glucose and TNF-α for five days, which reduced tissue viability, increased inflammatory mediators (IL-1α and IL-8) and expression of the corresponding inflammatory genes ( IL1A and CXCL8 ), reduced expression of the oxidative stress-responsive gene HMOX1 , disrupted epidermal differentiation ( LOR and FLG downregulation), and decreased VEGF secretion. NLC-SA treatment exerted multifaceted therapeutic effects. In RHE, treatment improved tissue viability, downregulated IL1A and CXCL8 mRNA expression, and increased HMOX1 and LOR mRNA expression. In both RHE and HSE models, NLC-SA reduced IL-1α and IL-8 secretion and enhanced VEGF release. Pro-angiogenic activity was further supported by the chick chorioallantoic membrane assay, in which NLC-SA increased relative vessel growth and total vessel length. In conclusion, NLC-SA demonstrated significant cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory, and pro-angiogenic properties in a human-relevant 3D chronic wound model, providing a rationale for further evaluation of its therapeutic efficacy in diabetic wound models in vivo .

works.title: Natural product integrated metal-organic frameworks for chronic wound healing: From pathological signal responsiveness to on-demand drug delivery
works.abstract: Natural products (NPs) possess remarkable structural diversity and broad biological activities, giving them substantial potential in chronic wound therapy. However, unfavorable physicochemical properties and poorly controlled local exposure often limit their therapeutic performance. Integrating NPs with metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) offers benefits beyond improved drug delivery. NPs can be encapsulated as cargo, incorporated as coordinating ligands, or immobilized on MOF surfaces, while natural macromolecules may themselves form bioactive dressing matrices. Thus, the key issue is not only which NP is incorporated, but also how its material role affects bioavailability and stage-specific therapeutic function. Centered on NPs, this review establishes a framework for understanding MOF-based wound therapies and explains how NP chemistry and material roles govern responsiveness to endogenous pathological signals or external physical stimuli. These effects are further linked to the changing needs of chronic wound healing, from early control of microbial burden and persistent inflammation to tissue regeneration and extracellular matrix remodeling. By moving beyond the conventional view of NPs as passive cargo, this review provides a unified design rationale for stage-adaptive NP-MOF biomaterials and bioactive dressings.

Osteoarthritis‐Microenvironment‐Triggered Phase Alteration of Injectable Conductive Hydrogel for Attenuating Cartilage Degradation
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which contributes substantially to chondrocyte dysfunction, oxidative stress, and cartilage degradation. Although stimuli-responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for OA therapy, conventional hydrogel-based systems exhibit limited sensitivity and require external detection equipment, highlighting the need for a simple, sensitive, and directly observable monitoring system. To address these challenges, we developed a ROS-triggered, in situ-forming gel-sol transition of a polydopamine (PDA)-loaded, diselenide-crosslinked polymer dot (PD) injectable hydrogel (HGC-PDA@PD or OA gel) as a monitorable theranostic for OA therapy at physiological temperature (37°C). The monitorable OA microenvironment-responsive hydrogel relied on interactions between the high ROS levels in OA cartilage and the OA gel, which triggered diselenide bond cleavage and the release of PDA from PD, causing a unique gel-sol transition of the OA gel. Owing to PDA release after diselenide breakage, the fluorescence and electroconductivity of the OA gel changed, which could serve as additional signals during OA detection. In vitro studies demonstrated the sensitive gel-sol transition of OA gel towards OA-induced immature articular chondrocytes (IL-1β/siSOD1/siCatalase-transfected iMACs). Furthermore, the OA gel showed a distinct gel-sol transition in cartilage of an in vivo OA mouse model compared with that in control mice. The lower transcription levels of cartilage matrix-degrading enzymes (ADAMTS4, ADAMTS5, MMP-3, and MMP-13) observed after OA gel injection confirmed that the OA gel could scavenge ROS and attenuate cartilage damage, revealing its potential application for dual-function OA diagnosis and rehabilitation.

works.title: Core‐Shell Microneedles for Sequential Delivery of Antibacterial, Antioxidant, and Anti‐Inflammatory Agents in Infected Wound Healing
works.abstract: Infected wounds are dynamic pathological processes that progress through acute, chronic, and repair phases, each with distinct therapeutic requirements. Conventional treatments, which release all drugs simultaneously, often fail to meet these stage-specific needs. In this study, we develop a multifunctional core-shell microneedle (MN) system capable of sequential delivery of different therapeutics to address the requirements of various healing stages. During the acute phase, the shell composed of gelatin-hydroxyphenylalanine (Gtn-HPA) hydrogel rapidly releases bacitracin (Bac), thereby inhibiting bacterial proliferation. During the chronic phase, MMP9-responsive peptide nanoparticles (INM-1@EDA) within the MN core undergo enzymatic cleavage, releasing the edaravone (EDA) and indomethacin (INM) moieties to exert antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, respectively. During the repair phase, the residual gelatin at the site supports keratinocyte proliferation and migration, promoting skin tissue regeneration. In a mouse wound model with Staphylococcus aureus infection, core-shell MN treatment achieves nearly complete wound closure in 12 days (96.7 ± 1.3%) with markedly reduced bacterial burden and decreased inflammatory cytokine levels. This MN system achieves sequential release of antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant therapeutics based on wound microenvironments, offering new strategies for efficacious treatment of infected wounds.

works.title: Breaking the Vicious Cycle for Diabetic Wound Healing: A Dynamic‐Static Dual‐Mode Nanofiber Platform for NETs Degradation, Inflammation Resolution, and Scar Prevention
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic diabetic wounds are trapped in a self‐perpetuating vicious cycle—persistent infection, oxidative stress, and NET‐driven inflammation—that severely impairs healing. Here, we engineer a piezoelectric nanofiber membrane (DMTP) that breaks this cycle via a dynamic‐static dual‐mode strategy. DMTP integrates a Mn‐Ti bimetallic MOF with sustained DNase I release, enabling four coordinated functions: (i) piezodynamic ROS generation for on‐demand antibacterial action; (ii) an electric field to guide fibroblast migration; (iii) sustained DNase I release to degrade pathological NETs; and (iv) intrinsic POD/SOD enzyme‐mimetic activity for continuous ROS scavenging. Mechanistically, we show that NETs drive fibroblast differentiation into α‐SMA + myofibroblasts, a key fibrotic driver, and DMTP effectively suppresses this pro‐fibrotic process. In diabetic mice, DMTP achieves 94.32% wound closure with orderly collagen deposition and modulated inflammation (TNF‐α↓, TGF‐β↑). In a rabbit ear hypertrophic scar model, DMTP significantly reduces scar formation by inhibiting α‐SMA expression. This work offers a transformative strategy to achieve diabetic wound healing with diminished scarring by directly dismantling the infection–oxidative stress–NETs–fibrosis axis.

works.title: Microwave‐Responsive AIE Nanocomposite Induces Immunogenic Senescence for Imaging‐Guided Therapy and Bone Repair in Osteosarcoma
works.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains challenging due to incomplete tumor resection, local recurrence, and limited immunostimulatory efficacy of current microwave (MW)-based therapies. Here, we develop a multifunctional theranostic nanoplatform, GPC3@TTBC, by conjugating an osteosarcoma-targeting anti-GPC3 peptide onto aggregation-induced emission (AIE) nanoparticles. GPC3@TTBC enables selective tumor accumulation and high-contrast near-infrared fluorescence imaging, allowing precise tumor margin delineation and superior tumor-to-background resolution compared with clinically used dyes, including effective visualization in patient-derived xenograft models. Upon MW irradiation, lysosome-localized GPC3@TTBC generates robust nonthermal reactive oxygen species (ROS) through enhanced charge separation and electron transfer, resulting in substantial tumor cell apoptosis while simultaneously inducing a prominent immunogenic senescence-associated phenotype and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) response. Importantly, MW + GPC3@TTBC suppressed tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and reduced pulmonary metastatic lesions in vivo. Meanwhile, the SASP promoted dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte activation, thereby enhancing antitumor immune responses and remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. Beyond tumor eradication, GPC3@TTBC facilitates osteogenic microenvironment reconstruction and bone regeneration after tumor clearance, while exhibiting favorable biosafety. Collectively, GPC3@TTBC integrates targeted fluorescence-guided imaging, MW-enhanced ROS generation, immunogenic senescence induction, and bone regeneration, providing a comprehensive theranostic strategy for precise osteosarcoma treatment.

works.title: Hypoxia‐Guided Magnetic Catheter for Localization and Minimally Invasive Intervention in Early‐Stage Lung Cancer
works.abstract: To enable the precise localization and minimally invasive treatment of early-stage pulmonary lesions, we developed a magnetic catheter system integrating magnetic navigation, hypoxia fluorescence imaging, and multifunctional minimally invasive intervention. The distal end of the system incorporates multiple permanent magnets, a miniature camera equipped with an optical filter, multiple fiber-optic channels, and a flexibly switchable multifunctional working channel. Under a 40 mT magnetic field applied perpendicular to the initial catheter axis, the catheter incorporating 2.0 mm-diameter magnets achieved a bending angle of 39.63° ± 2.47° and successfully navigated to multiple designated branches in the bronchial phantom. A proof-of-concept model was established using A549 lung cancer spheroids labeled with hypoxia-responsive fluorescent probes, enabling fluorescence-guided localization of simulated hypoxic lesions. In the bronchial phantom, the system successfully identified simulated hypoxic lesions and subsequently performed biopsy sampling, simulated drug delivery, and localized laser irradiation. The system was further evaluated in porcine lungs to demonstrate its navigation and localized intervention capabilities. This magnetic catheter system provides a new technological strategy for the precise localization and in situ treatment of early-stage lung cancer.

works.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson’s disease therapy
Breast milk is an overlooked biofluid for point-of-care biosensing
Regulation of hepatic stellates cell activation by biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels with uniform and heterogeneous matrix stiffness
works.abstract: Current research on liver fibrosis predominantly relies on culture matrices with uniform stiffness, largely overlooking the pathophysiological relevance of stiffness heterogeneity-the spatially uneven stiffness distribution characteristic of fibrotic liver tissue. To address this, we engineered biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels using decellularized liver matrix (DLM) from fibrotic tissues and methacrylated hyaluronic acid (MeHA). These hydrogels replicated the distinct stiffness profiles of normal, earlystage fibrotic, and late-stage fibrotic liver. Using a custom honeycomb-shaped mold, we integrated them into a unified platform featuring both uniform and heterogeneous mechanical regions. By co-culturing hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) on this platform, we investigated how matrix stiffness regulates HSCs proliferation, migration, and activation. Results demonstrated that on uniformly stiff substrates, particularly those mimicking late-stage fibrosis, ECM components and high stiffness promoted HSCs activation, upregulated the Piezo1-YAP signaling axis. In contrast, although the lowstiffness region of the mechanically heterogeneous platform exhibited increased HSC proliferation and activation, the proliferation and activation levels in the medium-and high-stiffness regions were significantly reduced. The expression patterns of the Piezo1-YAP signaling pathway further corroborated this phenomenon. These findings suggest that mechanical heterogeneity may exert a negative regulatory effect on HSC activation. This study provides new insights into the mechanobiological mechanisms underlying hepatic fibrosis and reveals potential therapeutic targets.

works.title: Electrospun Janus Nanofibrous Membranes for Diabetic Foot Ulcers: Structure-Function Relationships and Multifunctional Synergistic Therapy
works.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are critical chronic diabetic complications that remain difficult to heal owing to excessive exudation, persistent infection, prolonged inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired tissue regeneration. Conventional wound dressings often fail to address these interconnected pathological conditions. Electrospun Janus nanofibrous membranes (JNMs) with asymmetric structures offer unique opportunities to spatially regulate the wound microenvironment while integrating multiple therapeutic functions within a single platform. This review summarizes recent advances in electrospun JNMs for DFU treatment from the perspective of structure-function relationships. The fabrication methods and structural design principles of JNMs, including asymmetric wettability, pore structures, interfacial functionalization, and spatial therapeutic distribution are first discussed. The relationships between these structural characteristics and key functional properties, including directional exudate transport, controlled therapeutic delivery, antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity, mechanical adaptability, and microenvironment regulation, are then analyzed. Subsequently, the therapeutic applications of JNMs in DFU management, together with recent developments in stimuli-responsive and bioelectronic systems, are reviewed. Finally, current challenges related to mechanical and structural stability, degradation-regeneration compatibility, scalable manufacturing, biosafety, standardized evaluation, and clinical translation are discussed. By linking DFU-specific pathological requirements with JNM structural design, functional regulation, and therapeutic outcomes, this review provides a framework for the rational development of multifunctional Janus dressings for DFU treatment.

works.title: Advances in Flexible Electronic Systems for Electrical Stimulation Assisted Wound Healing
works.abstract: Progress in miniaturization techniques coupled with advancements in material science and wearable technologies has transformed electrical stimulation (ES) technique of wound healing into a smart stand-alone patch. The present review article begins with a glimpse of the market demand and need for ES followed by a brief highlight on wound healing stages and the effects of ES in them. Thereafter, a roadmap on the use and effects of different ES modes is provided covering trials over in vitro cell-culture models as well as in vivo animal models along with details of ES safety parameters and biomaterial interface challenges. Following this, the article provides a detailed description of various inorganic flexible electronic-based ES patches for accelerated wound healing developed during the last decade along with an exhaustive study on various wound monitoring sensors like pH, temperature, moisture, bacterial infection, and metabolites, as well as their interdependency in influencing overall wound health and healing status. Additionally, the article also presents a brief insight into modern ES patches categorized under self-powered nanogenerator-driven and hydrogel-based patches along with integration of wireless communication and closed-loop control systems for an efficient wound healing system. Finally, the article concludes with a brief note highlighting the current unresolved bottlenecks required for its wider acceptance as well as the future attributes of ES patches catering the needs of generic to complex, hard-to-heal wounds with sophisticated multiparameter monitoring units and integrated AI/ML-driven solutions for driving the next-generation smart bandages.

works.title: Gene-activated matrices as nanomedicine platforms for bone regeneration: Delivery, translation and patent landscape
works.abstract: Protein biologics are constrained in critical-size bone defects not by insufficient potency, but by rapid clearance and the inability to sustain therapeutic signaling at the repair site. Dose escalation does not overcome this pharmacokinetic limitation and instead increases the risk of ectopic bone formation, osteolysis, and soft tissue toxicity. Sustained, localized delivery, not higher dosing, is the unmet requirement. Gene-activated matrices (GAM) address this problem by integrating nucleic acid cargo and delivery vectors within an implantable scaffold, converting infiltrating host cells into local sources of regenerative signals. This review examines GAMs as nanomedicine platforms for bone regeneration, tracing their development from scaffold bioactivity and the limitation of protein biologics to nucleic acid-based delivery. We compare viral vectors, lipid nanoparticles, polymeric polyplexes, calcium phosphate nanoparticles, and scaffold-integrated systems across transduction efficiency, expression kinetics, immunogenicity, and bone-site retention. We then examine how scaffold composition, architecture, and fabrication govern vector retention, release, and substrate-mediated transfection. This review then evaluates nucleic acid cargo selection and coordinated osteogenic and angiogenic gene delivery, including pDNA, mRNA, siRNA, miRNA, and explores emerging multi-factor, stimuli-responsive, and CRISPR-based GAMs alongside their translational constraints. A distinct feature of this review is its claim-level patent analysis, which identifies substantial intellectual-property white space in GAM development. Despite strong preclinical evidence, no GAM platform has simultaneously achieved scalable manufacturing, regulatory readiness as a combination product, and validation in a human-scale bone defect model. Clinical translation will require coordinated optimization of vector-scaffold interactions, manufacturing scalability, safety, and clinically relevant validation.

works.title: Brain-penetrating and lesion-triggered hydrogen sulfide nanocarrier for multiple pathogenic interventions in Parkinson's disease therapy
works.abstract: : The defective hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) metabolism in brain has emerged as a crucial pathogenic event and therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease (PD). However, current H 2 S delivery approaches for PD remain predominantly limited by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and on-demand supply. This work aimed to upgrade the delivery of H 2 S to across BBB, thereby adequately harnessing its neuroprotective effect in PD brain. We developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-triggered H 2 S nanocarrier with brain-penetrating capability (RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY) for targeted H 2 S delivery in PD brain. In this system, the H 2 S donor GYY4137 was assembled by a ROS-responsive thioketal linker (TK), while the surface is modified with the brain-homing peptide RVG29. Notably, this formulation achieved a good BBB penetration rate of 22.1%. In addition, pathological evaluation results demonstrated that the controlled H 2 S release by RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY can exert multiple PD pathogenic interventions, including scavenging excessive ROS, alleviating nitrative stress, decreasing nerve cells apoptosis, reducing glial cell activation and promoting nerve regeneration. Critically, RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY treatment significantly attenuated the motor deficits of PD model mice. Collectively, this study not only provide a H 2 S-nanocarrier for PD multiple pathological therapy, but also contributing to the development of H 2 S delivery in other neurodegenerative diseases treatment.

works.title: A Biomimetic Microneedle Platform Using Neutrophil Membrane for Synergistic Antibacterial Therapy of MRSA Infection
works.abstract: Persistent bacterial infection has become life-threatening challenge worldwide. Bacterial biofilm formation, causing induced antimicrobial resistance and suppressive immune microenvironment, is one of the critical pathways leading chronic and persistent infection. Herein, an integrated microneedle patch harboring neutrophil membrane and antibiotics is designed to elicit therapeutic in-situ immunization for the management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection. When applied on the infected skin, microneedles can physically penetrate the biofilm barrier, helping the diffusion of antibiotics to kill the bacteria deep in the biofilm. After breaking the integrated structure of biofilm, neutrophil membrane tightly binds to the bacterial debris to enhance the phagocytosis of antigen-presenting cells followed by the robust activation of T helper cells. Naïve B cells then differentiate to plasma cells or memory B cells to produce specific antibodies, thereby efficiently managing infection and preventing relapse. Overall, our study highlights the capability of eliciting therapeutic in-situ immunization mediated by the integrated biomimetic microneedle, providing an attractive perspective for the treatment of persistent bacterial infection.

works.title: Nanobody‐Modified Outer Membrane Vesicles Attenuate Alzheimer's Disease‐Like Neurodegeneration by Modulating Mitophagy‐Associated Phenotypes and cGAS‐STING‐Related Inflammatory Signaling
works.abstract: This study examined anti-transferrin receptor (TfR) nanobody-functionalized bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) as an engineered platform for improving Alzheimer's disease (AD)-like neuronal injury. Escherichia coli-derived OMVs were characterized for morphology, size distribution, surface charge, protein features, nanobody loading, residual endotoxin levels, endotoxin-associated inflammatory responses, and repeated-exposure immune-safety readouts, and were evaluated in neuronal-related cells and APP/PS1 mice. Engineered OMVs showed receptor-associated uptake and preferential brain-delivery signals, increased HT-22 cell viability, reduced apoptosis, and elevated mitophagy-associated markers including LC3-II, PINK1, and Parkin. OMV treatment also reduced cytosolic mtDNA abundance, DNA/cGAS colocalization, phosphorylation of STING/TBK1/IRF3, and inflammatory-marker expression. PINK1 or Parkin knockdown partially weakened OMV-associated mitochondrial and inflammatory readouts, whereas pharmacological autophagy modulation supported a contribution of autophagy-related processes without establishing selective PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy in vivo. In APP/PS1 mice, OMV administration improved Morris water maze and rotarod performance and alleviated neuroinflammatory and histological injury-related changes. Overall, anti-TfR nanobody-modified OMVs were associated with enhanced receptor-related delivery, mitophagy-linked phenotypes, reduced cytosolic mtDNA/cGAS-STING-related inflammatory signaling, and improved AD-like outcomes, supporting further delivery-system optimization and mechanistic validation.

works.title: Biocompatible Conjugated Electrospinning Nanofibrous Membrane With Self‐Powered Piezoelectric Capacity for Accelerated Wound Healing
works.abstract: Extensive research has demonstrated that electrical stimulation (ES) accelerates wound healing by promoting cellular proliferation and migration. However, the delivery of continuous and noninvasive ES to the wound site remains a major challenge. Conventional ES devices generally depend on external power supplies and often suffer from limited biocompatibility. To address these limitations, we developed an innovative wound healing strategy that integrates ES with biocompatible materials. Specifically, a self-powered nanofibrous membrane (PGPM) was fabricated via conjugated electrospinning by combining the piezoelectric polymer poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (PVDF-TrFE) and MXene with polycaprolactone (PCL) and gelatin, two polymers with excellent biocompatibility. The resulting PGPM has inherent piezoelectric properties allowing the generation of localized electrical signals in response to mechanical stimuli, for example, skin tension, compression or ultrasound. These electrical signals significantly promote the growth and migration of wound healing-related cells, as well as the deposition of type I/III collagen fibers, α-SMA expression, and VEGF production in vivo. Together, such an approach has offered a self-powered and biocompatible platform on which wound healing can be accelerated using endogenous ES.

works.title: Small‐Pore Chitosan Microcarriers Support Surface‐Adherent Growth of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell–Derived Neural Stem Cells and Improve Intranasal Therapy of Murine Anosmia
works.abstract: Intranasal delivery of neural stem cells offers a non-invasive strategy for central nervous system repair, yet its efficacy is limited by rapid mucociliary clearance and poor cellular retention. Although chitosan-based carriers have been explored, the architectural principles governing neural stem cell behavior in the intranasal microenvironment remain poorly defined. We compared chitosan microcarriers (CSMs) with three pore architectures (mean surface pore sizes 4.7 ± 1.7, 15.9 ± 3.2, and 20.5 ± 0.7 µm), fabricated via freezing-controlled phase separation, using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neural stem cells (iPSC-NSCs). Cellular responses did not vary linearly with pore size: the smallest-pore formulation, CSM-196, supported surface-adhesion-dominant growth, whereas both larger-pore formulations supported infiltration-dominant growth. CSM-196 was also associated with increased proliferative activity, spontaneous neuronal differentiation, and elevated neurotrophic factor secretion without exogenous induction factors. In a methimazole-induced anosmia model, the CSM-196-iPSC-NSC formulation produced greater improvements in olfactory behavioral recovery, olfactory epithelial thickness, neuronal marker expression, and epithelial proliferation than cell-only delivery administered by the same route and schedule. This chitosan-based platform provides a surface-adhesion-oriented cell-delivery strategy that warrants further evaluation for intranasal neural regenerative therapy.

A fibrochondrogenic polymer fibre-reinforced collagen-based scaffold with graded architecture, mechanics and composition for meniscus repair
works.abstract: Developing biomaterials for meniscal repair that reproduce native tissue biomechanics while providing pro-regenerative bioinstructive cues remains challenging. To address this need, we developed a zonal biomimetic fibre-reinforced collagen-based scaffold designed to recreate key microstructural and mechanical features of the meniscus and support fibrochondrogenesis in vitro. A multilayer scaffold was fabricated with a circumferential electrospun (ES) fibre core composed of polycaprolactone (PCL), polylactic acid (PLA), or a hybrid PCL/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/PLA reinforcement, together with radially oriented melt-electrowritten (MEW) PCL intermediate zones and multidirectional MEW PCL superficial zones, followed by integration with a collagen I-chondroitin-6-sulfate matrix. Fibre-reinforced scaffolds combining MEW PCL with the hybrid ES PCL-PVA-PLA reinforcement framework demonstrated the best-balanced biomechanical performance, achieving mechanical properties within the range reported for native meniscus under comparable test conditions, including tensile, compressive and complex moduli of 140.62 ± 26.31 MPa, 723.21 ± 147.09 kPa and 25.91 ± 1.21 kPa, respectively. Moreover, human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells cultured on this scaffold exhibited enhanced sulfated glycosaminoglycan production, balanced type I and type II collagen expression, and fibrocartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition with the reinforced architecture supporting deeper and more uniform matrix formation. Together, these findings support zonal fibre reinforcement as a design strategy to integrate mechanical fidelity with scaffold-dependent modulation of hMSC fibrochondrogenesis in vitro, identifying the hybrid PCL-PVA-PLA-reinforced scaffold as a best-balanced configuration for meniscal repair.

works.title: Robotic winding of wet-spun fibers for biofabrication of aligned, perfusable, muscle-based tissue
works.abstract: Structural alignment of muscle and integrated vasculature enables the function of geometrically complex tissues in the body, such as the gastroesophageal junction and the ventricles. However, replicating this complexity is an ongoing challenge. Described here is the wet-spun & robotically articulated placement (WRAP) method for deposition of aligned cellular fibers on scaffolds, resulting in large structures fabricated from the inside-out. WRAP enables complex, multi-oriented muscle and vascular placement by creating a continuous cellular fiber through wet spinning, and then using a robotic arm programmed with a set of tissue profiles to maneuver the fiber around an organ scaffold. Wet-spun fibers, consisting of muscle cells combined with endothelial cell fibers via double-core spinning, exhibited the ability to mature, align, contract, and initiate tubulogenesis, creating perfusable fibers. Further, the robotic arm could accurately create physiologically relevant fiber patterns with high precision. The potential to generate perfusable blood vessels alongside functional muscle is paramount to fabricating muscle-based constructs. The WRAP method offers a high throughput and versatile solution to the scale-up problem plaguing the biofabrication of muscle-based tissues.

works.title: Scaffold-free self-assembled cell ring organoids enable efficient tumor modeling with high engraftment rates, superior tumor uniformity, and reduced animal consumption
works.abstract: Background Conventional tumor cell suspension xenografts suffer from low engraftment efficiency, prolonged latency, and poor tumor uniformity, with high animal consumption conflicting with the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement). This study aimed to develop a scaffold-free self-assembled cell ring organoid platform to address these bottlenecks. Methods Tumor cells and fibroblasts were mixed at optimized ratios and seeded into microwell molds, spontaneously self-assembling into ring-shaped organoids within 24–48 h without exogenous matrices or hydrogels. In vitro characterization included live/dead staining, histology, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, Western blotting, and transcriptomic sequencing. In vivo performance was evaluated by orthotopic transplantation into the lateral femoral condyle of immunodeficient or immunocompetent mice, with longitudinal monitoring by bioluminescence imaging and micro-CT. Results Cell rings maintained high viability during in vitro culture and were compatible with both cell lines and clinical primary sarcoma cells. Immunofluorescence and Western blotting revealed that co-cultured fibroblasts underwent cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-like phenotypic transformation (α-SMA upregulation) within the cell ring organoids. Transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that the gene expression profiles of cell ring organoids closely resembled those of original tumors, whereas 2D-cultured cells showed the greatest number and magnitude of differentially expressed genes. In vivo , cell ring organoids achieved higher engraftment rates, better tumor uniformity, and stronger bone invasion capacity compared with cell suspensions. Conclusion The scaffold-free self-assembled cell ring organoids platform provides an efficient, uniform, and 3R-compliant strategy for animal tumor modeling. Without requiring exogenous matrices, this technology achieves significantly higher engraftment rates and tumor uniformity compared with conventional methods, effectively reduces animal consumption, and may offer a potential platform for future preclinical drug screening and tumor microenvironment (TME) research.

works.title: Multifunctional bio-derived hydrogel loaded with ADSCs for promoting diabetic wound healing
works.abstract: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) hold substantial therapeutic potential for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs). However, their efficacy is often limited by poor survival within the harsh microenvironment of chronic wounds. In this study, we developed a multifunctional bio-derived hydrogel composed of gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and ferrous ions (Fe 2+ ) that integrates ADSCs with local microenvironment modulation. This approach targets key pathological challenges in DFUs treatment, including persistent inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and oxidative stress. The hydrogel demonstrated potent antibacterial, antioxidant, and pro-angiogenic activities. Moreover, it significantly accelerated diabetic wound healing, enhanced re-epithelialization and collagen deposition, and promoted macrophage polarization toward the reparative M2 phenotype, thereby effectively improving the wound microenvironment. These results indicate that the GelMA/GA/Fe@ADSCs hydrogel is a promising regenerative therapy with strong translational potential for DFUs and other chronic wounds.

works.title: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles delivering CERS1 promote squamous differentiation in HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia via remodeling sphingomyelin metabolism
works.abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), a precursor of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven cervical cancer, poses a severe threat to women's health. High-risk HPV infection drives CIN progression, whereas well-defined intervention targets and effective non-invasive therapies remain lacking. Herein, Using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), specifically HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids as a human-relevant disease model, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of engineered cell-free small extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSC-sEV). We found that hucMSC-sEV significantly promoted squamous differentiation in S12 cells and HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids. Mechanistically, integrated multi-omics analyses within this NAMs platform revealed that hucMSC-sEV delivered ceramide synthase 1 (CERS1) to upregulate C18 ceramide (C18 Cer) synthesis, activating the non-canonical p53 signaling to drive squamous differentiation. In NCG mice bearing subcutaneous xenografts of S12 cells, hucMSC-sEV effectively inhibited S12 xenograft growth and modulated squamous differentiation via regulation of C18 ceramide metabolism, while this therapeutic effect was abrogated in CERS1-knockdown hucMSC-sEV. This study delineates the molecular mechanism by which hucMSC-sEV remodel sphingolipid metabolism to promote cervical squamous epithelial differentiation and suppress S12 xenograft development, providing novel potential targets and therapeutic strategies for CIN intervention.

Emergent directional persistence in fibrous granular scaffolds guides myotube organization
works.abstract: Granular scaffolds have emerged as promising platforms for tissue regeneration, offering injectability and cell-scale porosity that support robust cell infiltration and tissue formation. However, the isotropic pore structure of spherical building blocks does not provide the directional cues needed to guide organized tissue formation. Addressing this requires asking not just whether granular scaffolds can be made anisotropic, but whether directional cues persist across the pore network at scales relevant to cell behavior. We first demonstrate that spherical granular materials lose orientational coherence at the cellular scale, confirming that isotropic building blocks are fundamentally incapable of providing structural guidance beyond individual pore neighborhoods. In contrast, using high aspect ratio GelMA hydrogel fibers as building blocks extends persistence into the multicellular range, occupying an intermediate architectural regime akin to many tissues between simple isotropic or uniaxial alignment previously inaccessible to granular scaffold design. We show this regime is functionally meaningful; myotubes undergo contact guidance through locally persistent but globally variable pore structure, and greater persistence is associated with increased myotube elongation and multinucleation in primary human muscle progenitor cells. Together these results expand the design space for granular scaffolds beyond pore size and porosity, and establish persistence as a variable linking granular scaffold architecture to organized tissue formation. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Granular scaffolds composed of spherical building blocks have emerged as promising platforms for tissue regeneration, however their uniform pore structure does not provide the directional cues needed to guide organized tissue formation. To address this limitation, we fabricated high aspect ratio hydrogel fibers as granular scaffold building blocks where larger fibers resulted in pores with greater orientational coherence, or persistence. We then showed that persistence is functionally meaningful with myotubes showing increased elongation and multinucleation in granular scaffolds with increased persistence. Together these results expand the design space for granular scaffolds beyond pore size and porosity, and establish persistence as a variable linking granular scaffold architecture to organized tissue formation.

works.title: Magnetically Actuated 3D Constructs Direct Strain Gradient-Induced Migration in Breast Cancer Metastasis Models
Glycosaminoglycan-Induced Macrophage Reprogramming Orchestrates Pro-Regenerative Crosstalk with Fibroblasts
works.abstract: Macrophages and fibroblasts play central roles in coordinating inflammation and tissue repair, whilst dysregulation of macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk drives pathological outcomes such as chronic inflammation and fibrosis. Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), key components of the extracellular matrix (ECM), interact with cytokines and growth factors that modulate macrophage polarisation and direct fibroblast activity, making them attractive candidates for developing immune-instructive biomaterials. However, the optimal GAG compositions that promote macrophage-mediated repair and fibroblast-driven ECM remodelling remain unclear. Here, we report an unbiased screening of 82 surface-adsorbed GAG combinations to identify candidates capable of modulating macrophage-fibroblast interactions. Leveraging cytokine profiling, surface marker immunostaining, gene expression, principal component analysis (PCA), and hierarchical clustering, we identified 'hit' GAG combinations that induced distinct, non-canonical macrophage activation programmes characterised by coordinated inflammatory and regulatory signalling, alongside enhanced fibroblast proliferation. Shortlisted formulations were validated using expanded biological replication, orthogonal phenotypic, transcriptional and functional analyses, assessment in macrophage-fibroblast co-culture systems, and in an in vivo diabetic wound model. These data demonstrated that 'hit' GAG formulations modulated macrophage functional activation states, promoted collagen and ECM synthesis, facilitated vascular and lymphatic vessel formation, and accelerated wound closure. Complementary metabolomic profiling using OrbiSIMS and molecular formula prediction (MFP), revealed macrophage metabolic reprogramming as a potential mechanism underlying these pro-healing effects. Collectively, this study established an unbiased methodology for discovering immune-instructive GAGs in supporting pro-healing responses for potential wound-healing applications. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are key extracellular matrix components with significant potential to regulate immune responses. However, their immunomodulatory effects are highly context-dependent, varying with sulfation pattern, molecular composition, and the local microenvironment, making it challenging to identify GAG combinations that consistently promote pro-regenerative immune responses and tissue repair. Here, we developed an unbiased combinatorial screening platform to systematically identify GAG combinations that reprogram macrophages toward pro-regenerative functional states. The selected GAG combinations enhanced macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk in vitro and improved diabetic wound healing in vivo by promoting collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and lymphatic remodelling. OrbiSIMS metabolomics further revealed macrophage metabolic reprogramming associated with these regenerative responses. This work establishes a generalizable discovery framework for identifying immune-regulatory GAG formulations and provides new design principles for developing extracellular matrix-inspired immunomodulatory biomaterials for regenerative medicine.

works.title: Corrigendum to “Spatiotemporal self-reinforcing hydrogel spray with antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties for accelerated diabetic wound healing” [Acta Biomaterialia 202 (2025) 193-204]
Research platforms and recent advances of mechanoimmunology
works.abstract: Unlike most tissue-resident cells that inhabit relatively homeostatic mechanical microenvironments, immune cells encounter diverse mechanical cues as they circulate throughout the body and transmigrate across tissue barriers. Mechanical stimuli have emerged as fundamental upstream regulators of both innate and adaptive immune responses. Mechanotransduction processes governed by core biomechanical sensors and effectors, including Piezo1, TRPV4, and YAP/TAZ, have recently attracted escalating research attention across immunological and mechanobiological fields. Notably, cellular mechanosensing is intrinsically context-dependent, shaped by the interplay between local mechanical properties and biochemical cues within tissue microenvironments. As a result, mechanoregulated immune phenotypes and functional outputs are highly sensitive to the experimental configurations of preclinical models. In contrast to previous reviews that mainly outline mechanotransduction signaling cascades, this review systematically categorizes prevalent biomechanical research platforms, detailing their technical specifications and key parametric characteristics, while contextualizing the mechanical regulation of immune behaviors within specific experimental frameworks. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Mechanoimmunology has revealed that mechanical forces are fundamental regulators of immune cell function, yet the field is plagued by contradictory findings arising from inconsistent platform parameterization. This review provides the first systematic classification of five major biomechanical research platforms - 2D hydrogel systems, 3D matrix models, microfluidic devices, single-molecule force spectroscopy, and in vivo genetic models - detailing their technical specifications, parametric boundaries, and experimental contexts. By anchoring immune mechanobiological conclusions to specific platform parameters, we establish a framework for resolving apparent phenotypic contradictions and standardizing cross-study comparisons. This context-aware approach directly informs the rational design of immunomodulatory biomaterials with tunable mechanical properties, bridging biomaterials engineering and immune cell biology for applications in tissue repair, cancer immunotherapy, and regenerative medicine.
