Interplays Between Therapeutic Radiopharmaceuticals and Tumor Microenvironment
works.abstract: Radiopharmaceuticals have progressed from diagnostic agents toward theranostic. With the accelerating development of therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals, radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) is being increasingly implemented in clinical practice in oncology. However, current therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals often contribute to tumor stabilization rather than complete remission. A major determinant of this limited clinical response is the tumor microenvironment (TME), which critically influences the delivery, penetration, and retention of radiopharmaceuticals. Meanwhile, the radiopharmaceuticals can modulate multiple components of the TME, thereby contributing to antitumor effects. These interactions provide opportunities for advancing radiopharmaceuticals to enhance RPT efficacy. In this review, the bidirectional relationship between therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals and TME in solid malignancies is comprehensively discussed. First, common therapeutic strategies that modulate TME are outlined. The impact of the TME on radiopharmaceutical efficacies and how radiopharmaceuticals reshape the TME are then highlighted. In addition to elucidating the bidirectional interplay between RPT and the TME, we examine two fundamental clinical barriers that constrain RPT efficacy: dosimetric limitations and systemic immune collateral damage. Finally, critical challenges and potential strategies to enhance next-generation therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals in solid malignancies are inspected.

works.title: Biodegradable Monometallic Manganese Nanoparticles for Multimodal Tumor Therapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Synergistic therapeutic nanoplatforms are of considerable interest in tumor therapy, but their translational potential is often limited by complex multicomponent designs and unknown in vivo degradation behavior. Herein, we show a degradable, single‐component manganese nanoparticles (Mn NPs) using liquid‐phase exfoliation of commercial bulk manganese powder for cancer therapy. In the acidic tumor environment, Mn NPs react with H + to generate Mn 2+ and H 2 and raise the local pH. The released Mn 2+ drives Fenton‐like reactions to produce ROS, while H 2 causes mitochondrial damage, which together lead to tumor cell death. In addition, Mn 2+ activates cGAS‐STING signaling and initiates antitumor immunity. Moreover, Mn NPs inhibit tumor growth in CT26, 4T1, and B16F10 mouse models and show better effects than Mn 2+ alone. Transcriptomic analysis further reveals activation of multiple immune‐related signaling pathways following Mn NP treatment. In a bilateral tumor model, unilateral injection of Mn NPs triggers a systemic antitumor immune response, leading to effective inhibition of distant, untreated tumor growth. Collectively, this study identifies Mn NPs as a simple, biodegradable, single‐component nanoplatform that offers a promising new route for multimodal tumor therapy.

works.title: Rutin‐Coated Ultrasmall Gadolinium Oxide Nanoparticles with High T1 Relaxivity for MRI of Blood Vessels and Glucose Transporter‐Overexpressing Malignant Tumors
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The straightforward one‐step wet‐chemical approach represents a promising strategy for the preparation of ultrasmall gadolinium oxide nanoparticles (GdONs) featuring high T 1 relaxivity and excellent aqueous dispersion stability. However, achieving specificity for conventional GdONs still requires multi‐step modifications with targeting molecules, introducing uncertainty into their application prospects. Herein, rutin (Ru)‐coated ultrasmall GdONs (Gd@Ru) possessing both high T 1 relaxivity and glucose transporter (GLUT)‐overexpressing tumor‐targeted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) capability were successfully prepared via a one‐step wet‐chemical method. Among all the as‐prepared Gd@Ru, Gd@Ru‐5 with the lowest Gd content (∼3.8 wt% Gd, as determined by EDS) exhibits the smallest crystalline size (∼ 1.8 nm) and hydrodynamic diameter (∼ 4.0 nm), achieving the highest T 1 relaxivity (40.4 mM − 1 s − 1 at 1.5 T) along with exceptional stability. Moreover, Gd@Ru‐5 showed satisfactory biosafety and excellent magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) performance in SD rats and New Zealand rabbits, as well as effective targeted imaging of GLUT‐overexpressing 4T1 breast tumors. Overall, we present a facile one‐step wet‐chemical strategy for fabricating ultrasmall GdONs that integrate high T 1 relaxivity, excellent MRA performance, and tumor‐targeted MRI capability.

works.title: Stiff Extracellular Matrix Rejuvenates Aged Mesenchymal Stem Cells via PI3K‐AKT Signaling
works.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are widely used to modulate immune responses and promote tissue regeneration, but cellular senescence significantly impairs their therapeutic potential. MSCs undergo senescence characterized by an enlarged morphology, reduced proliferative capacity, and altered expression of genes related to the cytoskeleton. This study revealed that the mechanical microenvironment critically regulates MSC aging. Culturing senescent MSCs on high-stiffness extracellular matrix (ECM) hydrogels reverses key aspects of the senescent phenotype, including the restoration of normal morphology, improved cytoskeletal integrity, and enhanced proliferation. This mechanical rescue is accompanied by genetic reprogramming and activation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway. The inhibition of PI3K-Akt with LY294002 abolished these rejuvenating effects. These findings demonstrate that the mechanical microenvironment can reprogram senescent MSCs through PI3K-AKT-mediated mechanotransduction, offering a novel strategy to restore stem cell function in aging and regenerative medicine.

works.title: Microfluidic Nano‐Assembly of Red‐Blood‐Cell (RBC) Lipids and Components for Engineering Extracellular Vesicles (Adv. Healthcare Mater. 41/2026)
works.abstract: Red Blood Cell Lipids The cover illustrates the microfluidic production of engineered red blood cell extracellular vesicle (eRBCEVs) from RBC lipids. The central vesicle encapsulates adeno-associated virus (AAV), highlighting efficient viral loading and immune-evasive delivery. The fluorescent cellular background represents successful eGFP-AAV9 transduction of HEK293T cells despite the presence of neutralizing AAV9 antibodies. More details can be found in the Research Article by Eduardo Reátegui, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adhm.202504351).

works.title: A Non‐Cryogenic Dugout‐Structured Microneedle Patch for Co‐Delivery of Irisin and Fibroblasts in Diabetic Wound Repair (Adv. Healthcare Mater. 41/2026)
works.abstract: Cell-Delivery Microneedles A dugout-structured microneedle patch carries live fibroblasts together with irisin. A portable vacuum pump draws the cell-laden alginate into three internal microchannels within minutes, so no freezing or cryoprotectants are needed. Pressed onto a diabetic wound, the patch releases both payloads beneath the surface, lowering TNF-α, raising fibronectin and TGF-β1, and closing wounds faster than topical treatment. More details can be found in the Research Article by Shu-Hung Huang, Hung-Wei Yang, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adhm.71598).

works.title: Issue Information: Adv. Healthcare Mater. 41/2026
Polymeric Biomaterials with Multiple Stratified Layers for Periodontal Ligament/Bone Regeneration: A Review
works.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic pathological condition initiated by bacterial plaque accumulation and characterized by the progressive destruction of the tooth-supporting tissues, including the periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone. If left untreated, it may result in tooth mobility, pathologic tooth migration, and ultimately tooth loss. Despite numerous regenerative strategies, complete periodontal regeneration remains challenging. Guided tissue regeneration (GTR) and guided bone regeneration (GBR) promote the regeneration of the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone; however, current GTR/GBR biomaterials often exhibit inadequate mechanical stability and osseointegration. To overcome these limitations, various multilayer biomaterials with enhanced functionalities have been developed. This review outlines the key properties required for GTR/GBR, evaluates the design and performance of current multilayer biomaterials, and examines their major limitations, particularly their inability to fully replicate native periodontal tissues due to structural incompatibilities between layers. Finally, future directions and recommendations are presented to guide the development of next-generation GTR/GBR biomaterials.

works.title: Durable and reversible epigenetic programming of human hematopoietic stem cells as a platform for modulation of platelet function
works.abstract: Programmable epigenome editing offers control of gene expression without altering DNA sequence, but its capacity to program human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and their differentiated progeny remains incompletely characterized. Here, we establish that DNA methylation-based epigenome editors delivered transiently as RNA induce heritable gene silencing in primary human HSCs. Targeting the platelet integrin β3 (ITGB3) produced silencing that persisted through long-term HSC self-renewal and megakaryocytic differentiation, impaired aggregation of in vitro-derived platelets, and was partially reversed through targeted demethylation at this locus. Silencing remained stable in human HSCs 4 months after transplantation into mice. Targeting additional platelet-associated genes demonstrated broad applicability with this approach. Together, these findings establish DNA methylation-based epigenome editing as a platform for durable and reversible programming of human HSCs and demonstrate its application to modulating platelet function.

works.title: Epiblast complementation enables generation of live offspring from pluripotent stem cells
Perivascular macrophages restrict CXCR4-dependent accumulation of stem-like CD8+ T cells in tumors and limit chemotherapy efficacy
works.abstract: The perivascular (Pv) niche coordinates immune-stromal interactions that facilitate cancer progression. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic inactivation of the enzyme heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) in LYVE-1 + Pv tumor-associated macrophages (PvTAMs) synergizes with cytotoxic chemotherapy (CCT) to achieve immunological tumor control in murine breast cancer models. We investigated the tumor microenvironment (TME) during the transition to immunological control and identified an increase in stem-like TCF1 + PD-1 + CD8 + T cells and enrichment of tumor-selective effector T cells. Stem-like CD8 + T cells were clonally diverse and rapidly acquired a TCF1 − differentiated phenotype in the TME. Their tumor accumulation depended on CXCR4 and was associated with a treatment-induced expansion of proliferating CXCL12 + CD34 + Pv cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). In human breast cancer, greater abundance of the stem-like CD8 + T cell program was associated with improved outcomes following CCT. These findings identify PvTAM HO-1 activity as a regulator of a stromal-stem-like T cell axis that limits chemotherapy efficacy and anti-tumor immunity.

Neural interface instructs layer 4-appropriate circuit reconstruction with engrafted human brain organoids and improves visually guided behavior
works.abstract: Repairing precise neural microcircuitry after cortical injury remains a pivotal challenge. Human brain organoids (hBOs) are a promising cell source, but disorganized integration limits their therapeutic potential. Here, we demonstrated that targeted neuromodulation, steered by endogenous narrowband gamma (NBG) rhythms, instructed structural and functional integration of hBO grafts in the injured adult mouse visual cortex. Using a neural interface system, we promoted general graft-host coupling and then delivered NBG-rhythmic stimulation to specific functional clusters. This strategy guided the emergence of layer 4-appropriate molecular and functional properties in grafts, enabled bidirectional connectivity with the host visual circuit, and supported the development of advanced visual processing, including direction selectivity in hBO neurons. Electrophysiologically, graft spiking phase locked to host NBG oscillations. Behaviorally, host visual acuity and contrast sensitivity were significantly restored. Our work established a framework for circuit-level repair, highlighting a synergistic strategy that moves beyond cell replacement to direct the assembly of neural grafts.

works.title: Shared molecular regulation of quiescence in neural and glioma stem cells reveals therapeutic vulnerabilities
works.abstract: Quiescent glioma cells evade chemoradiation and drive glioblastoma recurrence by reactivating to repopulate the tumor, but are hard to study due to their rarity and difficulty maintaining quiescence in vitro . We hypothesized that quiescence programs conserved between neural stem cells and glioma cells could be exploited to lock glioma cells in quiescence and prevent reactivation. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and patient-derived glioma stem cell lines, we found that although glioma cells resist entering deep quiescence, they share conserved activation trajectories with neural stem cells. Because this conservation lets a tractable neural progenitor line act as a surrogate for rare quiescent glioma cells, we queried LINCS L1000 signatures across >3,000 compounds and validated the top classes (mTOR, ATPase, and histone lysine methyltransferase inhibitors) as quiescence promoters in glioma stem cell lines. By establishing conserved activation programs and enabling cross-cell-type screening, our work provides a strategy for driving therapy-resistant glioma cells into quiescence.

works.title: Peroxisome dysfunction disrupts metabolism of photoreceptor outer segments in human retinal pigment epithelium
works.abstract: Peroxisomes are ubiquitous organelles that compartmentalize metabolic reactions including lipid catabolism and cellular detoxification. Pathogenic variants in PEX1 and PEX6 disrupt essential peroxisome functions and cause profound neurodegenerative diseases called peroxisome biogenesis disorders (PBDs). Despite retinal degeneration and blindness occurring frequently in PBDs, precisely how impaired peroxisome activity disrupts retinal function remains to be fully explored. To address this, we differentiated PEX1-/-, PEX6-/-, and wildtype human induced pluripotent stem cells into retinal pigment epithelium (iRPE) to study the consequences of peroxisome dysfunction in this disease-relevant cell type. Despite exhibiting impaired peroxisome matrix protein import, PEX1-/- and PEX6-/- iRPE had comparable morphology, tight junctions, and expression of proteins characteristic of RPE compared to wildtype iRPE. Targeted lipid profiling revealed reduced docosahexaenoic acid, a polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) essential for retinal function, and elevated lipid species exclusively metabolized by peroxisomes in PEX1-/- and PEX6-/- iRPE. Following a photoreceptor outer segment (POS) challenge, PEX1-/- and PEX6-/- iRPE demonstrated disrupted PUFA retroconversion and lipid droplet accumulation. Additionally, PEX1-/- and PEX6-/- iRPE had impaired rhodopsin degradation, lysosomal dysfunction, and reduced transepithelial electrical resistance. These findings suggest that dysregulated POS metabolism in the RPE is a potential mechanism driving retinal degeneration in patients with PBDs.

works.title: Diet-induced chromatin states influence intestinal stem cell behavior
works.abstract: SUMMARY Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) integrate dietary cues through a metabolic–transcriptional axis, but whether these mechanisms create a lasting epigenetic memory remains unclear. Here, we investigate diet-induced chromatin adaptations in ISCs using a high-fat Western diet (HFD) mouse model. HFD broadly remodels chromatin accessibility, altering pre-existing open regulatory regions. Many differentially accessible regions (DARs) persist during the differentiation of ISCs into transient amplifying cells (TACs). Notably, HFD-induced DARs are retained following diet normalization despite phenotypic reversibility, and HFD re-exposure enhances ISC self-renewal and adenoma growth compared with naïve HFD exposure. The HFD-induced chromatin changes require Ppar-d/a nuclear receptors but are independent of their transcriptional targets. Although a subset of HFD-induced DARs is maintained following Apc loss, extensive chromatin remodeling driven by tumor suppressor inactivation largely overrides diet-dependent differences in Lgr5 ⁺ ISCs. Together, these findings demonstrate that ISCs retain a chromatin-based memory of dietary fat exposure.

works.title: mGluR6 is required for cone terminal targeting and synaptic layer assembly during human retinal development
works.abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptor 6 (mGluR6), encoded by GRM6 , is a core component of the ON-bipolar signaling cascade in the retina, but its role in human retinal development remains unclear. Here, we used temporally controlled CRISPR-based genetic ablation in human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal organoids to define the developmental functions of mGluR6. Unexpectedly, we found that mGluR6 is expressed not only in ON-bipolar cells but also transiently in cone photoreceptors during human retinal development, a pattern not observed in the mouse retina. Early loss of GRM6 before synaptogenesis disrupted cone pedicle architecture, leading to mislocalization of synaptic proteins including Bassoon, ELFN2, and TRPM1, and ultimately resulting in widening or duplication of the outer plexiform layer. In contrast, deletion after synapse formation did not alter retinal architecture. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized, temporally restricted role for mGluR6 in cone terminal targeting and synaptic layer assembly during human retinal development.

works.title: Optimized feeder-dependent culture enables efficient hypothalamic-pituitary organoid induction from human pluripotent stem cells
works.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived hypothalamus-pituitary organoids recapitulate key processes of pituitary development in vitro, where cellular interactions between hypothalamic and oral ectodermal lineages are essential for organoid formation. However, how maintenance culture conditions for hPSCs influence the processes of lineage specification remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that feeder-dependent culture conditions critically determine lineage specification during organoid formation. hPSCs maintained on SNL feeders preferentially differentiated into oral ectodermal cells, whereas maintenance on MEF feeders favored hypothalamic lineages. Co-culturing SNL- and MEF-maintained hPSCs or combining their conditioned media effectively balanced these lineages, enhancing pituitary induction efficiency. Furthermore, a stabilized FGF2 mutant enabled a "weekend-free" protocol that reduced labor and cost while maintaining high differentiation efficiency. Our findings underscore the significance of maintenance conditions and hypothalamus-oral ectoderm interactions in pituitary development, establishing a robust platform for efficient and reproducible generation of hypothalamus-pituitary organoids.

works.title: Secondary bile acids disrupt hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis
works.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis caused by a high-fat diet disrupts hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify gut microbial secondary bile acid deoxycholic acid (DCA) as a key mediator of HSC dysfunction in mice. Plasma DCA levels were elevated during aging, consistent with previously reported increases in high-fat diet-fed mice. Chronic DCA administration upregulated Spred1 in mouse HSCs, as also observed during aging, contributing to HSC loss. DCA treatment in Spred1-deficient mice triggered myeloproliferative neoplasm-like disease, highlighting Spred1's role in mediating a trade-off between HSC aging and tumor suppression. Unexpectedly, DCA-counteracting ursodeoxycholic acid also promoted age-associated expansion of myeloid-biased mouse HSCs. In contrast, a high-fiber diet lowered plasma DCA levels and mitigated aging-associated HSC decline. Our findings reveal that systemic gut microbial metabolites, particularly secondary bile acids, critically affect HSC fate, and suggest that dietary interventions targeting the gut microbiota can regulate hematopoietic homeostasis.

works.title: Endothelial fate mapping reveals spatiotemporal restriction in yolk sac-derived innate lymphoid cells
works.abstract: While the development of bone marrow hematopoietic stem cell-dependent innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) in mice is well elucidated, their earliest embryonic production site remains to be investigated. Our study identifies a spatiotemporally restricted contribution of yolk sac-derived hematopoiesis to ILC development. Using inducible lineage tracing and single-cell transcriptomics, we demonstrate that yolk sac-derived progenitors generate ILCs that arise in early embryogenesis and are selectively specified in the fetal small intestine. Although these cells are detectable across multiple fetal organs, the activation of ILC-specific transcriptional programs is confined exclusively to the intestinal environment. This contribution to ILC development is temporal, diminishing rapidly after birth, and is restricted to a narrow developmental window. These findings provide new insights into the temporal and spatial regulation of early hematopoietic contributions to the ILC lineage, revealing an unappreciated role for yolk sac-derived progenitors in shaping the early stages of ILC development.

works.title: What impact has iPSC technology had on your research and/or field?
works.abstract: In our field, induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology removed the final barrier between pioneering retinal stem cell research and clinical application. We had previously been the first to generate retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells from primate ES cells and to demonstrate their therapeutic efficacy in animal models. However, because the target diseases mainly affect elderly patients, we were deeply concerned that using allogeneic cells with systemic immunosuppression could create unacceptable clinical risks.

works.title: Temporal changes in subcellular localization of synaptic proteins in human inner ear organoids recapitulate ribbon synapse development
A scaffold-free rotary culture system enables scalable production of functionally convergent perinatal MSC spheroids with enhanced pro-regenerative potency
works.abstract: Mesenchymal stromal cell spheroids (MSC sp ) represent promising bioactive constructs for regenerative medicine; however, scalable scaffold-free approaches for generating functionally enhanced and consistent MSC sp across different tissue sources remain limited. Here, we evaluated a rotary cell culture system (RCCS)-based dynamic 3D platform for scalable MSC sp generation using MSCs derived from amniotic membrane, umbilical cord, and fetal placenta. RCCS-MSC sp harvested at day 2 exhibited compact morphology, uniform size, high viability, and improved mitochondrial function. Compared with monolayer MSCs and hanging drop spheroids, RCCS-MSC sp displayed reduced apoptosis, enhanced antioxidative capacity, and increased extracellular matrix deposition. Transcriptomic analysis revealed conserved activation of immunoregulatory, angiogenic, extracellular matrix, and tissue repair programs across MSC sources. Functionally, RCCS-MSC sp promoted endothelial protection, macrophage polarization, and diabetic wound repair through enhanced vascularization and tissue remodeling. Moreover, RCCS-mediated spheroid formation partially reduced source-associated functional variability among perinatal MSCs. This study provides a scalable scaffold-free 3D bioengineering strategy to generate standardized, functionally enhanced MSC spheroids for translational regenerative applications.

works.title: A multifunctional QK@ZIF-8@GA hydrogel promotes vascularized bone regeneration in diabetic bone defects by remodeling the osteoimmune microenvironment
works.abstract: Diabetic bone regeneration is severely compromised by hyperglycemia, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and impaired angiogenesis. Here, we developed a multifunctional QK@ZIF-8@GA composite hydrogel by loading QK peptide into ZIF-8 and incorporating the resulting nanoparticles into a lithospermic acid (LA)-functionalized GelMA hydrogel, thereby enabling coordinated antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and vascularized osteogenic regulation. QK@ZIF-8@GA reduced ROS accumulation, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and promoted macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype, thereby remodeling the paracrine microenvironment, enhancing HUVEC migration and tube formation, and promoting osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization of BMSCs. Transcriptomic and protein analyses identified changes in PI3K/Akt signaling associated with macrophage functional remodeling. In a T2DM rat calvarial defect model, QK@ZIF-8@GA markedly promoted neovascularization and vascular maturation, new bone formation, and trabecular reconstruction. In vivo transcriptomic analysis further revealed coordinated enrichment of programs associated with immune regulation, vascular development, bone mineralization, and osteogenic differentiation. No evident systemic toxicity was observed. Collectively, QK@ZIF-8@GA alleviates oxidative stress, remodels the osteoimmune microenvironment, and coordinates angiogenesis and osteogenic regeneration, providing a promising multifunctional biomaterial strategy for diabetic bone defect repair.

works.title: Neutrophil-hitchhiking and microglia-homing liposomes co-delivering artemisinin and edaravone for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury treatment
works.abstract: ABSTRACT: Clinical outcomes of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remain unsatisfactory, largely because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts the delivery of most neuroprotective agents to the brain parenchyma. Although artemisinin (ART) and edaravone (EDV) have shown promising therapeutic potential for CIRI, their clinical application is hindered by their short in vivo half-lives and poor aqueous solubility. Neutrophil infiltration triggered by CIRI provides a unique opportunity for drug delivery across the BBB, whereas targeted modulation of microglia represents a key strategy for mitigating reperfusion-induced injury. However, existing neutrophil hitchhiking delivery systems primarily focus on BBB traversal and generally lack a secondary targeting mechanism to promote preferential drug accumulation within the inflammatory core of the ischemic brain. Here, we developed a dual-modified liposomal system functionalized with sialic acid (SA) and phosphatidylserine (PS) (ART/EDV-PS/SAL) for the co-delivery of ART and EDV. This system enables sequential two-step targeting through SA-mediated neutrophil hitchhiking for BBB traversal, followed by PS-mediated microglial homing within ischemic brain tissue. In a mouse model of CIRI, ART/EDV-PS/SAL markedly reduced cerebral infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and significantly improved neurological and behavioral outcomes. Mechanistically, ART/EDV-PS/SAL exerted neuroprotective effects by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation, attenuating pyroptosis, and promoting microglial polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. By harnessing endogenous immune cells to achieve efficient and sequential drug targeting, this study establishes a promising nanodelivery platform for the treatment of ischemic stroke and other neuroinflammatory disorders.

works.title: Magnetoelectric Nanomaterials for Wireless Peripheral Nervous System Interfacing: Synthesis, Applications, and Open Challenges
works.abstract: Magnetoelectric (ME) nanostructures convert applied magnetic fields into localized electric fields via magnetostrictive-to-piezoelectric coupling, enabling wireless, implant-free modulation of neural activity. While their potential for central nervous system (CNS) applications has been extensively explored, their use in peripheral nervous system (PNS) interfacing, where direct access to sensory, motor, and autonomic pathways could transform neuroprosthetics, pain management, and bioelectronic medicine, remains largely uncharted. Here, we review the design, synthesis, and application of ME nanomaterials for PNS interfacing, with focus on core-shell ME nanoparticles (MENPs) based on cobalt ferrite–barium titanate (CoFe 2 O 4 –BaTiO 3 ). We discuss the physical principles of magnetoelectricity and methods for quantifying the ME coupling coefficient from bulk to single-particle resolution. Liquid-phase synthesis strategies are reviewed, showing how morphology and interface quality govern ME performance, colloidal stability in biological media and biocompatibility. MENP integration into hybrid polymeric scaffolds for neural stimulation, sensing, and regeneration is assessed alongside experimental and computational studies spanning off-resonance and resonant regimes. Three priorities for clinical translation emerge: low-temperature synthesis resolving the thermal conflict between phase purity and colloidal stability, reproducible methods to quantify ME coupling with single-particle resolution, and standardized in vitro and in vivo protocols for stimulation and detection.

works.title: Lithium-Based Biomaterials for Bone Regeneration: A Dose–Space–Time–Host Framework for Immunometabolic Control
works.abstract: Functional bone restoration remains a major clinical challenge in orthopedics and regenerative medicine. Skeletal defects impair patient quality of life, while autografts, allografts, and synthetic implants are limited by their inability to precisely control bone metabolism. Lithium, a bioactive ion, has emerged as a promising candidate because it bidirectionally regulates bone remodeling: it promotes osteoblast proliferation, differentiation, and matrix mineralization while inhibiting osteoclast differentiation, shifting bone metabolism toward anabolism and compensating for the limited bioactivity of synthetic materials. However, lithium’s efficacy is not intrinsic; it depends on local dose, exposure duration, carrier degradation kinetics, and host pathology—a concept termed lithium therapeutic programming. Lithium has been incorporated into metals, bioceramics, coatings, hydrogels, and 3D-printed scaffolds, but the field remains fragmented. Most studies assess isolated outcomes such as osteogenesis, osteoclast inhibition, macrophage polarization, or angiogenesis, or classify materials by composition rather than by control over lithium bioavailability. This obscures a key point: lithium is not universally regenerative, but a context-dependent signaling modulator. We reinterpret the literature through a Dose–Space–Time–Host (DSTH) framework. Biologically, GSK-3β inhibition and Wnt/β-catenin modulation are the best-established mechanism; osteoimmune coupling via NF-κB, RANKL/OPG, and macrophage signaling is context-dependent; extracellular vesicle/non-coding RNA regulation and neurovascular–immune coupling are emerging but lack complete causal evidence. We therefore conceptualize lithium biomaterials as therapeutic programming systems, in which regeneration arises from coupling among lithium exposure, multicellular signaling, material-controlled release, and host pathology. Current limitations include inconsistent reporting of local exposure, unclear systemic versus local therapeutic windows, overinterpretation of M1/M2 polarization, limited causal validation of EV and neurovascular mechanisms, confounding co-doped ions, and weak small-animal-to-clinical translation. Next-generation lithium biomaterials should move from simple lithium incorporation toward quantitative ion pharmacokinetics, stage-adaptive release, pathology-specific design, and mechanism-guided translational validation, converting lithium from a broad bioactive dopant into a programmable immunometabolic signal for bone regeneration(Figure 1).

works.title: A biomarker-guided photonic-crystal aptasensor for urinary HSPA5 in prostate cancer
works.abstract: Urinary prostate-cancer biosensors can be analytically sensitive yet translationally weak when target selection is not biologically justified. We developed a proteomics-guided photonic-crystal aptasensor for heat shock protein family A member 5 (HSPA5/GRP78). A contamination-aware urinary-proteomic and biological filtering cascade prioritized HSPA5 using differential abundance, reproducible elevation in the uEV-P20 fraction, tissue concordance, PSA gray-zone behavior and unfolded-protein-response biology. Structure-informed computational sequence prioritization and docking nominated three 30-nt candidates; ITC and SPR established the Apt1 > Apt2 > Apt3 affinity hierarchy, and peptide-competition SPR supported involvement of the HSPA5 552-581 region without assigning residue-level contacts or the complete folded-protein interface. Apt1 was covalently immobilized on a 200-nm carboxylated polystyrene photonic-crystal surface and read by wavelength shift (Δλ) with an orthogonal signed peak-amplitude change (ΔT, arbitrary units). The tested series comprised 20 levels from 250 fg mL -1 to 1 μg mL -1 ; the restricted Δλ calibration fit used 0.5-125 ng mL -1 . The response-domain LoD was 0.3315 nm, with a model-extrapolated concentration equivalent of 0.159 ng mL -1 . Recombinant non-target responses were 1.7-4.8%, interference recovery was 96.33-102.00%, spike recovery was 96.39-104.21%, and the urine-matrix challenge produced maximum individual mean responses of 6.34% at 1× and 12.30% at 10×, a full-cocktail response of 19.13%, and HSPA5-plus-cocktail recovery of 105.33%. In the n = 100 urine cohort, Apt1-PC response was higher in prostate cancer than in benign groups and correlated positively, but non-interchangeably, with paired HSPA5 ELISA. The creatinine-normalized sensor-equivalent analysis yielded AUC 0.767 (95% CI 0.669-0.854); the out-of-fold PCa-versus-BPH combined-model AUC was 0.768 (0.672-0.858). The workflow supports investigation of aptamer-detectable urinary HSPA5 species rather than prostate-specific expression or recognition of every proteoform. Clinical results are exploratory same-cohort comparisons and require independent validation with a locked assay and model.

works.title: Engineering functional perfusion in vascularized cardiac grafts through bioactive biomaterials and biofabrication
works.abstract: Vascularized cardiac grafts are being developed to overcome the limited survival and incomplete integration of engineered myocardial tissues after implantation. Although many platforms can now generate endothelial networks, the central challenge is no longer the presence of vascular-like structures alone, but the establishment of networks that remain perfusable, mechanically stable, and functionally coupled to the host circulation. This review discusses cellular design, bioactive biomaterial selection, biofabrication strategies, flow-mediated endothelial maturation, and preclinical evaluation of vascularized cardiac grafts. We compare the roles of cardiomyocytes, endothelial and mural cells, and supportive stromal populations, and examine how bioactive matrix cues, bioprinting, perfusion culture, and hemodynamic conditioning influence vascular stability. Attention is given to the distinction between structural vascularization and functional perfusion, as this remains a major bottleneck in interpreting experimental outcomes and advancing translational studies. Finally, we highlight emerging challenges related to hiPSC-derived cell maturity, manufacturing reproducibility, long-term patency, electromechanical integration, and large-animal validation. Progress in this field will likely depend on treating vascularized grafts as integrated living systems rather than static tissue constructs.

works.title: A multi-targeted, barrier-penetrating inhalable nanoplatform for simultaneous immunomodulation and antifibrotic therapy in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
works.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and fatal lung disorder characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, myofibroblast activation, and chronic inflammation. Current pharmacotherapies are hindered by modest anti-fibrotic efficacy and poor drug accumulation within fibrotic lesions. Herein, we developed an inhalable, collagenase-modified liposomal nanoplatform co-encapsulating methylprednisolone and pirfenidone (termed CMPNPs) to address these limitations. The CMPNPs exhibited favorable physicochemical properties and retained collagenase activity under atomization-induced shear forces, enabling efficient penetration through collagen-dense barriers and enhanced lung accumulation. In vitro, CMPNPs suppressed TGF-β1-induced myofibroblast differentiation and migration, and shifted macrophage polarization away from pro-fibrotic and pro-inflammatory phenotypes. In a bleomycin-induced IPF mouse model, inhaled CMPNPs improved survival, reduced collagen deposition and fibrotic lesions, and demonstrated superior lung retention and anti-fibrotic efficacy compared to intravenous administration. Collectively, this multi-targeted, barrier-penetrating strategy overcomes key bottlenecks of current IPF therapies and offers a promising translatable approach for treating progressive pulmonary fibrosis.

works.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing
works.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure–activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. These phytosterols altered LNP mechanics and morphology, promoting cellular uptake. In vitro results and molecular dynamics simulations revealed differential interactions between phytosterols and Niemann–Pick C1 (NPC1), a late endosomal membrane protein involved in intracellular cholesterol transport. These interactions influenced the late-endosomal retention of phytosterol-substituted LNPs and contributed to enhanced transfection. Furthermore, rather than simply prolonging retention, phytosterol substitution modulated LNP trafficking kinetics, establishing a formulation-dependent optimal intracellular residence window. In vivo results demonstrated reduced serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in mice receiving phytosterol-substituted LNPs. Collectively, these findings elucidate how cholesterol analogues regulate LNP physicochemical properties and intracellular trafficking, providing mechanistic insights and design principles for developing more efficient and precise mRNA delivery systems.

works.title: Sequentially responsive nanodroplets restore immune-microbial homeostasis in ulcerative colitis
works.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is an inflammatory bowel disease characterized by persistent mucosal inflammation and gut microbial dysbiosis. Current therapies primarily target excessive inflammation but often fail to restore the microbial imbalance, resulting in limited efficacy. In this study, we developed a sequentially responsive oral nanodroplet platform based on charge-reversible nanodroplets (SA@PL@CND) to simultaneously restore immune and microbial homeostasis in UC. The SA@PL@CND were prepared by sequentially coating curcumin-loaded bovine serum albumin nanodroplet (CND) with polylysine and sodium alginate. After oral administration, the alginate shell protected the formulation during gastrointestinal transit and was designed to undergo enzymatic de-shielding in the colonic environment. At inflamed lesions, the pathological acidification could promote dissociation of PL through the intrinsic charge transition of albumin. In UC mice, SA@PL@CND significantly alleviated disease severity by suppressing inflammation and promoting the recovery of gut microbial homeostasis. Collectively, sequentially responsive nanodroplets offer an effective strategy to restore immune and microbial homeostasis for UC therapy.

works.title: Metabolic Interference Coupled with mTOR Inhibition for Suppression of Colorectal Cancer Stemness
works.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with treatment resistance being associated with stem-like properties and metabolic plasticity. To address these challenges, we developed a nanoengineered delivery system based on chondroitin sulfate (CS)-functionalized zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) for the co-delivery of cisplatin (CDDP) and rapamycin (RPM). This integrated nanoplatform was designed to integrate CDDP-induced DNA damage, RPM-mediated mTOR inhibition, and metabolic interference associated with ZIF-8-derived Zn 2+ . Upon exposure to acidic conditions, ZIF-8 undergoes pH-responsive degradation, releasing Zn 2+ ions that may contribute to the observed reductions in glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) expression and intracellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels. These effects were accompanied by reduced stemness-associated phenotypes in CRC cells. Surface functionalization with CS was designed to facilitate interactions with CD44-expressing CRC cells and was associated with increased cellular uptake and tumor-associated fluorescence. In vitro and in vivo evaluations, including an orthotopic CRC model and a postoperative tumor recurrence model, showed suppression of tumor growth, reduced postoperative recurrence, and no evident short- or long-term toxicity under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings support further investigation of a therapeutic strategy integrating CDDP chemotherapy, mTOR inhibition, and Zn 2+ -associated metabolic interference for CRC treatment.

works.title: A Brachytherapy-Activated Radiosensitizer Converts Cancer Stemness into Pyroptotic Lethality to Overcome Radioresistance
works.abstract: Locoregional recurrence after radiotherapy remains a major clinical challenge due to acquired radioresistance, which promotes therapeutic evasion and limits the efficacy of re-irradiation. Using paired clinical specimens and radioresistant models, we discovered that cancer stem cells (CSCs) enriched in recurrent tumors exhibit marked upregulation of gasdermin C (GSDMC), revealing a stemness-associated vulnerability to pyroptosis. Capitalizing on this targetable weakness, we engineered an injectable PWCo-ALG (Na 10 [(PW 9 O 34 ) 2 Co 4 (H 2 O) 2 ]·48H 2 O-alginate) hydrogel that undergoes calcium-mediated solidification within the tumor microenvironment and releases cobalt ions in a spatially controlled manner upon brachytherapy activation. This radiation-triggered nanocluster specifically induces caspase-8/GSDMC-mediated pyroptosis in radioresistant CSCs, eliciting potent immunogenic cell death with release of damage-associated molecular patterns such as HMGB1 and ATP. The resulting immune activation recruits dendritic cells and enhances CD8 + T-cell infiltration, effectively reversing the immunosuppressive microenvironment and triggering a systemic antitumor response that suppresses both local recurrence and distant metastasis. By leveraging the intrinsic pyroptotic susceptibility of CSCs through a brachytherapy-activated nanoplatform, this work provides a paradigm-shifting strategy to overcome acquired radioresistance and achieve durable tumor control.

works.title: A Glucose-Competitive Hydrogel Targeting GLUT1 Accelerates Diabetic Oral Wound Healing
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Oral wound healing is notoriously difficult in diabetes. Hyperglycemia upregulates GLUT1, driving excessive glucose influx and compounding local dysbiosis, which together fuel oxidative damage and persistent inflammation. Current topical therapies lack both mucosal retention and etiology-directed design, failing to reverse this underlying metabolic disruption. To address these challenges, we developed AA2G@Q4F-FG, an injectable, thermosensitive, and glucose-responsive hydrogel, designed not only to provide rapid hemostasis and antibacterial activity through quaternized chitosan against oral pathogens, but also to fundamentally combat glucose overload via GLUT1-targeted substrate competition. Ascorbic acid 2-glucoside (AA2G) was validated as a functional GLUT1-engaging substrate via molecular docking, SPR binding kinetics, competitive 2-NBDG uptake, and feedback downregulation of GLUT1 at the transcriptional/protein level. When loaded in this mucoadhesive matrix with glucose-triggered release, AA2G enables sustained, on-demand competition at the wound interface. In vitro, the hydrogel scavenged ROS, promoted macrophage polarization toward an M2-like state, and restored fibroblast/epithelial/endothelial cell functions. In vivo, it accelerated closure, increased collagen deposition and angiogenesis, and remodeled the pathological milieu. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that the hydrogel broadly reprogrammed the wound microenvironment across metabolic, inflammatory, and repair signaling networks. Notably, the hydrogel unexpectedly induced endogenous FGF1, activated AKT/ERK signaling, and modulated the Hippo/YAP1 pathway, with YAP1 redistribution to the cytoplasm, consistent with restored cellular homeostasis. Taken together, this glucose-competitive dressing targets the metabolic root of delayed oral healing: AA2G engages GLUT1 as a rapidly reversible competitive substrate to curb glucose influx, and the hydrogel modulates FGF1-dependent AKT/ERK–Hippo/YAP1 signaling associated with restored tissue homeostasis and repair.

works.title: NIR-Activated Nanohybrid Microneedles Eradicate Biofilms and Intracellular Bacteria for Diabetic Wound Repair
works.abstract: Persistent infection in diabetic wounds involves extracellular biofilms and bacteria sheltered within macrophages, making bacterial control across both compartments an important therapeutic challenge. Here, we developed FPS@MSNs-Cer-HA, a near-infrared (NIR)-activated dissolving hyaluronic acid microneedle platform incorporating ceramide-loaded FePS 3 @mesoporous silica nanohybrids for localized treatment. The mesoporous silica shell improves nanosheet dispersibility and enables ceramide loading, whereas the FePS 3 nanosheet core serves as an NIR-responsive source of photothermal heat, photoinduced ROS, and released iron ions that amplify Fenton-like oxidative stress. Under acidic conditions and 808 nm NIR irradiation, nanohybrid disassembly and Fe 2+ release were accelerated, enhancing oxidative antibacterial activity. FPS@MSNs-Cer-HA achieved >99% killing of planktonic Escherichia coli and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and markedly disrupted established biofilms. Importantly, FPS@MSNs-Cer-HA enhanced macrophage-mediated clearance of intracellular MRSA by elevating intracellular ROS and NO production, increasing iNOS expression, and promoting macrophage polarization toward an M1-like phenotype. In an MRSA-infected diabetic wound model, NIR-activated FPS@MSNs-Cer-HA reduced tissue bacterial burden and inflammationwhile accelerating wound closure, improving re-epithelialization, collagen remodeling, and angiogenesis without apparent systemic toxicity. These findings establish a reservoir-targeted microneedle strategy that integrates extracellular biofilm eradication, macrophage-assisted intracellular bacterial clearance, and repair-supportive local delivery for the treatment of infected diabetic wounds.

works.title: CuCo bimetallic single-atom nanozyme microneedle patch for synergistic therapy of drug-resistant infected wounds
works.abstract: ABSTRACT: Drug-resistant bacterial wound infections remain a formidable clinical challenge. We report a tannic acid-modified CuCo bimetallic single-atom nanozyme-loaded dissolvable microneedle patch (TCCS@MN) for spatiotemporal reactive oxygen species (ROS) regulation for synergistic therapy of drug-resistant infected wounds. Atomically dispersed Cu-Co dual sites synergistically boost peroxidase-, oxidase-, and glutathione peroxidase-like activities, enabling pH-dependent bidirectional ROS modulation. In the acidic infectious microenvironment, TCCS@MN catalyzes a ROS burst and depletes glutathione, disrupting bacterial redox homeostasis and inducing lipid peroxidation; in the neutral healing microenvironment, its catalase- and superoxide dismutase-like activities shift the balance toward ROS scavenging, alleviating oxidative stress and promoting regeneration. The integrated ROS burst, glutathione depletion, and lipid peroxidation constitute a triple antibacterial mechanism. The microneedle patch breaches the stratum corneum, improves local retention, and rapidly releases TCCS into the wound bed. This design combines single-atom catalysis with microneedle delivery to overcome the skin barrier and improve therapeutic exposure at the infection site. In vitro, TCCS@MN disrupts bacterial membranes and inhibits methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by >99.9%, while also showing activity against Escherichia coli. In an MRSA-infected full-thickness wound model, the patch accelerates healing, achieving 98.14% closure within 7 days with favorable biosafety. This platform provides a promising therapeutic strategy for drug-resistant infected wounds and warrants further preclinical investigation.

works.title: Barbed microneedle patch with programmable CO release for long-term and stage-specific therapy of chronic infected wounds
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic infected wounds are difficult to heal because bacterial colonization drives persistent inflammation, which further impairs tissue regeneration. This dynamic pathology requires stage-specific intervention, with rapid bacterial suppression followed by sustained inflammatory regulation. Carbon monoxide (CO) has concentration-dependent antibacterial and immunomodulatory activities, but on-demand and temporally programmed local CO release remains challenging. Here, we report a barbed core-shell microneedle patch (COMN) for programmed CO release. Inspired by bee stingers, barbed microneedles improve tissue anchoring during light activation. To match wound-healing stages, flavonoid-based CO450 was chemically immobilized in the shell through boronate ester formation with glucose-derived diol groups, enabling acid-amplified burst CO release under blue-light activation for rapid MRSA and Escherichia coli killing and biofilm disruption. BODIPY-based CO530 was covalently incorporated into the photocured core network, providing green-light-activated sustained CO release for macrophage immunomodulation by suppressing inflammatory cytokines and enhancing repair-associated cytokine secretion. In a diabetic MRSA-infected wound model, programmed blue/green light activation achieved a bacterial killing rate of 91.16% and reduced the residual wound area to 4.96% on day 14, compared with 20.74% in the infected control group. These results suggest that COMN enables dual-light activated sequential CO release for long-term, stage-specific treatment of chronic infected wounds.

works.title: Multi-Scale Photophysical Regulation Enables High-Fidelity Dual-Lock Nanoprobe for Early Atherosclerosis Imaging
works.abstract: Atherosclerosis is the primary etiology of many severe cardiovascular diseases, making early and accurate detection crucial. This study engineers a self-assembled dual-locked nanoprobe, bBAH @ Cy-PEG , through synergistic multi-scale regulation of intermolecular and intramolecular photophysical processes, enabling sequential activation by reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid droplets (LDs) for precise imaging of early-stage atherosclerosis. The nanoprobe is initially quenched via Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) from bBAH to Cy-PEG . Upon ROS stimulation, Cy-PEG is cleaved, releasing bBAH , which remains non-fluorescent due to aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) in aqueous environments. Subsequent accumulation of bBAH in LDs activates its excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), turning on near-infrared fluorescence. Thus, emission occurs only upon the simultaneous overexpression of both ROS and LDs, achieving a superior signal-to-noise ratio through the synergistic integration of low background conferred by FRET and ACQ, and high signal output enabled by ESIPT. bBAH @ Cy-PEG can accurately detect LDs, with its signal-to-noise ratio and the number of detected LDs significantly higher than those of commercial BODIPY method in foam cells. Furthermore, bBAH @ Cy-PEG is able to accurately detect atherosclerotic plaques in mice at an early stage (8 weeks of high-fat diet). This dual-locked nanoprobe enables earlier and more accurate detection of atherosclerotic lesions and holds potential for clinical diagnosis.

works.title: Engineered Micro-Nano System for ADSC-Exosomes-Based Therapy of Liver Fibrosis via ROS Elimination and PPARγ/PCK1 Pathway Reactivation
works.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a progressive hepatic disorder driven by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated transcriptional reprogramming of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Effective clinical interventions remain extremely limited, as targeting a single pathological pathway provides only partial benefit and fails to fully arrest disease progression. Herein, by screening a dynamic human liver fibrosis organoid model, we identified miR-3682-3p as a previously unrecognized pro-fibrotic driver that was upregulated during fibrosis progression and associated with disease severity. To enable dual-pathway intervention, we engineered a targeted nanotherapeutic platform based on adipose-derived stem cell exosomes (ADSC-EVs), loaded with a miR-3682-3p inhibitor (in-3682) and surface-decorated with cRGDyk-modified cerium oxide (CeO 2 ) nanozymes. This platform, termed RC@EVs-in3682, preferentially targets activated HSCs and concurrently mitigates oxidative stress and pro-fibrotic signaling, thereby suppressing HSC activation, contraction, and migration. Moreover, in a carbon tetrachloride (CCl 4 )-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis, RC@EVs-in3682 reduced collagen deposition and restored hepatic architecture. Mechanistically, our findings support that inhibition of miR-3682-3p and CeO 2 -mediated ROS scavenging together promote the restoration of the peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ (PPARγ)/PCK1 axis; accordingly, RC@EVs-in3682 restores PPARγ-dependent PCK1 expression and the associated metabolic program. Collectively, our study provides a multifunctional nanoplatform and establishes RC@EVs-in3682 as a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for liver fibrosis by simultaneously targeting oxidative stress and pro-fibrotic signaling.

Sustained delivery of 3D-bioprinted stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles promotes neural regeneration following traumatic brain injury via the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 axis
works.abstract: Background Clinical translation of stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) for traumatic brain injury (TBI) is restricted by low yield in 2D culture and rapid in vivo clearance. Objective To develop an in situ sustained delivery system (3D-sEVs@Gel) encapsulating 3D-bioprinted adipose stem cell (ADSC)-derived sEVs (3D-ADSC-sEVs) within GelMA (Gelatin methacryloyl) hydrogel for long-term functional repair after TBI. Methods SEVs derived from coaxially bioprinted 3D-ADSCs were isolated, and a GelMA hydrogel-based delivery system was subsequently constructed. Following orthotopic transplantation of the 3D-sEVs@Gel system into the lesion site after TBI, functional recovery, neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and lineage-associated responses, and the underlying molecular mechanisms were systematically evaluated through behavioral tests, immunofluorescence, multi-omics, and pharmacological inhibition. Results SEVs generated using the coaxial alginate-microfiber culture system exhibited an approximately eightfold higher yields and protein loading compared with those obtained from 2D culture. In vivo , 3D-sEVs@Gel prolonged local retention, reduced tissue loss, and significantly improved long-term sensorimotor coordination and spatial memory following TBI. In addition, treatment increased the numbers of proliferating cells co-expressing neural progenitor-, neuronal-, and oligodendroglial-lineage-associated markers within the examined neurogenic regions. Mechanistically, 3D-sEV treatment increased nuclear CREB1 levels in NSCs, promoting PGC-1α transcription and subsequent FNDC5 expression, thereby supporting endogenous neurogenesis and functional neural repair. Conclusion The 3D-sEVs@Gel system promotes chronic neurological reconstruction post-TBI by modulating NSC proliferation and neural lineage-associated responses through the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 pathway, offering a promising cell-free strategy for neural repair and tissue engineering.

works.title: An optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched dual-crosslinkable hydrogel for cell-free remodeling of the corneal stroma
works.abstract: Corneal trauma is a leading cause of visual impairment and blindness worldwide, yet corneal stromal repair and regeneration remain a significant challenge in ophthalmology because of its limited intrinsic repair capacity and fibrotic scar formation during healing process. Here we report an optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel that enables cell-free corneal stromal remodeling. By integrating dynamic covalent crosslinking with static photocrosslinking strategy, the optimized hydrogel-based substitute achieved high optical transparency, a refractive index of approximately 1.35, and an elastic modulus of 83.8 ± 13.4 kPa, closely resembling the properties of the healthy human cornea. In a rabbit model of deep corneal defects, the optimized in situ -forming hydrogel adapted to the defect geometry, adhered stably to the wound bed, recapitulated the optical and biomechanical properties of the native cornea, and supported scarless corneal stromal remodeling. Incorporation of the antimicrobial peptide HHC36 further endowed the hydrogel with robust antibacterial activity without compromising its optical and biomechanical properties. In a rabbit model of P. aeruginosa –infected deep corneal defects, the HHC36-loaded in situ -forming hydrogel effectively mitigated clinical signs of infection and substantially promoted corneal stromal remodeling within 30 days while reducing fibrosis. Overall, this optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel might be a promising substitute for corneal stromal remodeling.

works.title: Reprogrammed macrophage-derived nanovesicle–lipid nanoparticle hybrids for cardiac siRUNX1 delivery: Therapeutic evaluation in Ang II-induced cardiac remodeling
works.abstract: Targeted delivery of small interfering RNA (siRNA) to the heart remains challenging because conventional lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) predominantly accumulate in the liver following systemic administration. To improve cardiac siRNA delivery, we developed a biomimetic hybrid nanoplatform by co-extruding siRUNX1-loaded LNPs with reprogrammed macrophage-derived nanovesicles (rMNVs) obtained from sequentially LPS/TGF-β1-treated RAW264.7 macrophages, followed by surface functionalization with a cardiac-targeting peptide (CTP). The sequentially treated donor cells exhibited a phenotypic shift characterized by reduced M1-associated markers and enhanced M2-associated features. The resulting CTP-hLNPs maintained a nanoscale spherical morphology, high siRNA encapsulation efficiency, and retained donor-cell-derived membrane components, including CD206. In vitro, CTP-hLNPs showed reduced uptake by RAW264.7 macrophages while maintaining cellular internalization and siRUNX1 activity in H9c2 cardiac-derived cells. Following intravenous administration, CTP-hLNPs exhibited reduced liver-associated fluorescence and increased heart-associated fluorescence at 24 h compared with conventional CTP-LNPs. Therapeutic efficacy was subsequently evaluated in an angiotensin II (Ang II)-induced mouse model of cardiac remodeling. CTP-hLNP@siRUNX1 reduced cardiac RUNX1 mRNA expression and improved left ventricular systolic function, as indicated by increased left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening. Treatment also attenuated cardiac hypertrophic remodeling, including reductions in the heart weight-to-body weight ratio and cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area. In addition, CTP-hLNP@siRUNX1 reduced myofibroblast-associated α-SMA expression, collagen deposition, and myocardial fibrotic area. Collectively, these findings support rMNV–LNP hybridization combined with CTP functionalization as a potential delivery strategy for cardiac RNA interference therapy and demonstrate its therapeutic effects in Ang II-induced cardiac remodeling.

works.title: Dual-action nanotheranostics targeting cell-free DNA rescues aberrant alternative polyadenylation to ameliorate periodontitis
works.abstract: ) are known to severely disrupt macrophage post-transcriptional homeostasis, the precise extracellular instigator remains elusive. Here, through comparative transcriptomic profiling, we identify cell-free DNA (cfDNA) as this fundamental pathogenic trigger. Comprehensive bioinformatic analysis uncovers that cfDNA governs macrophage fate by fundamentally rewiring the global alternative polyadenylation (APA) equilibrium. Specifically, cfDNA forces pro-inflammatory (M1) transcripts into translationally hyperactive short-3'-untranslated region (3'UTR) isoforms, while simultaneously suppressing anti-inflammatory (M2) programs via 3'UTR lengthening. To therapeutically intercept this cfDNA-APA pathogenic axis, we engineered a homologous nanotheranostic platform (DA-APAT). Addressing the unique clinical demands for early periodontitis screening, its polycationic PEI shell enables highly sensitive salivary cfDNA theranostic monitoring. Crucially, this monitoring readout directly calibrates the in situ enzymatic clearance load executed by the internally encapsulated DNase I. Synergized by the intrinsic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capability of the hollow mesoporous cerium oxide core, this monitoring nanoplatform decisively silences intracellular DNA-sensing pathways (cGAS-STING/TLR9), rectifies the disrupted APA, and contributes robust M2 macrophage repolarization. In an orthotopic murine periodontitis model, this nanotherapy effectively halts alveolar bone loss and facilitates profound periodontal regeneration with excellent biocompatibility. This work unveils a cfDNA-driven RNA regulatory paradigm in immune dysregulation and provides a monitoring precision nanotheranostic modality for inflammatory therapy.

works.title: A pH-responsive GelMA-KerMA hydrogel delivering luteolin-loaded PLGA nanoparticles promotes myocardial repair via Akt/Bad signaling and multitarget regulation
works.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers cardiomyocyte apoptosis, oxidative stress imbalance, ventricular fibrosis, and impaired angiogenesis. Luteolin, a natural flavonoid compound, possesses antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and cardioprotective properties, making it a promising candidate for MI treatment. However, its poor water solubility, low bioavailability, and chemical instability severely hinder its clinical translation. To address these limitations, we developed a photo-crosslinked composite hydrogel delivery system using gelatin methacryloyl and keratin methacryloyl (GelMA-KerMA). Luteolin-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles were uniformly dispersed within a three-dimensional gel network to achieve pH-triggered local drug delivery. The covalent GelMA–KerMA network retained structural integrity under both pH conditions. In the weakly acidic infarct microenvironment, acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of PLGA ester bonds was the primary driver of accelerated luteolin release, whereas the network mainly acted as a sustained-retarding reservoir. The incorporation of KerMA endowed the patch with enhanced mechanical stability and cytocompatibility, enabling better mechanical matching with the infarcted myocardium. The composite hydrogel promotes myocardial repair and functional recovery through the coordinated regulation of the rapid Akt/Bad phosphorylation cascade. It also sustains MAPK/Rap1-dependent transcriptional reprogramming. It inhibits mitochondrial apoptosis, scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), suppresses fibroblast activation, and promotes neovascularization. This study presents a protein-based delivery platform that integrates tailored physicochemical and mechanical properties with multi-pathway myocardial repair capabilities, offering a biomaterial strategy for minimally invasive local drug delivery in ischemic MI.
