Magnetoactive Hydrogels to Probe Curvature‐Directed Endothelial Cell Mechanosensing
works.abstract: The vascular system exhibits complex, nonplanar geometries that become further distorted during pathological remodeling, including arterial tortuosity and aneurysms. Although hemodynamic shear stress is a well-established regulator of vascular function, the direct effects of curvature as an intrinsic geometric cue remain poorly defined. This is largely because existing in vitro models are static and fail to capture the dynamic changes that accompany disease progression. To address this gap, we used a magnetoactive hydrogel platform that enables real-time, on-demand curvature of endothelial monolayers to reproduce clinically established tortuosity metrics. Using this system, we found that elevated curvature increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP), with the strongest response in convex relative to concave regions of highly tortuous endothelial monolayers. This mechanosensitive response was accompanied by reduced VE-Cadherin junctional thickness and increased membrane localization of endothelial nitric oxide synthase. These findings identify local curvature, independent of shear stress, as a regulator of endothelial cell mechanosensing and function, and establish a dynamic hydrogel platform for isolating geometric regulation from shear stress inputs in vascular mechanobiology.

works.title: TiCoCr‐Based Multi‐Principal Element Alloys for Biomedical Applications
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Next‐generation biomedical implants require materials with excellent wear resistance, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. This study developed two novel multi‐principal element alloys (MPEAs) based on the TiCoCr composition (equiatomic and non‐equiatomic) with ultra‐high hardness, excellent wear resistance, corrosion stability, and biocompatibility. The as‐cast microstructures revealed a multiphase combination of Ti‐rich hexagonal closed packing (HCP), C 14 Laves, and face‐centered cubic (FCC) phases. Upon heat treatment, equiatomic (Ti 33 Co 33 Cr 33 ) MPEA developed two major body‐centered (BCC) phases and a minor HCP phase, whereas heat treatment of non‐equiatomic (Ti 50 Co 25 Cr 25 ) MPEA revealed one BCC and C 14 Laves phase. The hardness of both MPEAs was slightly reduced after heat treatment. Wear and corrosion tests conducted in Hanks' balanced salt solution (HBSS) at 37°C on heat‐treated MPEAs demonstrated improved tribological and corrosion behavior, with reduced wear and a lower coefficient of friction (COF). Electrochemical analysis indicated superior corrosion resistance, particularly for Ti 33 Co 33 Cr 33 MPEA. With respect to biocompatibility, both MPEAs demonstrated excellent cell adhesion and proliferation properties. Cell viability improved significantly, increasing from the control (100%) to ∼105% and 115% after 3 and 5 days, respectively. The combined results highlight the strong potential of these MPEAs for biomedical applications, offering a unique balance of high “density‐normalized” hardness, excellent corrosion resistance, and biological compatibility for future implant solutions.

works.title: Measuring Blood Plasma Glutamine Levels Using a Nanopore‐Based Sensor
works.abstract: Measuring blood glutamine (GLN) levels is valuable for managing urea cycle disorders. Currently, patients visit the hospital to have their GLN levels checked using analytical techniques that, despite being highly accurate and reliable, lead to long waiting times and delay clinical decisions. A point-of-care device would enable patients to monitor GLN levels at home, allowing for greater control over the condition. Here, we made use of a highly sensitive GLN biosensor system based on dodecameric Cytolysin A variant AS (ClyA-AS) nanopore coupled with the GLN-specific protein, the substrate-binding domain 2 (SBD2). Measurements are performed on a single ClyA-AS nanopore embedded into an artificial lipid bilayer, where the application of a small voltage generates ionic currents that report on the binding and unbinding of GLN (added in the trans side of ClyA-AS) to SBD2 (added in cis). We demonstrate that the ClyA-AS and SBD2 biosensor pair can quantify GLN levels in patients' blood plasma. To facilitate the use of this sensor in clinical and point-of-care settings, we also developed a dedicated algorithm that accelerates signal processing and data analysis. Together, these advances represent a significant step toward a point-of-care device for GLN monitoring, both at the hospital and home-care levels.

works.title: Mesoporous Silica Nanoplatforms: From Controllable Synthesis to Versatile Biomedical Applications
works.abstract: The increasing global burden of severe diseases, such as cancers, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disorders, highlights the urgent need for advanced diagnostic and therapeutic agents. Although techniques like computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and chemotherapy show promise, their effectiveness is frequently constrained by the inherent drawbacks of conventional agents, such as poor solubility, low stability, and lack of targeting ability, as well as physiological barriers like the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which limit bioavailability and induce systemic toxicity. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) have emerged as promising platforms to overcome these challenges, offering high surface area, tunable pore size, and facile surface functionalization for efficient cargo loading. Therefore, in this work, the recent advances in the synthesis, structural control, and functional design of MSNs-based composites are systematically reviewed, with a focus on their biomedical applications in diagnosis (e.g., fluorescence imaging (FLI)/MRI/PET), therapy (e.g., chemo-, dynamic, thermal, and gas therapy), and tissue engineering. Key strategies for performance optimization and structure-property relationships are discussed in depth. Finally, we delineate prevailing challenges and future directions for the clinical translation of MSNs-based nanomaterials, providing an integrated perspective to guide their rational design and biomedical implementation.

works.title: A single-step injectable Janus-adhesive hydrogel for endoscopic gastrointestinal fistula repair
In-chip volumetric printing of perfusable and stretchable collagen-I scaffolds for mammary tissue models
works.abstract: Engineered epithelial models require three-dimensional extracellular matrix environments that support organized cell growth and allow independent access to luminal and basal compartments.However, many organ-on-chip (OoC) fabrication strategies rely on planar geometries, nonnative materials, or multi-step assembly workflows that limit architectural complexity and experimental control. Here, we report a direct in-chip volumetric printing strategy for fabricating stretchable and perfusable collagen-I scaffolds inside custom OoC devices. A vitamin C-regulated ruthenium/sodium persulfate photocrosslinking system enabled highfidelity printing of collagen-I into open-lumen architectures with ductal-and alveolar-inspired features. By generating scaffolds directly within the final culture device, this workflow eliminates post-print transfer and integrates defined collagen architectures with compartmentalized fluidic access and a mechanically actuable chip format. To support chipbased culture, printed collagen constructs were stabilized after fabrication using EDC/NHS chemistry, which limited thermally induced collagen densification, improved shape retention, and maintained scaffold anchorage during perfusion. The chip design provided separate access to the printed lumen and surrounding basal compartment, which enabled compartment-specific fluid handling while preserving scaffold integrity during inflation, stretching, and perfusion of the printed construct. On the collagen-I scaffolds, human milk-derived mammary epithelial cells formed epithelial layers with tight junctions and lactation associated markers. The platform further supported perfusion culture, in situ staining, and whole-chip volumetric imaging. Together, this work establishes direct in-chip collagen-I volumetric printing as a biofabrication strategy for creating perfusable epithelial tissue chips with native matrix architecture and compartment-specific fluidic access.

works.title: Silk-hyaluronic acid bioinks recreate a dynamic chondrogenic niche for stem cell differentiation and matrix-driven maturation in bioprinted cartilage models
works.abstract: Progress in cartilage engineering requires advanced tissue models capable of replicating the structural and cellular organisation of native tissue whilst supporting extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and functional tissue maturation. In this study, methacrylated silk fibroin (SFMA) and hyaluronic acid (HAMA) were combined into a dual-component, photopolymerisable biomaterial ink designed to recapitulate aspects of the biochemical composition and mechanical dynamics of the native cartilage ECM in bioprinted constructs. HAMA incorporation produced a denser, structurally stable hydrogel system, maintaining long-term stem cell viability and a rounded, chondrocyte-like cell morphology. Under inductive culture conditions, human mesenchymal stem cells underwent chondrogenic differentiation within SFMA-HAMA hydrogels, characterised by the expression of cartilage-associated markers including SOX9, COL2A1, and ACAN, and the deposition of a cartilaginous matrix containing sulphated glycosaminoglycans, collagen type II, and hyaluronic acid. Time-resolved mechanical analysis revealed progressive stiffening of cell-laden SFMA-HAMA constructs over 28 d, distinct from the intrinsic time-dependent mechanical changes observed in acellular hydrogels and temporally associated with cartilage-like ECM formation. Bioprinted constructs retained chondrogenic potential and construct shape fidelity following fabrication. This work demonstrates that SFMA-HAMA bioinks recreate a dynamic chondrogenic niche that supports stem cell chondrogenesis, cartilage-like ECM formation and construct maturation closely associated with cell-mediated matrix deposition-providing a foundation for the development of advanced bioprinted models for studying cartilage biology, disease modelling, and regenerative strategies.

works.title: Development of a Novel Anal-Fistula Plug Scaffold from Porcine Acellular Dermal Matrix/Hyaluronic Acid and Autologous Concentrated Growth Factor for Accelerating Fistula Healing
works.abstract: In this study, a novel fistula plug stent (ACGF@G-PADM/HA) was designed to accelerate fistula healing. The scaffold uses a composite matrix of porcine acellular matrix and hyaluronic acid (PADM/HA) as a three-dimensional porous collagen framework, which functions as the "structural support", and autologous concentrated growth factor (ACGF) is a highly concentrated bioactive agent extracted from the patient's own blood, rich in a variety of growth factors, acting as "functional agents". The as-developed ACGF@G-PADM/HA plug scaffold showed excellent mechanical strength, overcoming defects such as the fast gelation of fibrin glue and the fixed shape of the anal plug, which allowed it to conform to the irregular and complicated structures of the fistula. Simultaneously, the ACGF was employed to induce angiogenesis (neovascularization) and fibroblast proliferation, thereby attaining a synergistic effect in promoting fistula healing. The novel filling material was capable of effectively preventing bacterial contamination, promoting the proliferation of granulation tissue, and accelerating wound healing. This facilitated tissue remodeling and ensured the integration of the fistula plug with the host tissue prior to its expulsion. The study anticipates that this new filling material can be utilized as a potential fistula plug scaffold for fistula treatment.

works.title: Engineered Magnetic Nanoparticles for Dual-Modality Cancer Therapy: Advances in Hyperthermia and Magnetically Controlled Drug Delivery
works.abstract: Cancers remain among the most lethal diseases worldwide, accounting for a substantial proportion of human mortality. Despite significant advances, conventional therapeutic strategies are often limited by tumor microenvironment-mediated resistance, non-specific biodistribution, and severe systemic toxicity, underscoring the urgent need for more effective and targeted treatment modalities. Magnetic hyperthermia (MHT), coupled with magnetically guided drug delivery using biocompatible magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs), has emerged as a promising clinical approach for selective cancer therapy. This strategy enables precise localization at tumor sites, enhanced colloidal stability, and the effective preservation of surrounding healthy tissues. This review consolidates recent progress in the design, synthesis, and physicochemical characterization of MNPs developed for dual-modality cancer treatment. Various material platforms are critically examined, including iron oxide-based nanoparticles, ferromagnetic alloys, lanthanum strontium manganites, zirconium-based materials, carbon-based nanostructures, bioactive glasses, and glass-ceramic composites, with a particular emphasis on the structure-property correlations influencing magnetic performance and therapeutic outcomes. Key mechanisms governing alternating magnetic field-induced heat generation and thermally triggered drug release are discussed. The strategic tuning of the Curie temperature within biologically safe limits, combined with thermoresponsive surface functionalization, enables controlled hyperthermia and spatiotemporally regulated drug release. This integrated nanoplatform significantly enhances tumor selectivity while minimizing systemic toxicity.

works.title: Ultrasound-Triggered HSC Membrane-Cloaked Nanotherapeutics Attenuate Liver Fibrosis via Simultaneous Modulation of Mitophagic Flux and the TGF-β/Smad3 Cascade
works.abstract: This study presents an ultrasound-triggered therapeutic platform based on melatonin-loaded and perfluoropentane-encapsulated mesoporous silica nanoparticles, which are further cloaked with activated hepatic stellate cell membranes (HM-Mel@PFP-MSNs), designed for the precision treatment of liver fibrosis. This innovative drug delivery system leverages the inherent targeting properties of cell membrane coatings, effectively functioning as a "gatekeeper" that prevents premature drug release. By incorporating melatonin and perfluoropentane (PFP), our approach enables ultrasound-mediated controlled release, enhancing therapeutic efficacy. In vitro investigations revealed that upon ultrasound activation, HM-Mel@PFP-MSNs significantly inhibited the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and alleviated mitochondrial damage. Mechanistic studies employing Western blot analysis revealed that this nanotherapeutic strategy was associated with altered expression of autophagy-related proteins, including a reduced LC3-II/I ratio, increased P62 accumulation, and downregulated PINK1/Parkin. These findings suggest an overall suppression of autophagic activity, encompassing both general autophagy and mitophagy; however, a causal link remains to be established. Furthermore, using a rat model of liver fibrosis, robust histological assessments (including HE, Masson, Sirius Red, and α-SMA staining) demonstrated that our system markedly ameliorated fibrotic lesions under precise ultrasound guidance. This research introduces a novel strategy that integrates targeted delivery, controlled drug release, and visualizable therapeutic outcomes, thereby representing a significant advancement in the management of liver diseases. By simultaneously modulating mitophagic flux and the TGF-β/Smad3 signaling cascade, our HM-Mel@PFP-MSN-based nanotherapeutics open new avenues for liver fibrosis treatment, emphasizing the potential of leveraging ultrasound in enhancing therapeutic precision and efficacy.

works.title: MXene-Enabled Biomaterials for Wound Healing: Recent Advances, Mechanistic Insights, and Translational Prospects
works.abstract: The skin is the body's largest organ and its primary barrier against chemical, radiological, and microbial challenges. When wound healing is impaired or delayed, patients face significant clinical risks, including severe and potentially life-threatening complications. To address these challenges, a wide range of advanced dressing technologies such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), hydrogels, fibers, nanoparticles, and enzyme-based systems has been developed to support tissue repair and prevent infection. Many of these dressings incorporate bioactive components, including antibiotics, nanoparticles, and growth factors, to enhance therapeutic efficacy. Among emerging strategies, bioactive inorganic nanoparticles have drawn increasing attention for their ability to reinforce the regenerative functions of wound dressings. MXene-based nanoparticles show strong potential owing to their electrical conductivity, hydrophilicity, antibacterial activity, and biocompatibility. These features make MXenes promising building blocks for next-generation wound care materials. This review summarizes recent advances in integrating MXenes into MOFs, hydrogels, fibers, nanoparticle systems, and enzyme-based platforms. It also discusses the key factors that shape their performance, outlines strategies to improve their therapeutic effectiveness, and identifies priority research directions for accelerating the development and clinical translation of MXene-enabled biomaterials for wound healing.

works.title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects
works.abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

works.title: "Threefold dual" copper homeostasis regulation strategy: Targeted copper surge for enhanced cancer immunotherapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Copper-based therapeutics disrupting intracellular copper homeostasis hold immense promise for cancer immunotherapy, yet their efficacy is severely limited by inadequate copper accumulation, intratumoral antioxidant defenses, and nonspecific drug release. To surmount these limitations, we engineered CuTF-DC_AC50, an innovative copper homeostasis nanomodulator implementing a "threefold dual" strategy to maximize therapeutic outcomes. Specifically, the nanomodulator drives massive copper overload through a dual-channel influx and efflux regulation mechanism, concurrently delivering exogenous Cu 2+ and inhibiting ATOX1-mediated copper efflux via its DC_AC50 component. Simultaneously, it dismantles the intracellular antioxidant barrier through dual-mechanism glutathione (GSH) depletion, mediated by disulfide bond cleavage within the TPH scaffold alongside Cu 2+ reduction. Furthermore, CuTF-DC_AC50 undergoes dual-responsive degradation triggered by the acidic and GSH-abundant tumor microenvironment (TME), enabling precise drug release and spatial-temporal orchestration of the therapeutic cascade. This targeted copper surge synergistically triggers cuproptosis and pyroptosis, thereby robustly activating immunogenic cell death (ICD). Consequently, in vivo investigations demonstrate that this nanomodulator profoundly remodels the immunosuppressive TME, promotes robust immune cell infiltration, and substantially suppresses tumor growth. By exploiting the CuTF-DC_AC50-induced PD-L1 upregulation, its combination with αPD-L1 markedly amplifies therapeutic efficacy in CT26 tumor-bearing mice, establishing a highly programmable and clinically translatable combinatorial strategy for potentiated cancer immunotherapy.

works.title: Injectable thermoresponsive hydrogel integrating pH-responsive nanoparticles for antioxidant therapy of intervertebral disc degeneration
works.abstract: : Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is one of the leading causes of low back pain and spinal dysfunction, severely impairing patients’ quality of life and imposing a substantial societal burden. However, effective therapeutic strategies capable of fundamentally slowing or delaying disease progression remain lacking. Given the central role of oxidative stress in IVDD progression, the development of therapies with both antioxidant capacity and multi-target regulatory effects is of considerable importance. Previous studies have demonstrated that epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and metformin (MET) exert synergistic antioxidant and cytoprotective effects; however, their clinical application is limited by the low bioavailability of EGCG and the relatively weak antioxidant capacity of MET.In this study, EGCG–MET self-assembled polyphenolic nanoparticles (EMNP) were constructed via a Mannich reaction to enable synergistic delivery and functional enhancement of both agents. This nanosystem exhibits pH-responsive dissociation under acidic microenvironmental conditions, thereby facilitating on-demand drug release. Furthermore, EMNP were incorporated into a thermosensitive hydrogel composed of poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAAm) and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), fabricated via in situ free-radical polymerization (PNIPAAm–PVA hydrogel), to form an injectable, in situ gelling composite delivery system (TPP@EMNP). The phase-transition behavior of PNIPAAm enabled rapid gelation in vivo, while PVA enhanced mechanical stability and local retention.In an IVDD model, TPP@EMNP effectively scavenged reactive oxygen species, thereby attenuating degenerative processes at multiple levels. This strategy integrates pH-responsive self-assembled nanoparticles with a thermosensitive hydrogel-based delivery platform, offering a promising approach with potential clinical translational value for minimally invasive treatment of IVDD.

works.title: Restorative endothelium and polarization-assisted inflammatory regulation nanomedicine (REPAIR) for acute lung injury treatment
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Acute lung injury (ALI) is marked by uncontrolled inflammation and excessive immune cell infiltration, ultimately causing endothelial barrier disruption and impaired pulmonary function. To counteract these pathological processes, we develop a Restorative Endothelium and Polarization-Assisted Inflammatory Regulation nanomedicine (REPAIR) that integrates endothelial protection with alveolar macrophage reprogramming. REPAIR is fabricated by loading the P2X7 receptor‌ (P2X7R) antagonist A740003 into apoptotic NIH3T3 cell vesicles (Apo-Vesicles), thereby combining apoptotic cell-derived “eat-me” signals with targeted inhibition of P2X7R-mediated inflammatory pathways. Benefiting from its apoptotic cell-mimetic surface, REPAIR exhibits markedly enhanced uptake by alveolar macrophages (AMs), driving the transition of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. At the same time, the released A740003 efficiently suppresses P2X7R activation, preventing macrophage necrosis and preserving endothelial vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin to maintain vascular barrier integrity. In vitro and in vivo studies further confirm that REPAIR substantially reduces inflammatory cytokine production, limits macrophage necrosis, and stabilizes endothelial junctions through the synergistic interplay of apoptotic mimicry and P2X7R antagonism. These results highlight REPAIR as a promising and mechanistically comprehensive nanotherapeutic strategy for ALI and other inflammation-driven pulmonary diseases.

works.title: Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration
works.abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro . GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

works.title: Biomimetic Hf-MOF/Mn3O4 STING nanoagonist potentiates radio-immunotherapy by remodeling tumor microenvironment and activating cGAS-STING pathway
works.abstract: Tumor hypoxia and immunosuppression not only drive radioresistance in cancer radiotherapy but also compromise the efficacy of immunotherapy. Here, a biomimetic core–shell nanoagonist (CM/HPM) integrating a radiosensitizing hafnium-based metal-organic framework (Hf-MOF) core with a tumor microenvironment (TME)-responsive Mn 3 O 4 shell is reported to orchestrate robust radio-immunotherapy. The Hf-MOF core serves as a powerful radiosensitizer, enhancing localized radiation energy deposition and amplifying radiation-induced DNA damage. The Mn 3 O 4 shell exhibits multienzyme-mimicking activities, catalyzing oxygen generation to relieve hypoxia, depleting glutathione to amplify oxidative stress, and releasing Mn 2+ ions upon TME-triggered degradation. The liberated Mn 2+ acts as a critical immune co-agonist, sensitizing cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) to cytosolic DNA fragments from Hf-MOF-enhanced radiotherapy, thereby synergistically activating the cGAS-STING pathway. Moreover, the cancer-cell-membrane coating enables homologous targeting and facilitates uptake by both tumor cells and immune cells. In bilateral 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, CM/HPM combined with X-ray irradiation ablates primary tumors and evokes a potent abscopal effect, suppressing distant tumors via enhanced intratumoral T-cell infiltration and dendritic cell (DC) maturation. This synergistic nanoplatform overcomes radioresistance and elicits systemic antitumor immunity, offering a promising paradigm for metastatic cancer therapy.

works.title: Transcription activator-like effector base editing delivered by a targeted lipid nanoparticle for therapy of lung cancer
Stress-relaxing and ROS-scavenging hydrogel microspheres restore osteoimmune homeostasis for bone regeneration under mechanoinflammatory conditions
works.abstract: Periodontitis drives alveolar bone loss, tooth mobility, and even tooth loss. Although orthodontic treatment can reposition compromised teeth and extend their functional lifespan, orthodontic tooth movement in patients with periodontitis occurs within a mechanoinflammatory microenvironment, where mechanical forces and persistent inflammation synergistically disrupt alveolar bone homeostasis and compromise stem-cell-mediated repair, culminating in bone loss. Breaking this vicious cycle demands a therapy that can simultaneously buffer physical stress and neutralize biochemical insults. Here we report injectable, stress-relaxing, and ROS-scavenging hydrogel microspheres that function as a protective microniche for dental follicle stem cells (DFSCs). Constructed from dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid and phenylboronic acid-modified gelatin, these viscoelastic microspheres rapidly dissipate mechanical stress while their catechol moieties mitigate oxidative damage. Under a combined mechanoinflammatory challenge, the microspheres preserved DFSC viability, stemness, osteogenic potential, and immunomodulatory function. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the microspheres rescued the expression of the DNA repair enzyme OGG1, thereby preventing oxidative DNA damage and suppressing the downstream NF-κB inflammatory cascade. In a murine model of periodontitis-associated orthodontic tooth movement, DFSCs-loaded microspheres not only prevented bone loss but also restored a pro-regenerative osteoimmune homeostasis. Together, this study presents a viscoelastic and redox-active biomaterial-based strategy to safeguard stem cell function and restore osteoimmune balance in mechanically and immunologically challenged tissues.

works.title: Engineering Antigen Density on M13 Bacteriophage for Personalized Nanovaccine
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanovaccines have been engineered to co‐deliver antigens and adjuvants for robust immune responses. While extensive studies have examined the effect of nanovaccine size, shape, surface charge, and targeting on vaccine efficacy, the impact of antigen density remains underexplored. Here, we systematically optimize the anti‐tumor CD8 + T cell response by modulating the antigen density on an M13 phage‐based nanovaccine. By fine‐tuning the antigen ratio from ∼6.0% to ∼70.4% on the phage capsid, the anti‐tumor CD8 + T cell response was enhanced. Further investigation demonstrated that the antigen density affected not only antigen presentation efficacy but also dendritic cell uptake. Applying this strategy to a neoantigen in the MC‐38 colorectal cancer model, we achieved up to a ∼7‐fold increase in the neoantigen‐specific CD8 + T cell frequency, resulting in significant tumor suppression. These findings underscore the critical role of antigen density in nanovaccine design and establish M13 bacteriophage as a universal platform for personalized cancer vaccine applications.

works.title: Peri‐Infarct Cortical Network Remapping During Stroke Recovery via a Soft Liquid Metal Neural Interface
works.abstract: Stroke causes substantial reorganization of neural activity and connectivity in the peri-infarct cortex during functional recovery. Tracking these changes at high resolution, however, remains difficult. Mechanical mismatch of conventional rigid neural probes is exacerbated in the fragile peri-infarct region, destabilizing the tissue-electrode interface and limiting long-term recording. Here, we present a fully soft, liquid metal-based multichannel neural interface that enables stable electrophysiological recording in freely moving mice. Using this platform, we performed longitudinal recordings before and after ischemic stroke, enabling within-animal comparisons. We applied complementary analyses of population-level latent dynamics and functional connectivity, capturing network-level coordination and pairwise interactions. Both analyses revealed acute suppression followed by partial recovery without restoration of the pre-stroke state. Instead, neural networks reorganized into a distinct and reproducible functional configuration. These findings establish soft liquid metal neural interfaces combined with population-level analysis as a useful approach for resolving neural reorganization during stroke recovery.

works.title: Closing the loop on blood flow control in spinal cord injury
Optimal closed-loop feedback control of blood flow after spinal cord injury with norepinephrine
works.abstract: After spinal cord injury, clinical management aims to support tissue perfusion, but current methods rely on the indirect control of arterial blood pressure without direct measurement of the local blood flow. This limits the ability to tailor drug delivery to the injured tissue. Here, we show that spinal cord blood flow can be regulated using a closed-loop controller that adjusts vasopressor infusion on the basis of real-time ultrasound flow measurement. We characterize the dynamic relationship between drug infusion, arterial pressure and spinal cord blood flow, and we use these data to design a feedback controller that targets a predefined flow level. We validate the system in simulations, implement the controller in real time in rodents and translate it to pigs. We show that the controller reduced blood flow deviations and variability compared with constant dosing and supported functional recovery in a rodent survival model. These results show a closed-loop spinal cord perfusion control strategy that leverages clinically available measurements and pharmacological interventions, supporting its translation to clinical settings for the management of acute spinal cord injury.

works.title: Microfiber-Reinforced GelMA Hydrogels with Tunable Poisson's Ratio Enhance Chondrogenesis under Dynamic Loading
works.abstract: Hydrogels are widely used in cartilage tissue engineering but fail to replicate key mechanical features of native cartilage, particularly its near-zero Poisson's ratio, which governs lateral deformation under load. Here, we demonstrate that matching deformation behavior in addition to compressive stiffness may contribute to the enhanced chondrogenic response under physiological mechanical stimulation. Human articular chondrocytes were encapsulated in GelMA hydrogels reinforced with melt electrowritten scaffolds engineered to independently tune the effective compressive modulus and Poisson's ratio. Reinforcement increased the compressive modulus from 33 kPa (neat GelMA) to 245-345 kPa, while reducing the Poisson's ratio from 0.42 to 0.12 in hybrid designs, approaching native cartilage values. Under dynamic loading, constructs matching both properties showed significantly higher expression of the chondrogenic markers SOX9 and ACAN compared to both neat GelMA and lattice-reinforced constructs, which exhibited a physiologically relevant compressive modulus but a higher Poisson's ratio, along with increased COL2A1 expression compared to the latter specifically. Histological analysis confirmed enhanced and more homogeneous extracellular matrix deposition, with up to 76% GAG and 36% collagen type II coverage. These findings suggest that lateral deformation behavior, alongside compressive stiffness, contributes to directing chondrocyte matrix synthesis under mechanical stimulation, establishing Poisson's ratio as an important and previously underexplored design parameter in cartilage tissue engineering, and providing a framework for engineering mechanically instructive biomaterials for load-bearing tissues.

works.title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived spheroids and microtissues for biofabrication: advances in bioassembly and bioprinting strategies
works.abstract: Abstract Biofabrication integrates biological and engineering principles to generate functional tissues for regenerative medicine, drug screening, and disease modeling. Among the diverse cellular sources available, mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have emerged as a critical component due to their multipotency, immunomodulatory capacity, and scalability. This review focuses on MSC-derived spheroids and microtissues as building blocks for biofabrication, organizing recent advances in bioassembly and bioprinting strategies around the axis of undifferentiated versus pre-differentiated microtissues and how the timing of differentiation shapes construct functionality. Key technological innovations, including dynamic culture systems, scaffold-free assembly, and high-resolution bioprinting (e.g. droplet-based), have enabled enhanced control over microtissue maturation and structural fidelity. The role of the cellular microenvironment in determining MSC fate is examined, emphasizing how biochemical cues, mechanical properties, and oxygen gradients can be engineered during microtissue formation. Cellular heterogeneity is addressed as a path-dependent variable continuously reshaped by donor-specific factors (age, sex, health status) and process-imposed cues (isolation methods, expansion conditions, and mechanical stress) throughout the in vitro life cycle, and concrete mitigation strategies are discussed, including prospective cell sorting and a proposed functional potency panel (extracellular matrix deposition, fusion competence, and secretome profiling), alongside recent advancements in automated and machine learning-based biofabrication platforms. Vascularization and immunological integration are examined as central translation bottlenecks, covering endothelial co-culture, prevascularized spheroids, sacrificial bioprinting, and MSC-driven modulation of the host immune response. By integrating the fabrication route, heterogeneity as a manufacturing process variable, and translational/regulatory bottlenecks into a single framework, this review highlights recent advances, discusses current limitations, and outlines future directions for clinical translation of MSC-based biofabrication.

works.title: Sono-enzymatically engineered tannic acid/doxycycline-lignin nanoparticles enable self-assembled bioactive chitosan hydrogels for chronic wound healing
works.abstract: Chronic wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to their multifactorial pathology, characterised by excessive proteolytic and oxidative enzyme activity, persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, and biofilm formation. Here, we report a green, nano-enabled hydrogel fabricated through the in situ self-assembly of thiolated chitosan (TCS), driven by tannic acid/doxycycline-functionalised lignin nanoparticles (PLD NPs). Doxycycline was incorporated at a sub-inhibitory concentration (12.5 μg/mL), enabling PLD NPs (0.5 mg/mL) to inhibit matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) activity by approximately 50% without inducing antibacterial effects. Dynamic interactions between the polymer network and NPs produced injectable, self-healing hydrogels capable of stimuli-responsive NPs release under chronic wound-like conditions, including variations in pH, hydrogen peroxide, and lysozyme. Ex vivo evaluation using human chronic wound exudates demonstrated potent inhibition of MMP and myeloperoxidase activities by 73% and 80%, respectively. The hydrogels further exhibited strong antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , achieving 4.8- and 4.3-log reductions in bacterial viability while preventing 73% and 65% of biofilm formation, respectively. In vitro studies confirmed excellent biocompatibility with human keratinocytes and fibroblasts, together with up to 82% cellular antioxidant activity and enhanced fibroblast migration. Importantly, in an in vivo full-thickness S. aureus -infected mouse wound model, the hydrogels achieved complete wound closure within 18 days, outperforming commercial antiseptic treatments. Overall, this work demonstrates a multifunctional hydrogel platform that simultaneously modulates the chronic wound microenvironment, controls infection and biofilm formation, reduces oxidative stress, and promotes tissue regeneration, offering a promising strategy for advanced chronic wound management.

works.title: Progress and applications of microneedle-based gene therapy
works.abstract: Gene therapy holds considerable promise for treating a wide range of intractable diseases through the modification of specific genes. However, gene therapeutics such as plasmid DNA, messenger RNA, and CRISPR-based systems are susceptible to degradation, face challenges in crossing cellular barriers, and may induce immune-related adverse effects, thereby limiting their clinical translation. Microneedles create microchannels that penetrate tissue barriers and, when combined with various carrier materials, enhance nucleic acid stability and intracellular delivery efficiency. This review summarizes the compatibility of different microneedle configurations with gene-delivery vectors, compares the effects of various fabrication processes on the activity of therapeutic agents, and elucidates the mechanisms underlying barrier penetration and delivery by microneedles. Recent advances in the application of microneedle-based gene therapy in dermatology, oncology, and nucleic acid vaccination are also discussed. Finally, current challenges, including drug loading, mass production, and safety evaluation, are analyzed, and the prospects for smart, responsive, and integrated diagnostic and therapeutic microneedles are highlighted.

works.title: Biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip: Real-time visualisation of biomaterial thrombosis at clinical heparin levels
works.abstract: Blood-contacting medical device thrombosis causes device failure, embolism and bleeding due to reliance on anti-thrombotic drugs. The interplay between biological, material and flow parameters in medical device thrombosis remains poorly understood. Importantly, tools to evaluate acute, dynamic thrombotic events on materials in real-time are lacking, impacting the successful development and translation of new anti-thrombotic materials. We developed a biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip model to evaluate acute material thrombogenicity in real-time using human whole blood, mimicking clinical heparin doses (0.5-5 U/mL) and shear rates (50-2000 s -1 ). System validation showed expected platelet adhesion on hydrophilic glass and platelet passivation and detachment at increasing shears on hydrophobic silicone. For the first time, we characterised fibrin events on materials, finding a shear dependent decrease on glass but not silicone, pre-coating materials with albumin abolished fibrin on silicone but not glass, and inhibition of FXIIa reduced but did not abolish fibrin on either material. More and larger fibrin events (aggregation and channel occlusion) occurred at 0.5 U/mL compared to 5 U/mL heparin, and the heparin level did not affect platelet adhesion dynamics. Glass showed the most severe fibrin events, followed by polyvinyl chloride (PVC) > silicone > polycarbonate. Most fibrin events occurred in association with platelets and although platelets were P-selectin positive, very few platelets were procoagulant (P-selectin and Annexin V positive). This clinically relevant, biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip model could allow biomaterial thrombosis mechanism elucidation and fast-track evaluation and development of anti-thrombotic materials to improve medical device function and reduce adverse thrombotic and bleeding patient outcomes.

works.title: Charge-neutralized anti-swelling hydrogels enable mechano-curvature-coupled microphysiological system
3D-Printed Microneedles for Periodontal and Oral Mucosal Therapy: A Systematic Review of Therapeutic and Fabrication Strategies
works.abstract: Microneedles (MNs) technologies have emerged as a promising platform for localized drug delivery in the mouth, offering minimally invasive access to the oral mucosa, including gingival tissues. However, their integration with advanced additive manufacturing remains underexplored, despite the need for high-precision, patient-specific devices that can overcome the limitations of conventional pharmacotherapy. This review analyzes the recent developments in 3D-printed MNs for intraoral drug delivery, focusing on polymeric designs enabled by stereolithography, digital light processing, continuous liquid interface production, and two-photon polymerization. High-resolution vat-photopolymerization systems demonstrate superior spatial resolution and fabrication accuracy, allowing the reproducible production of MNs geometries with optimized tip radii, internal channels, and drug-loading microstructures. MNs-mediated delivery of antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and healing-promoting agents demonstrates potential not only for the management of periodontal inflammation, oral mucosal lesions, and soft-tissue defects but also for preventive interventions in early-stage diseases and for the control of recurrence. Despite these advances, major barriers persist, including limited in vivo validation under dynamic oral conditions, insufficient mechanical assessment under masticatory forces and salivary flow, and a lack of standardized regulatory frameworks for intraoral MNs devices. Overall, the current findings indicate that 3D-printed MNs represent an emerging and highly promising class of localized therapeutic delivery systems for the management of conditions affecting the periodontal tissues and the oral mucosa, with substantial opportunities for technological refinement and clinical translation.

works.title: Bioinspired Hydroxyapatite-Mineralized Silk Fibroin/Ionic Liquid Interpenetrating Hydrogels for Biomedical Applications
works.abstract: Surgical site infection remains a critical barrier to successful bone tissue engineering, and silk fibroin (SF)-based scaffolds, despite their excellent biocompatibility, lack intrinsic antibacterial activity. Here, we report a multifunctional biohybrid nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates methacrylated silk fibroin (SFMA) with an antibacterial imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer, 1-vinyl-3-hexylimidazolium bromide ([C6VIm]Br), fabricated via a bioinspired bidirectional freeze-casting strategy followed by in situ biomineralization with hydroxyapatite (HAp). Successful methacrylation (degree of substitution = 35%) and ionic liquid synthesis were confirmed by NMR spectroscopy, while FT-IR, TGA/DTG, and XRD analyses verified the formation of the interpenetrating SF/IL network and progressive HAp deposition, with mineral content rising from 12.1 to 32.9 wt % over successive mineralization cycles. SEM imaging and elemental mapping revealed a highly interconnected, anisotropic porous architecture with uniform calcium/phosphorus distribution, closely emulating native bone microstructure, and mineralization enhanced the swelling capacity to approximately 170%. Biologically, the ionic liquid component conferred potent, additive-free antibacterial activity against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, while HAp incorporation improved MG-63 osteoblast-like cell adhesion and the viability of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), with MSC viability exceeding 120% of the control in the mineralized sample. All formulations exhibited hemolysis well below accepted safety limits, confirming excellent hemocompatibility. By combining intrinsic antibacterial function, bioinspired anisotropic architecture, and biomimetic mineralization within a single platform, this work offers a promising, metal- and antibiotic-free strategy for infection-resistant scaffolds for bone tissue engineering, with significant potential for advancing bone tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

works.title: A TGF-β1-Binding and Stem Cell-Homing Peptide Hydrogel Loaded with BMSC-Exosomes Enhances the Endogenous Repair of Surgically Induced Osteochondral Defects
works.abstract: To address the poor self-repair capacity of experimental osteochondral defects and the inefficacy of conventional hydrogels, this study developed a biodegradable peptide hydrogel, Exos@TRM. This study used an acute surgically created osteochondral defect model in rats, which does not fully reproduce experimental cartilage defects or chronic human cartilage degeneration. Based on the RADA16 framework, this hydrogel incorporates a TGF-β1-binding peptide and a stem cell-recruiting motif, and is loaded with exosomes derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In vitro experiments demonstrated that Exos@TRM effectively binds TGF-β1, promotes BMSC migration, and enables sustained exosome release for up to one week, thereby facilitating BMSC proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation. In a rat cartilage defect model, Exos@TRM reduced pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages, recruited endogenous TGF-β1 and BMSCs to the injury site, promoted chondrogenic differentiation at week 3, and achieved tissue regeneration resembling natural cartilage with functional mechanical properties by week 8. Mechanistic studies confirmed that the regenerative effects are TGF-β1-dependent, and comprehensive biosafety evaluation revealed no systemic toxicity. This study demonstrates that Exos@TRM achieves significant cartilage repair without exogenous cells or high-dose growth factors through synergistic immunomodulation, localized TGF-β1 recruitment, and stem cell homing, offering a clinically promising strategy for experimental cartilage defects.

works.title: Electroconductive patch promotes heart repair by directing epicardial cells toward endothelial fate
Organoids and organs-on-a-chip as new approach methodologies at the convergence of cell biology and bioengineering
EPCR expression marks CD150neg deeply dormant long-term hematopoietic stem cells
works.abstract: Cell surface expression of the Slam family member CD150 is widely used for the prospective isolation of multipotent long-term hematopoietic stem cells (LT-HSCs). Here, we identify a bona fide endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR) + CD150 − HSC subset, termed LT-HSC2, that sustains serial multi-lineage reconstitution. Long-term label-retaining assays reveal that LT-HSC2s are more deeply dormant than conventional EPCR + CD150 + LT-HSC1s, exhibit reduced cell cycle activation in response to inflammatory stress, and preserve stemness for prolonged periods in vivo . Moreover, combining EPCR with established HSC and multipotent progenitor (MPP) markers resolves the earliest stages of lineage divergence toward megakaryocytic/erythroid-biased CD150 + and lymphoid-biased CD150 − trajectories. Thus, EPCR expression in HSCs and MPPs is associated with increased stemness, whereas CD150 expression does not encompass the full spectrum of long-term repopulating HSCs. Our findings establish EPCR + CD150 − LT-HSC2s as a distinct, exceptionally dormant stem-cell subset and reveal an additional layer of HSC heterogeneity governing self-renewal, decreased stress sensitvity. and earliest lineage priming.

works.title: Developing precision nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems for Alzheimer's disease therapy
works.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an irreversible neurodegenerative disease that has thus far suffered from unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes. Despite ongoing research into AD pathogenesis and related drugs, few disease-modifying therapies are currently available. Moreover, efficient drug delivery is significantly hindered by low permeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and non-specific distribution within the brain, further limiting the efficacy of existing anti-AD medications. Nanotechnology has recently emerged as a promising approach to overcome these challenges. This review aims to offer a comprehensive overview of recent advances in precision nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems for AD therapy. First, we outline the multiple pathological mechanisms and representative pathogenesis-inspired therapies of AD. Next, we summarize various types of nanoparticles that have been utilized in AD drug delivery, including polymeric, lipid-based, inorganic, and biomimetic nanocarriers. Subsequently, we highlight the nanoparticle-mediated strategies for cascaded precision drug delivery at different levels, focusing on both the BBB and specific pathologies or cell populations within AD lesions. Finally, we discuss potential challenges and prospects in employing precision delivery systems, aiming to accelerate the development and clinical translation of nanoparticle-based therapies for AD.

3D model to study the immunomodulatory functions of adipocyte/T lymphocytes paracrine crosstalk
works.abstract: studies investigating adipocyte-immune interactions rely on simplified two-dimensional systems that incompletely recapitulate human AT physiology. Here, we developed a patient-derived three-dimensional (3D) human adiposphere model to investigate adipocyte-T-cell crosstalk under controlled metabolic conditions. Adipospheres were generated from the stromal vascular fraction of human subcutaneous AT obtained from donors with clinically distinct metabolic profile. Following 3D adipogenic maturation under normogenic or obesogenic conditions, adipospheres retained donor-specific adipogenic and metabolic characteristics during long-term culture, as demonstrated by differential expression of adipogenic markers, insulin-responsive AKT signaling and lipolytic activity. Compared with normogenic maturation condition, obesogenic maturation induced marked alterations in adiposphere morphology, cytokine secretion and metabolic function. In a second step, mature adipospheres were co-cultured with activated blood-derived T cells using a Transwell-based paracrine system. T-cells co-culture further modulated adiposphere inflammatory and metabolic- related responses. Transcriptomic analyses revealed coordinated regulation of immune- and metabolism related pathways, indicating extensive transcriptional remodeling during adipocyte-T-cell crosstalk. Overall, this modular 3D adiposphere platform reproduces key features of human AT immunometabolic interactions while preserving donor-specific responses. The system provides a flexible framework for integrating additional cellular components and may facilitate future mechanistic studies and therapeutic screening approaches targeting obesity-associated metabolic and inflammatory disorders.

works.title: In Vitro Human Arteriole Microphysiological System with Physiological Scale and Functional Vasoactivity Enabled by a Dual Material Fabrication Strategy
works.abstract: Arterioles are the principal regulators of vascular tone, yet their small size and deep tissue location hinder direct investigation of their roles in microvascular disease. To address this, we developed a human microphysiological arteriole distinguished from previous models by simultaneously integrating an arteriole-scale caliber (~200 μm), continuous perfusion culture, and active vasoactivity. The vessel autonomously forms and matures under flow through a spatially regulated coating strategy that eliminates post-seeding manipulation. The engineered vessels exhibit vasoactivity in response to both biochemical and metabolic cues. In particular, the metabolic response is a physiological form of vasoactivity rarely reproduced in previous in vitro systems. Leveraging the ease of sample harvesting, proteomic profiling and mechanical testing indicated that flow-induced maturation promotes a contractile phenotype consistent with arteriogenesis-like remodeling. This accessible platform provides a versatile tool for studying arteriolar physiology and microvascular remodeling.

works.title: Engineering the synovial lining–sublining architecture in a human 3D model to study macrophage–fibroblast interactions in arthritis
works.abstract: Abstract The synovial membrane is a key regulator of joint homeostasis, inflammation, and tissue remodeling, yet human in vitro models that reproduce its spatial organization while enabling controlled investigation of macrophage–fibroblast-like stromal cell (FLS) interactions remain limited. Here, we developed a xeno-free, spatially organized 3D synovial membrane model that reconstructs the structural relationship between the macrophage lining and fibroblast-rich sublining compartment. The model was generated by establishing an apically organized macrophage-containing lining-like compartment on a transwell membrane, followed by stepwise assembly of FLS laden hydrogel constructs. Hydrogel screening identified a 1:3 VitroGel® RGD formulation as the most suitable condition to support FLS viability, homogeneous cell distribution, and stable tissue organization. Experimentally induced M1-like and M2-like macrophages were incorporated, and the model was stimulated with TNF- α , TGF- β , or Osteoarthritis (OA) synovial fluid (SF). Cytotoxicity, proliferation, metabolic activity, gene expression, and cytokine secretion were analyzed. Pharmacological responsiveness was evaluated using adalimumab and 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI). The spatially organized construct enabled compartment-specific analysis of macrophage–FLS communication. M1-like macrophages induced inflammatory FLS responses characterized by elevated IL1B, IL6, TNFA , and MMP1 expression, whereas M2-like macrophages promoted matrix-remodeling and myofibroblast-related programs, including increased TGFB and ACTA2 expression. Exposure to OA-SF and cytokine stimulation induced FLS hyperproliferation, metabolic adaptation, and distinct transcriptional responses. Treatment with adalimumab suppressed TNF-driven inflammatory responses, whereas 4-OI reduced selected inflammatory markers and altered remodeling-associated responses. Together, these findings establish a spatially organized, xeno-free 3D synovial membrane model as a defined and experimentally tractable platform for studying macrophage–FLS communication and synovial activation. By combining physiologically inspired tissue organization with compartment-specific analysis, the model provides a human in vitro platform for investigating OA-associated inflammatory and remodeling processes and evaluating pharmacological modulation under defined experimental conditions.

works.title: Linking Circulating Metal Levels to Cytokine Signatures in Total Joint Arthroplasty Patients
works.abstract: Arthroplasty may significantly improve the quality of life; however, wear and corrosion of metallic biomaterials can lead to the release of metal ions and particles, contributing to immune responses. Circulating metals may influence cytokine production, but systemic biomarkers of implant-related inflammation remain elusive. This study aimed to quantify systemic metal levels and cytokines to identify potential immunological signatures in patients exposed to arthroplasty metals. Peripheral blood samples from 150 patients scheduled for either primary or revision arthroplasty were analyzed. Whole blood multi-metal levels were quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. Plasma levels of 47 cytokines were quantified using a bead-based multiplex immunoassay. Cytokine patterns were examined via clustering and correlated with metal levels, adjusting for age, sex, prosthetic joint infection, lymphocyte count, C-reactive protein levels, and season. Blood levels of cobalt, chromium, titanium, niobium, and zirconium were significantly elevated in patients with arthroplasty implants, compared to arthroplasty-naïve controls. Selective correlations were observed, notably cobalt with IL-8 and multiple metals with IL-15. Cytokine clustering identified four distinct modules representing systemic immune activity. Multivariable linear regression modeling revealed associations of metal exposure with IL-1RA, IL-8, IL-15, and the proinflammatory cluster after adjusting for age, sex, periprosthetic joint infection status, inflammation markers, and season. This study shows that arthroprosthetic metal exposure is associated with systemic elevation of selective cytokines. Blood-based cytokine profiles may serve as biomarkers for monitoring implant-related immune activation, providing insights into mechanisms of systemic inflammation, yet must be interpreted within the context of multifactorial influences.

works.title: Phage-Derived Depolymerase-Functionalized Coatings Prevent Staphylococcal Biofilm Formation
works.abstract: Biofilm-associated infections caused by Staphylococci remain a major challenge in the context of biomedical implants due to their tolerance to antibiotics and resistance to host defenses. Here, we report the identification of a novel phage-derived depolymerase (DPO2) targeting staphylococcal biofilms and its integration into hyaluronic acid-based layer-by-layer (LbL) coatings. DPO2 was produced recombinantly and proved more effective preventing biofilm formation than destroying preformed Staphylococcus epidermidis biofilms. DPO2 antibiofilm activity was retained and even enhanced upon immobilization within DPO2/Hyaluronic Acid multilayered coatings. The resulting functionalized surfaces exhibited potent inhibition of biofilm formation by multiple S. epidermidis and Staphylococcus aureus strains from orthopedic infections, reaching nearly complete suppression under the tested conditions. This work demonstrates the potential of combining phage-derived enzymes with biomaterial surface engineering to develop efficient, non-antibiotic antibiofilm strategies. Such coatings represent a promising approach for preventing implant-associated infections.

works.title: Dynamic Bond-Mediated Self-Adaptive Injectable Conductive Hydrogels for Peripheral Nerve Regeneration
works.abstract: Injectable conductive hydrogels show promise for peripheral nerve regeneration. However, a trade-off exists between mechanical adaptability and stable electrical conductivity, limiting their therapeutic effectiveness. To overcome this limitation, a self-adaptive injectable hydrogel (AuSeGD) was developed. It features a hierarchical dynamic network comprising weak diselenide (Se-Se) bonds and strong gold-selenium (Au-Se) coordination bonds. The Se-Se bonds dissipate mechanical stress, while the Au-Se bonds maintain the integrity of the conductive framework. AuSeGD is created through UV-initiated polymerization of methacrylated gelatin, a diselenide-containing crosslinker, and gold nanoparticles. It exhibits shear-thinning injectability, rapid self-healing, moderate tissue adhesion, and stable electrical conductivity under repeated mechanical loading. In vitro studies demonstrate support for Schwann cell viability and excellent hemocompatibility. In a rat sciatic nerve crush injury model, AuSeGD forms an integrated electroactive bridge, accelerating axonal regeneration and remyelination. This is evidenced by increased expression of neurofilament and myelin basic protein, thicker myelin sheaths, and an optimized G-ratio. The structural repair leads to motor functional recovery, improving the sciatic function index and reducing gastrocnemius muscle atrophy. This bond strategy effectively balances adaptability and conductivity, offering a versatile material platform for electroactive biomaterials in complex tissue repair.

works.title: Multifunctional Three-Dimensional-Printed Bio-Ink from Waterborne Polyurethane and Natural Antioxidants for Advanced Wound Dressings
works.abstract: The development of multifunctional wound dressings capable of simultaneously addressing oxidative stress, bacterial infection, and tissue regeneration remains a major challenge in advanced wound care. Here, we report a printable, bioactive 3D-printed dressing based on a synergistic bio-ink composed of waterborne polyurethane (WPU), pomegranate peel-derived antioxidant polyphenols (POM), and TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibrils (TOCNF). POM was incorporated into the WPU matrix during in situ polymerization to introduce pomegranate peel-derived antioxidant and antibacterial functionality, while TOCNF served as a rheology modifier enabling extrusion-based direct ink writing. The resulting ink exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behavior, rapid viscosity recovery, and tunable yield stress, enabling successful, stable extrusion-based printing of multilayer architectures. Printed freeze-dried wound dressings exhibited highly interconnected porous structures (>90% porosity), robust swelling capacity, structural integrity under physiological conditions, and compressive stability after hydration. The incorporation of POM enhanced antibacterial performance against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli and provided strong free-radical scavenging activity. In vitro studies using HaCaT keratinocytes confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, enhanced metabolic activity, and significant attenuation of H2O2-induced oxidative stress. Notably, this wound dressing reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species levels and improved cell survival under oxidative challenge. This work establishes a strategy for integrating natural antioxidant bioactives into printable polyurethane networks to produce structurally programmable, biologically active wound dressings. The combination of rheologically optimized printability, hierarchical porosity, and multifunctional bioactivity highlights the potential of this platform for advanced wound-dressing applications and other oxidative-stress-related tissue-repair strategies.

works.title: Lifecycle tissue engineering: An AI-enabled multimodal sensing and digital twin roadmap
works.abstract: The clinical translation of tissue engineering (TE) is critically hampered by the absence of real-time, non-invasive monitoring throughout the entire lifecycle of tissue fabrication and repair. Current reliance on end-point assessments obscures dynamic biological events, making early detection of deviations and failures challenging. While multimodal sensing offers rich data streams, inherent issues such as long-term drift, noise accumulation, and difficulties in cross-modality comparability impede their transformation into reliable process metrics and actionable insights. This review introduces a novel, comprehensive four-layer framework consisting of Problem, Data, Model, and Application Evidence, to systematically integrate artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled multimodal sensing across the full TE lifecycle. The Problem Layer delineates critical biological uncertainties and monitoring requirements. The Data Layer surveys diverse in vitro and in vivo observables, sensing modalities, and readout strategies. The Model Layer bridges data acquisition with decision-making, emphasizing AI's role in signal processing, feature extraction, data fusion, and predictive analytics for early failure identification and outcome prediction. The Application Evidence Layer synthesizes current evidence, showcasing AI and sensing applications in donor or cell screening, in vitro process optimization, post-implantation quantitative readout, longitudinal assessment, and diagnostic prediction. This framework moves beyond fragmented approaches by proposing a unified architecture for lifecycle TE, addressing a significant gap in existing literature. We further delineate a strategic roadmap for clinical translation, underscoring the imperative for standardization, long-term reliability, unified evaluation protocols, and responsible AI development. By distinguishing demonstrated technologies from integration steps that remain conceptual or require TE-specific validation, this review outlines a structured roadmap for moving TE monitoring from isolated readouts toward more predictive, traceable, and verifiable translational workflows.

works.title: Disrupting the cholesterol–mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma
works.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor–stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol–mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo , FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

works.title: Injectable self-healing hydrogel delivering trispecific engineered exosomes for osteoporotic bone regeneration via activating mitophagy
works.abstract: Osteoporotic bone defects are characterized by impaired matrix remodeling, diminished osteogenic potential, and insufficient vascularization, posing major challenges for tissue regeneration. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSCs-Exos) have shown promise in promoting osteogenesis and angiogenesis, but their clinical translation is limited by rapid clearance and lack of targeted delivery. Here, we report the development of an injectable, self-healing SK/HA@A hydrogel for sustained delivery of trispecific RNA-engineered exosomes (Tri-Exos) targeting IL31, CELA1, and PCOLCE2. Tri-Exos were engineered via electroporation and rigorously characterized for morphology, size, marker expression, cellular uptake, and functional regulation of target genes in BMSCs. The hydrogel exhibited rapid gelation, robust mechanical properties, dynamic self-healing, and sustained release of Tri-Exos over 30 days. In vitro, SK/HA@A@EVs significantly enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, matrix mineralization, and HUVEC angiogenic responses, while simultaneously activating mitophagy-mediated mitochondrial regulation and autophagy-associated survival pathways, which are critical for maintaining cellular homeostasis under osteoporotic conditions. In a rat femoral defect model, hydrogel treatment improved bone volume, mineral density, and vascularization, as confirmed by micro-CT, histological analyses, and gene expression profiling. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the SK/HA@A@EVs platform orchestrates osteoporotic bone regeneration through synergistic modulation of osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and mitophagy-driven cellular survival pathways. This study provides a translational strategy integrating engineered exosomes with functional hydrogels for targeted, localized therapy of osteoporotic bone defects.

works.title: Naringenin-Mn self-fueling dual-dynamic hydrogel with cascade catalysis and immunomodulation properties for repairing MRSA-infected diabetic wounds
works.abstract: Chronic infectious wounds in diabetic patients remain a significant clinical challenge due to persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and bacterial resistance issues. This problem is particularly acute in the area of postoperative surgical incisions, where impaired healing can lead to serious complications. This study aimed to develop a self-healing cascade-catalyzed hydrogel, CS-PBA/ODex@NRGe-Mn (CPONM), featuring boronate ester bond and Schiff base bond. This hydrogel exhibits a dual dynamic network structure and incorporates naringenin-Mn nanoparticles (NM NPs) with SOD/POD-like activity. The hydrogel was synthesized by mixing CS-PBA solution with ODex solution containing NM NPs. CPONM exhibits high porosity, swelling capacity, adhesion strength (13.43 kPa), and pH-responsive release properties. In vitro studies demonstrated that CPONM effectively inhibited the growth of Escherichia coli ( E.coli , 93.15%) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus ( MRSA , 94.74%), disrupted bacterial biofilms by up to 92%, and reduced iNOS and IL-6 expression in macrophages. In a diabetic mouse wound model infected with MRSA , CPONM accelerated wound healing (reaching 97.47% by day 18), reduced bacterial infection risk, inhibited NF-κB, and activated Nrf2. Histopathological staining revealed the hydrogel's ability to promote wound epithelialization, collagen deposition, and vascular growth (VEGF, α-SMA). Quantitative measurements of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in wound tissue on Day 3 showed that O 2 · - decreased by 0.32 μmol/g, while ·OH increased by 18.7%, directly demonstrating the “self-fueling” cascade reaction of SOD and POD. Therefore, CPONM represents a promising approach for treating infected postoperative wounds in diabetic patients.

works.title: Bio-dissociable platinum quantum dot cluster nanozymes for nonhormonal endometriosis therapy through microenvironment remodeling
works.abstract: Endometriosis (EMS) is a chronic inflammatory disorder marked by ectopic endometrial lesions that commonly cause pain and infertility. Existing surgical and hormonal therapies are limited by adverse effects and high recurrence rates, while nanozyme-based approaches offer opportunities to develop alternative therapeutic strategies. Here, we developed bio-dissociable platinum quantum dot clusters (PtQDC) as nanozymes for nonhormonal EMS therapy. PtQDC undergoes gradual dissociation in lesion tissue fluid and exhibits sustained scavenging activity toward reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. The resulting shift of endometriotic cells from their highly oxidative state beyond a favorable redox window was accompanied by impaired energy metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. In the mouse model of EMS, PtQDC reduced lesion number and volume, remodeled the peritoneal microenvironment, inhibited pathological angiogenesis, and attenuated pain-associated signaling. PtQDC also reduced proinflammatory factors, increased IL-10, and modulated macrophage phenotypic profiles. RNA-seq analysis further revealed downregulation of Ptgs2, Mmp3, and Postn, genes associated with inflammation, invasion, and fibrosis. Thus, PtQDC integrates antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifibrotic, and antiangiogenic activities as a potential multitarget nonhormonal therapy for EMS.
