works.title: Bioengineering strategies for prenatal therapy
Development of High-Performance Chitosan-Silk Fibroin Hydrogels in Bone Repair: Mechanical and Biological Enhancements
works.abstract: Bone tissue engineering has attracted increasing interest, with natural polymers being explored for bone repair. However, most natural polymers lack sufficient mechanical strength for clinical application. In this study, methacrylated chitosan (CSMA) and silk fibroin (SF) were utilized as matrix components to develop an interpenetrating polymer network. To enhance the stability of the composite hydrogel, silk nanofibrils (SNFs) and amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) were added as reinforcing phases. Using this system, bone screws and plates were fabricated. Results showed that the incorporation of SNF significantly improved the mechanical properties of the hydrogel, increasing its fracture strength from 86 kPa to 212 kPa, representing a 146% enhancement. Additionally, the stiffness and toughness of the material were improved to approximately 386% and 65%, respectively. Moreover, the incorporation of ACP enhanced the structural stability of the hydrogel and promoted the adhesion and proliferation of osteoblasts. The manufactured bone screws and plates displayed fracture strengths of 38.1 MPa and 57.8 MPa, with moduli of 805.9 MPa and 3.15 GPa, respectively. In vitro degradation studies of the bone screws revealed moderate degradation rate and favorable structure stability. The composite material demonstrated high effectiveness in promoting osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and exhibited good osteoblast compatibility. The developed CSMA/SF/SNF/ACP composite material exhibits considerable mechanical and bioactive properties, providing new insights for the design of bone repair materials and presenting significant potential for biomedical applications.

works.title: Oxidized Pectin-Amine-Modified Chitosan/PEDOT with Decellularized Human Spinal Cord-Based Self-Healing and Electroconductive Hydrogel for Potential Spinal Regeneration Applications
works.abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM)-based biomaterials have emerged as promising therapeutic platforms for spinal cord injury (SCI) repair due to their ability to provide regenerative biochemical cues. In this study, we developed an injectable, electroconductive, and self-healing hydrogel for potential application in SCI repair. Injectability enables minimally invasive delivery, electroconductivity facilitates electrical communication that may promote neural regeneration, and self-healing properties allow restoration of the hydrogel network following shear stress during injection. The self-healing hydrogel was formulated using Schiff-base chemistry between aldehyde-functionalized pectin (PEC-ALD) and amine-functionalized chitosan (CS). Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) derivatives were incorporated to enhance electrical conductivity and support neuronal differentiation and axonal outgrowth. In addition, decellularized human spinal cord (dSC), prepared using a modified Hudson protocol, was incorporated to provide tissue-specific pro-regenerative cues. The resulting PEC-ALD-CS-PEDOT-dSC hydrogels exhibited dynamic self-healing behavior characteristic of native spinal cord tissue. Under high oscillatory strain (1000%), the hydrogel network structure temporarily dissociated, while recovery of the crosslinked network occurred upon reduction to low strain (1%). The hydrogels demonstrated a storage modulus of approximately 600 Pa, consistent with the mechanical properties favorable for neuronal growth. Incorporation of PEDOT derivatives resulted in an electrical conductivity of approximately 5.6 mS/cm. Schiff base-mediated crosslinking enabled rapid gelation within 20 min at 37 °C. Furthermore, the hydrogels exhibited shear-thinning behavior, supporting their suitability for injectable delivery. Biological evaluation demonstrated immunomodulatory potential, as RAW 264.7 macrophages encapsulated within the hydrogel exhibited greater CD206 expression relative to CD86 expression, even under lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammatory conditions. Additionally, the hydrogels supported proliferation of human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells, indicating cytocompatibility and potential to support neural regeneration. Overall, this study presents a multifunctional self-healing and electroconductive hydrogel platform incorporating decellularized spinal cord matrix for potential minimally invasive treatment of SCI.

works.title: 19F MRI-Traceable PLGA Nanocarriers: Influence of Particle Architecture on Co-Encapsulation and Release of Immiscible Payloads
works.abstract: Two perfluorocarbon (PFC)-loaded PLGA nanoparticles (NPs) of different architectures were previously established as 19F MRI tracers: sodium cholate (NaCh)-stabilized core-shell particles (CSPs) and PVA-stabilized multicore particles (MCPs). Differing in their stabilizers and internal PFC distribution, they exhibited significant differences in stiffness, permeability, cell uptake, and biological behavior, with MCPs showing dramatically faster in vivo fluorine clearance, addressing an important barrier to the clinical translation of PFCs. Here, we explore the incorporation of rapamycin, a small hydrophobic drug, as a third immiscible phase to develop a theranostic platform for cardiac regeneration. By comparing the drug-loaded particle systems (Rapa-MCPs and Rapa-CSPs) against drug-free and PFC-free (Rapa-PLGA NPs) controls, we study how PFC presence and stabilizer-governed NP architectures affect multipayload incorporation, release, and biological behavior. PFC presence was associated with enhanced drug loading but faster release. A higher drug-to-polymer ratio increased loading but constrained PFC encapsulation above 2 wt %. NP architecture governed multipayload incorporation trade-offs: Rapa-CSPs showed preferential stabilization of the PFC phase over the drug and dye, and unpredictable drug release, reflecting greater sensitivity to multipayload incorporation; Rapa-MCPs could more flexibly accommodate multiple immiscible payloads at the expense of robust PFC stabilization, and showed a fast but gradual release. In vitro, encapsulated rapamycin retained mTOR-inhibitory activity, and Rapa-MCPs reduced TGF-β-driven fibrotic signaling in human living myocardial slices, supporting their therapeutic potential. These findings indicate that the stabilizers and resulting particle architectures govern payload partitioning and release in mutually immiscible multiphasic systems and provide practical design guidelines for structurally tunable polymer nanocarriers for 19F MRI-guided drug delivery.

works.title: Programming a pro-regenerative microenvironment via a photocurable albumin-matrix hydrogel for hepatic tissue reconstitution
Pharmacologically programmed tolerogenic dendritic cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for CCR7-dependent lymphoid organ targeting in transplantation
Precursor-Encoded Metal-Free Carbon Dots Reshape the Bone-Regenerative Microenvironment: Materials Chemistry, Multiscale Mechanisms, and a Translational Roadmap
works.abstract: Bone-defect healing is a spatiotemporally coordinated continuum involving inflammatory initiation and resolution, redox re-equilibration, immune-cell state transitions, angiogenesis, osteogenic commitment of mesenchymal stromal/progenitor cells, and osteoblast-osteoclast coupling. Although metal-containing nanomaterials can enhance regeneration through ion release, catalysis, or photothermal effects, their performance is often constrained by local dose, oxidation state, release kinetics, and long-term accumulation. Metal-free carbon dots (CDs) combine nanoscale interfacial activity, programmable surface chemistry, electron-transfer capacity, intrinsic fluorescence, and scaffold compatibility and are consequently evolving from imaging probes into bioactive regulators of the bone-repair microenvironment. Following the sequence of precursor chemistry-carbonization reconstruction-surface state-protein corona/organelle response-tissue regeneration, this review compares CDs derived from citric acid, ascorbic acid, amino acids, curcumin, artesunate, yam, clove, ginger, and other natural or medicinal-food precursors. We critically examine context-dependent redox regulation, macrophage-state remodeling, osteogenic and epigenetic control, suppression of pathological osteoclastogenesis, infection control, and angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling. Current evidence is limited by ambiguous structural identity, confounded activity attribution, correlation-dominant mechanisms, overextension from simplified models, and insufficient long-term safety assessment. Translation will require fractionation-based identity definition, multi-batch potency assays, target-protein capture, organelle tracking, genetic rescue, spatial omics, and quantitative integration of chemistry, local exposure, degradation/clearance, and regenerative efficacy. Particular attention is given to how CD surface states interact with collagen, fibrin, and glycosaminoglycan matrices to govern protein adsorption, local retention, matrix organization, and growth-factor presentation. A two-tier evidence roadmap is proposed, prioritizing fraction-resolved activity attribution, compartment-specific redox assays, post-formulation identity testing, and context-matched progression from screening defects to load-bearing and comorbidity models.

Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death
works.abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu 2 O/Fe 2 O 3 ) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu 2 O/Fe 2 O 3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu 2 O/Fe 2 O 3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron–sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

works.title: Injectable bioactive glass hydrogels orchestrate metalloimmunotherapy by depleting pathogenic B cells and rescuing bone in rheumatoid arthritis
works.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive bone destruction. Transcriptomic profiling identified hyperactivated B cells as key contributors to osteoimmune dysregulation, supporting localized B cell intervention as a therapeutic strategy. Here, an injectable thermosensitive hydroxypropyl chitin hydrogel incorporating Cu/Zn-doped bioactive glass particles, termed BG@HPCH, was developed for localized metalloimmunotherapy. BG incorporation improved the shear-thinning behavior, thermosensitive gelation, storage modulus, and stability of the hydrogel. In vitro, ionic release from BG@HPCH selectively reduced pathogenic B cell survival while preserving mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) viability. The optimized M-BG@HPCH increased the B cell dead-cell area from 1.93 ± 0.48% to 91.12 ± 0.90% at 24 h, while maintaining MSC viability at 98.59 ± 0.26% after 3 days. In TNF-transgenic mice, a single intra-articular injection of BG@HPCH reduced arthritis index scores from 2.88 ± 0.18 to 1.81 ± 0.13 at day 28, limited bone erosion, and showed no detectable systemic toxicity. Micro-CT analysis showed improved bone preservation, with BV/TV increasing from 30.00 ± 6.74% to 55.66 ± 1.07%. OCN staining further confirmed enhanced osteogenic activity, with the OCN + area increasing by 2.16 times. Flow cytometry confirmed reduced B220 + CD45.2 + B cell accumulation in treated joints. Single-cell RNA sequencing of 23,921 joint cells showed that BG@HPCH reduced inflammatory B cell, macrophage, and fibroblast subsets while expanding osteoblast-associated regenerative populations, accompanied by suppression of CD23 − and CD74-associated B cell signaling axes. These findings establish BG@HPCH as a localized immunoregenerative biomaterial for coordinating pathogenic B cell depletion and bone repair in RA.

works.title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury
works.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.

works.title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration
works.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

works.title: Genetically engineered bacterial magnetosomes as optimized tracers for magnetic particle imaging
works.abstract: Medical imaging relies on tracer materials to enable accurate visualization and diagnosis of diseases. Magnetic Particle Imaging (MPI) is an innovative tomographic modality that offers exceptional sensitivity and temporal resolution. These characteristics make MPI particularly promising for clinical applications such as real-time vascular and perfusion imaging, tumor detection, and intraoperative guidance. However, MPI performance has so far been limited by the quality of available tracers, as conventional chemical synthesis provides only restricted control over the size, shape, and magnetic properties of iron oxide nanoparticles. Biogenic magnetic nanoparticles, so-called magnetosomes, produced by magnetotactic bacteria, represent a compelling alternative. Magnetosome biosynthesis is fully genetically encoded, enabling the natural formation of magnetite nanoparticles with uniform size and morphology, which is difficult to achieve through chemical synthesis. Moreover, genetic engineering of the bacterial production host allows precise tuning of particle characteristics, including size, shape, and magnetic behavior, to meet specific application requirements. In this study, magnetosomes isolated from different Magnetospirillum gryphiswaldense mutant strains, each biomineralizing particles with distinct core diameters, were systematically evaluated as potential MPI tracers. Magnetic particle spectroscopy (MPS) was used to identify the most promising candidates based on their signal properties. These tracers were subsequently subjected to detailed signal analyses and phantom experiments to directly compare their imaging performance. Our findings demonstrate that genetically tailored magnetosomes can substantially improve MPI signal quality, underscoring their potential as next-generation tracers. This work provides a foundation for the rational design of optimized biogenic nanoparticles to advance preclinical and future clinical MPI applications. Statement of significance: Magnetic Particle Imaging (MPI) is a novel imaging technology with high sensitivity and real-time capabilities, making it highly promising for clinical applications such as blood flow monitoring and tumor detection. The performance of MPI strongly depends on the properties of the tracer materials used. However, producing high-quality tracers through conventional chemical synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we introduce an innovative biological approach by using genetically engineered magnetotactic bacteria to produce uniform magnetic nanoparticles, so-called magnetosomes. This strategy allows precise control of particle size, shape, and magnetic properties, resulting in tracers with superior performance. Our findings pave the way for the development of next-generation MPI tracers, advancing both fundamental research and potential clinical translation.

works.title: Translation of in vivo CAR-T in China
Biomaterial-Based Activation Enables Scalable Expansion of Stable Human Regulatory T-cells
works.abstract: Regulatory T-cells (Tregs) hold significant promise for the treatment of autoimmune diseases and transplant rejection, yet their clinical translation is limited by inefficient and inconsistent manufacturing strategies that fail to generate stable and functional cell populations at scale. Current ex vivo expansion approaches rely on bead-based activation systems that often induce transient FOXP3 expression and variable product quality. Here, we present a bioinspired hydrogel-based activation platform that enables robust expansion and stabilization of regulatory T-cell phenotypes from primary human T-cells. Using PEG-based hydrogels functionalized with anti-CD3 and anti-CD28, we demonstrate significantly enhanced induction and persistence of FOXP3+ T-cells compared to industry-standard bead-based activation. Hydrogel activation yields >50% FOXP3+ cells and supports sustained expression following removal of activation cues, in contrast to the transient regulatory phenotype observed with conventional methods. Importantly, hydrogel-activated cultures exhibit substantial expansion of both CD4+ and CD8+ FOXP3+ populations, alongside increased expression of key immunosuppressive cytokines including IL-10 and TGF-β. While coculture with M2-polarized macrophages modestly enriches regulatory phenotypes, it reduces overall cell expansion and provides limited benefit beyond hydrogel activation alone. These findings identify material-mediated activation as a dominant driver of Treg differentiation and stability. Together, this work establishes a scalable, biomaterial-based strategy for generating high-quality regulatory T-cell products and provides a foundation for improving the manufacturing of Treg-based therapies.

works.title: Cytoskeletal and Extracellular Factors Regulating Stem Cell Differentiation: Mechanisms, Tools, and Emerging Applications
works.abstract: Stem cell lineage determination is governed not only by biochemical cues but also by the organization and force-generating state of the cytoskeleton, which integrates extracellular mechanical cues into transcriptional and epigenetic responses. Cytoskeletal organization and remodeling play essential roles in stem cell fate determination, as well as other relevant biological processes including development, tissue regeneration, and disease progression. In this review, we first outline the different types of cytoskeletal structures-actin filaments, microtubules, and intermediate filaments-and their coordinated roles in cell shape, polarity, and contractility. We then discuss how extracellular cues, including matrix stiffness, geometry, topography, shear, stretch, and compression remodel cytoskeletal distribution and adhesion dynamics to affect stem cell lineage commitment. We highlight matrix viscoelasticity and stress relaxation as time-dependent mechanical regulators that modulate traction transmission, focal adhesion, and cytoskeletal tension, thereby directing stem cell differentiation outcomes beyond stiffness alone. We next discuss mechanotransduction pathways, such as RhoA/ROCK-mediated contractility, Wnt/β-catenin, Piezo1/Piezo2, and YAP/TAZ nuclear shuttling, which couple cytoskeletal forces to gene regulation. We further summarize quantitative approaches to measure cell molecular forces, including traction force microscopy, molecular tension sensors, and advanced live-cell imaging platforms. Finally, we discuss the translational potential of cytoskeleton-informed design principles in regenerative medicine, where they can be leveraged to improve stem cell biomanufacturing, optimize tunable biomaterials, and develop more predictive mechanopathology models. Together, these developments will establish cytoskeletal organization as a controllable, engineerable lever for directing stem cell fate and enabling functional tissue formation.

works.title: Programmable apoptosis circuits enable subtractive engineering of stem cell-derived organoids and embryoids
Defining early human developmental identity: A curated, cross-platform marker framework
works.abstract: Early human development involves dynamic cell-state transitions, complicating distinction between transient transcriptional changes and stable lineage commitment in human pluripotent stem cell models. To address this challenge, we establish a curated, cross-platform marker framework for pluripotency and early germ-layer identity. Starting from an unbiased RNA-seq discovery set, we validated candidates by qPCR and evaluated the panel across independent bulk RNA-seq and embryonic single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets. This yielded 67 validated markers, of which 66 were retained for downstream transcriptomic analyses. Our framework identified early developmental states across heterogeneous datasets and showed lineage-associated enrichment in human and macaque embryonic references despite substantial transcriptional variability. Protein-level concordance was observed for detectable targets in KOLF2.1J proteomic data. To enable broad application, we introduce DeepDiff, a web-based resource integrating the marker framework and enabling automated fate classification. Together, this work provides a transferable framework for assessing early developmental identity across experimental contexts.

works.title: Modeling ocular tissues with organoids: A review of techniques and applications in lacrimal gland, cornea, lens, and retina organoid
works.abstract: Ocular dysfunctions constitute a major global health burden, causing vision impairment and blindness in millions worldwide. Numerous refractory pathologies affecting non-regenerative ocular tissues remain intractable due to poorly elucidated pathogenic mechanisms. Ocular organoids provide physiologically relevant in vitro models for mechanistic research and hold translational potential for ocular tissue reconstruction. This review synthesizes progress in ocular organoids from the ocular surface to posterior segments; evaluates methodological innovations, functional capabilities, and limitations; discusses bioengineered 3D constructs and organ-on-a-chip synergistic platforms; and envisions their role in bridging basic research and clinical translation for incurable ocular diseases.

works.title: Identification of human tooth germ ectomesenchymal stem cells
works.abstract: Cranial neural crest cells (CNCCs) contribute to most cranio-maxillofacial mesenchymal tissues, including the dental ectomesenchyme. However, the developmental relationships between human CNC-derived progenitors and the odontogenic lineage remain incompletely understood. Here, we mapped the single-cell transcriptomic landscape of prenatal human mandibles and reconstructed the putative differentiation trajectories of CNC-derived ectomesenchymal populations. Notably, we identified a distinct population of SLITRK6 + cells enriched in the odontogenic ectomesenchyme. These cells were detected in prenatal tooth germs and postnatal dental progenitor niches, including the apical papilla and dental follicle, but were rare in mature dental tissues. Functionally, SLITRK6 + cells exhibited enhanced clonogenic and odontogenic capacities and supported dentin-like matrix formation, pulp-dentin complex regeneration, and alveolar bone repair. SLITRK6 knockdown impaired odontogenic differentiation and reduced SMAD1/5/9 phosphorylation, suggesting potential involvement of BMP/SMAD signaling. Collectively, these findings identify SLITRK6 + tooth germ ectomesenchymal stem cells as prospectively isolatable progenitor populations associated with human dental development and regeneration.

works.title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review
works.abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

works.title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells
works.abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

works.title: Microglia-targeted delivery of MCC950 suppresses NLRP3–IL-18-mediated neuroinflammation and retinal injury in retinal vein occlusion
works.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) causes retinal ischemia, macular edema, and vision loss, yet current anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies primarily limit vascular leakage and leave ischemia-driven neuroinflammation insufficiently controlled. Here, we reveal a critical role for microglia-associated NLRP3–IL-18 signaling in amplifying inflammation during early RVO. Bulk retinal RNA sequencing showed broad innate immune activation, whereas single-cell transcriptomic profiling and spatial protein analysis identified prominent inflammasome-related changes in retinal microglia. Constitutive global deletion of Nlrp3 or Il18 attenuated microglial activation and preserved retinal structure and electrophysiological function. To translate this mechanistic insight into a targeted anti-inflammatory strategy, we engineered MG1-functionalized, MCC950-loaded nanoliposomes for microglia-targeted NLRP3 inhibition. MG1 functionalization promoted preferential nanoparticle uptake by activated microglia and suppressed NLRP3–IL-18 signaling more effectively than free MCC950 or non-targeted nanoliposomes. In experimental RVO, a single intravitreal dose administered 6 h after induction alleviated retinal inflammation and edema while preserving retinal electrophysiological responses. These findings establish microglia-associated NLRP3–IL-18 signaling as a therapeutic target in early RVO and support MG1-MCC950 nanoliposomes as a bioactive nanotherapeutic platform for RVO.

works.title: Spatial organization of magnetic nanoparticles in chitosan-gelatin hydrogels enables enhanced magnetic actuation and cell response under dynamic stimulation
works.abstract: Magnetically responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for remotely modulating HFF-1 fibroblasts behavior through dynamic mechanical stimulation; however, the influence of magnetic nanoparticle spatial organization on magnetic actuation and cell response remains unexplored. Herein, we report the development of chitosan-gelatin magnetic hydrogels with controlled Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticle distribution including homogeneously dispersed, and spatially patterned configurations, as a strategy to engineer localized mechanotransduction and magnetic actuation. The role of nanoparticle organization on the physicochemical, magnetic, and biological properties of the hydrogels has been analyzed. Structural characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles while preserving their crystalline inverse spinel structure. Morphological and topographical analyses revealed that patterned hydrogels exhibit well-defined nanoparticle-rich and nanoparticle-free regions, generating pronounced microscale heterogeneity throughout the material. The incorporation and spatial confinement of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles significantly influenced the hydrogel properties, increasing stiffness, reducing swelling capacity, and enhancing magnetic responsiveness. Notably, patterned hydrogels displayed higher saturation magnetization and magnetic susceptibility than homogeneously dispersed systems, indicating that nanoparticle confinement promotes cooperative magnetic interactions and more efficient magnetic actuation. Biological studies demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility for all hydrogel formulations. While static magnetic stimulation slightly reduced fibroblast proliferation, dynamic magnetic stimulation significantly enhanced cell proliferation, spreading, and cytoskeletal organization, particularly in patterned hydrogels. These effects are attributed to cyclic mechanical cues generated by amplified magnetic-to-mechanical transduction within the patterned magnetic domains. Overall, this study demonstrates that nanoparticle spatial organization is a key design parameter for engineering magnetically responsive hydrogels with tunable magnetic actuation and controllable cellular responses for tissue engineering applications.

works.title: Coacervate protocells-mediated mitochondrial transplantation restores gut epithelial energetic homeostasis in ulcerative colitis
works.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction in intestinal epithelial cells, yet current therapies fail to correct underlying energy metabolism defects. While exogenous mitochondrial transplantation offers a promising strategy, its clinical translation is hindered by rapid loss of mitochondrial bioactivity ex vivo , poor delivery efficiency, and lysosomal degradation following cellular uptake. Here, we developed a biomimetic coacervate-based protocell system (HTP) via liquid-liquid phase separation of polyethylene glycol, tannic acid, and sodium hyaluronate for efficient encapsulation and delivery of functional mitochondria (HTP@Mito). HTP protocells preserved mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis capacity for up to 72 h in HBSS buffer at 37°C, far exceeding the viability of free mitochondria. Notably, HTP markedly enhanced intracellular delivery of isolated mitochondria via lipid-raft-mediated endocytosis. In a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine UC model, rectally administrating HTP@Mito achieved superior therapeutic efficacy via restoring ATP levels and mitochondrial membrane potential, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Furthermore, by reducing oxidative stress, HTP@Mito rescued lysosomal function and restored impaired autophagic flux, thereby promoting mitophagy to clear damaged mitochondria. HTP@Mito treatment also repaired intestinal epithelial tight junctions, restored goblet cell-derived mucus secretion, and rebalanced gut microbiota by increasing beneficial Lachnospiraceae while reducing pathogenic Escherichia-Shigella . Collectively, this work established a versatile, biomimetic organelle delivery platform that could correct mitochondrial energy deficiency in the intestinal epithelium, providing a framework for mitochondrial transplantation in ulcerative colitis.

works.title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy
works.abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3 - ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

works.title: Trans-endplate delivery of arginine-based poly (ester amide) for structure-preserving therapy of intervertebral disc degeneration
works.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) remains a major cause of chronic low back pain, yet effective disease-modifying therapies are lacking. Current advanced interventions, including cell-based therapies and matrix supplementation, often disrupt disc structural integrity and fail to achieve sustained regeneration. Here, we rationally designed and synthesized a series of arginine-based poly(ester amide)s (Arg-PEAs) as endplate-penetrating biomaterials for non-direct disc therapy. Unlike conventional intradiscal injection, Arg-PEAs were administered into the adjacent vertebral bodies, enabling trans-endplate delivery into the nucleus pulposus (NP). Among them, the lead polymer 8A6S demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and efficient accumulation within the NP, as confirmed by ex vivo and in vivo imaging. Mechanistically, 8A6S suppressed IL-17 signaling by attenuating TRAF6-mediated NF-κB activation, thereby reducing inflammatory catabolism (MMP13, ADAMTS5) and restoring anabolic extracellular matrix markers (ACAN, COL2A1, SOX9). This re-establishment of matrix homeostasis promoted NP regeneration in both rat and caprine models of IDD. Collectively, this study establishes Arg-PEAs as a new class of bioactive polymers capable of trans-endplate delivery and inflammation-modulating regeneration, providing a minimally invasive and structurally preserving strategy for IDD treatment.

works.title: Inhaled nanogels ameliorate vascular remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension via normalization of endothelia-smooth muscle cell crosstalk
works.abstract: Maintaining appropriate vascular nitric oxide (NO) levels in pulmonary arteries is crucial for the alleviation of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, in the injured vascular microenvironment, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) deplete NO to generate peroxynitrite, which aggravates the oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Herein, ROS-responsive, zwitterionic nanogels (NGs), containing arginine pendants as NO precursors and encapsulating resveratrol (RSV) as an anti-oxidant, were developed for PAH management via inhalation. Benefiting from their zwitterionic surface that repels mucin adsorption, the inhaled NGs exhibit effective pulmonary mucus penetration and mucosal absorption, enabling robust diffusion to the injured pulmonary arteries. In the oxidative vascular microenvironment, the diselenide crosslinkers within the NGs are cleaved, promoting NGs dissociation and on-demand RSV release. The released RSV scavenges ROS and the arginine pendants are oxidized to generate NO, which cooperate to interrupt the ROS/NO disequilibrium. In a hypoxia/SU5416-induced PAH mouse model, inhaled NGs efficiently alleviate vascular remodeling and reduce pulmonary arterial pressure. This study offers an effective strategy for pulmonary drug delivery, and holds promising potentials for the management of PAH.

works.title: Achieving the targeted retention of nanomotors via a controllable “braking” mechanism based on molecularly programmed engine disassembly
Cell-enriched granular bioinks enable vascular integration and endometrial repair
Improved quality and reproducibility of cerebral cortical organoids under microfluidic culture conditions: a proof-of-concept study
works.abstract: models capable of recapitulating essential aspects of human brain development, thereby offering new opportunities for studying brain physiology and disease. Nonetheless, their use in preclinical settings remains limited by their high variability. Microfluidic devices offer a promising alternative to conventional culture supports by enabling improved recapitulation of the cellular microenvironment; however, most cerebral organoids-on-chips rely on custom-made academic prototypes, limiting their scalability and translatability. Here, we established a standardized brain organoid-on-chip model by combining a regionalized cortical organoid differentiation protocol with a commercially available microfluidic device (Duplex™, NETRI). Cortical organoid quality and reproducibility were evaluated using a previously established multi-criteria Quality Control (QC) framework based on a scoring system. To enhance objectivity and throughput, the non-invasive morphometric QC criteria were automated using deep learning-based image analysis. Using a single human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) line, we assessed whether microfluidic culture conditions could improve the quality and reproducibility of cortical organoids within a controlled genetic background. Compared with conventional cultures, on-chip cortical organoids displayed improved inter- and intra-batch reproducibility across multiple scales, including morphology, size, cytoarchitectural organization, and transcript expression, together with higher QC scores and reduced QC failure rates. Finally, the QC framework was adapted for neurotoxicity assessment using a decision tree to classify compounds according to their neurotoxic risk. While this study represents a proof-of-concept demonstration within a single genetic background, the integrated brain organoid-on-chip platform and standardized QC evaluations provide a flexible and translatable approach for preclinical and industrial studies and support future validation across multiple hiPSC lines.

works.title: Accelerated formulation screening of multi-component bioinks via a deep learning-integrated high-throughput gradient printing platform
works.abstract: Abstract The development of performant multi-component bioinks is severely bottlenecked by the astronomical size of the possible design space and the inefficiency of empirical, trial-and-error experimentation. Existing high-throughput screening methods, such as microarrays and droplet microfluidics, remain limited by discrete sampling, cell-unfriendly environments, and a lack of integrated analytics. Herein, a high-throughput gradient printing (HTGP) platform is employed to overcome these barriers by integrating continuous combinatorial bioprinting with deep learning (DL)-powered phenotyping. The HTGP system rapidly generates bioink libraries with gradients within a native three-dimensional hydrogel environment, preserving cell viability and enabling in situ , direct interrogation of cell-material interactions. Coupled with an automated neural network pipeline, the platform quantitatively deciphers complex relationships between bioink composition and cellular responses from massive images. Under the tested in vitro conditions, it identified a formulation that enhanced human umbilical vein endothelial cell proliferation and spreading, as well as a candidate bioink that exhibited osteo-inductive potential by promoting osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Critically, the formulation identified through DL-assisted screening showed an enhanced early regenerative response in a rat periodontal bone defect model compared with the controls. The HTGP platform shifts from discrete testing to intelligent, continuous exploration, poised to accelerate the discovery of advanced biomaterials for personalized tissue engineering.

works.title: Machine Learning-Based Taylor Cone Analysis for Electrospinning Process-Window Identification and Cell-Laden Nanofiber Scaffold Fabrication
works.abstract: Electrospinning is a powerful biofabrication technique for constructing fibrous scaffolds that mimic extracellular matrix architectures. However, the process is highly nonlinear and involves strongly coupled parameters, making fiber architecture and biological performance difficult to control empirically and limits reproducibility. Most machine learning (ML) studies still focus on static correlations between processing parameters and outcomes rather than on dynamic modeling of electrospinning evolution and regulation, thereby hindering real-time, precise process control. Here, we establish a data-driven framework that links process parameters, Taylor cone geometry, and nanofiber/cell outcomes through high-speed imaging and ML. A custom image-processing pipeline is developed to automatically extract cone angle, height, and width from in situ images with improved accuracy via a rotating-ray-based geometric algorithm. Using datasets collected from three representative polymer systems (PVDF, PVB, and PEO), random forest models outperform support vector machine and minimum description length, achieving moderate-to-good prediction of Taylor cone descriptors (R²≈0.57-0.83) across varied voltages, flow rate, and needle-collector distances. We further extend this framework to PEO-based cell electrospinning. By correlating predicted cone geometries with experimentally measured viability of 293T cells and umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells, we identify a Taylor cone "safe window" that simultaneously stabilizes jet formation and preserves cell survival (>95%). Guided by this window, a bilayer cell-laden scaffold comprising a PVB support layer and a PEO-cell layer is fabricated with improved process robustness. This enables stable delivery of high-density, highly viable cells and facilitates the fabrication of three-dimensional cell-laden nanofiber scaffolds. Overall, this Taylor cone analysis, ML-guided strategy provides a quantitative framework for process-window identification in polymer and cell electrospinning, and may support future integration with real-time monitoring, online inference, and closed-loop control in intelligent biofabrication.

works.title: Enhancing the structural integrity of 3D bioprinted urethral grafts for clinical applications using GelMA–fibrinogen bioinks infused with human primary cells
works.abstract: The demand for organ transplantation continues to grow, while challenges remain, such as the shortage of organ donors and complications associated with existing treatments. A promising alternative to transplantation is the implantation of artificial organs, which can be produced using 3D bioprinting technology. This approach offers the advantage of patient-specific solutions tailored to individual needs. Patients with urethral stricture or hypospadias who are unable to urinate require urethral reconstruction, which carries risks of complications and restricture. These patients may benefit from a tissue-engineered urethra fabricated using autologous cells and 3D bioprinting.A printer setup for tubular structures was developed for a 3D-Bioplotter and a gelatin-fibrinogen-based bioink was supplemented with GelMA to enhance mechanical properties for clinical applications while maintaining cell compatibility. Evaluation was performed through tensile testing, printability, suturability and cell viability analyses. An artificial urethral graft was successfully fabricated, demonstrating the operational capacity of our rod-based printer setup and the GelMA-fibrinogen hydrogel exhibited an increase in Young's modulus compared with the gelatin-fibrinogen hydrogel. The GelMA-fibrinogen hydrogel also exhibited good suturability and efficient cell recovery after 14 days of culture. Human urothelial- and smooth muscle cells developed characteristic morphologies within the print, and a 210% increase in burst pressure was observed for the urethral graft after 14 days of culture, compared with the acellular graft.This 3D bioprinted artificial urethra, containing human urothelial and smooth muscle cells, represents a significant step forward in developing new treatment options for urethral disorders.

works.title: Cryomicroneedles: a versatile platform for transdermal delivery of biotherapeutics
works.abstract: Cryomicroneedles (cryoMNs) are an emerging transdermal drug delivery platform that relies on low-temperature manufacturing. It combines cryoprotection with minimally invasive microneedle technology, effectively maintaining the activity of temperature-sensitive biotherapeutics, including cells, microbes, biomacromolecules and exosomes, overcoming the drawbacks of conventional microneedles. This review summarizes the materials, preparation methods, and wide applications of cryoMNs in cell therapy, microbial delivery, drug delivery, and wound repair. The underlying therapeutic mechanisms, current challenges, and future prospects are also discussed. In summary, cryoMNs have shown great potential in the clinical translation of biotherapeutics, and this article is intended to present valuable references for the continuous development of cryoMNs.

works.title: Corrigendum: Repairing a bone defect with a three-dimensional cellular construct composed of a multi-layered cell sheet on electrospun mesh (2017 Biofabrication 9 025036)
works.abstract: Abstract During a retrospective review of our research data and published figures, we identified an inadvertent image-selection error in the assembly of Figure 4 C. Panel C(b), which was intended to show the random group, was mistakenly populated with an enlarged micrograph from the same experimental group as C(a), containing an overlapping tissue region. Consequently, the two panels did not present independent representative images of their respective experimental groups. To correct this error, panel C(a) is retained as the authentic micrograph of the nestlike group, and panel C(b) has been replaced with the authentic representative micrograph of the 4-layered CSM construct from the random group, retrieved from the original microscopy acquisition archive. In addition, in panels B(a) and B(b), the scale-bar labels have been corrected from 50 μm to 25 μm to match the scale bar in the original raw images. The multi-layered structure and collagen presence shown in Figure 4 remain fully consistent with the corrected micrographs, without altering any scientific interpretations or conclusions. The authors apologize for the errors in Figure 4.

works.title: Glucose-Fueled Cascade Catalytic Micro/Nanomotors: Recent Advances and Biomedical Applications
works.abstract: With the advancement of micro/nanomotors toward greater functionalization and intelligence, increasing attention has been devoted to their biomedical applications, which in turn impose more stringent requirements on biocompatibility and propulsion performance. Given that glucose serves as both an energy source and a metabolic intermediate in living cells, glucose-fueled micro/nanomotors hold particular promise for life science applications. In this review, we focus on glucose-fueled micro/nanomotors driven by cascade catalytic reactions, which exhibit inherently favorable biocompatibility and enhanced propulsion. Beginning with the fundamental principles of cascade reactions, we summarize the types and current development status of cascade reactions employing glucose as a substrate. We then discuss the design strategies of glucose-fueled cascade catalytic micro/nanomotors in terms of carrier engineering, enzyme loading methodologies, propulsion mechanisms, and motility behaviors. Subsequently, we review recent progress in biomedical applications, with particular emphasis on in vitro and in vivo studies for cancer therapy, biological barrier penetration, and antibiofilm eradication. Finally, we conclude by addressing the current limitations of glucose-fueled cascade catalytic micro/nanomotors and the challenges that must be overcome to advance their practical translation.

works.title: Commercial and Novel Drug-Loaded Coatings with Anticoagulant and/or Antibacterial Functions for Clinical Applications
works.abstract: Drug-loaded coatings significantly improve the bioactivities of multiple medical devices. The most widespread applications are assembling anticoagulant coatings on blood-contacting medical devices to enhance blood compatibility and applying antibacterial coatings to prevent device-induced infection. Notably, a vicious cycle between bacterial infection and thrombosis may result in deterioration of condition and even lead to treatment failure. Thrombosis caused by blood incompatibility of medical devices provides niduses for bacterial colonization, whereas bacterial endotoxins accelerate thrombosis by activating platelets. In some situations, the interactional process can also trigger inflammatory responses and calcification processes. Therefore, the demands for anticoagulant and antibacterial are necessary and mutually influenced. This review presents a summary of current commercial drug-loaded anticoagulant coatings and a detailed report on novel drug-loaded coatings with anticoagulant and/or antibacterial effects. We highlight the synthesis and assembly techniques, drug-release duration, and biofunctional behavior of referenced coatings. Based on careful comparison and comprehensive summary of the state-of-the-art literature, this review reveals the difficulties in large-scale production of the emerging coatings and the functional differences compared to the existing commercial coatings, and predicts the general process for manufacturing and commercialization.

works.title: Phase separation of Rbpms sequesters translation elongation machinery to preserve hematopoietic stem cell function
A self-organized tri-lineage bone model in liquefied microcapsules captures matrix dynamics in early remodeling
A mechanically active microneedle platform integrated with engineered exosomes for enhanced tendon-bone regeneration
Spheroid-based generation of 3D myogenic tissues using transgene- and sorting-free differentiation of hiPSCs
works.abstract: Abstract Objective . Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) represent a clinically relevant cell source for skeletal muscle tissue engineering, yet transgene-free maturation remains challenging. Moreover, the potential of spheroids as building blocks for muscle engineering remains poorly defined. This study evaluated whether hiPSC-derived myogenic spheroids enhance biofabrication outcomes in an in vitro bio-artificial muscle (BAM) system compared to a conventional single cell approach. Methods . CD56 + hiPSC-derived myoblasts were generated using a transgene-free protocol and differentiated toward 2D myotubes. In 3D, myoblasts were aggregated into 140–200 µ m spheroids. Spheroids or single cells were encapsulated in a fibrin-based BAM, kept under tension using metal pins. Non-encapsulated spheroids and BAMs were cultured up to 15 d and evaluated for myosin heavy chain (MYH) + organization, transcriptional profile, and contractile function. Results . In 2D, MYH + myotubes showing multinucleation and, occasionally, sarcomere striation were formed. Spheroids were successfully generated, increased in size and circularity, and showed an enhancing MYH positivity, particularly during the proliferation phase, and displayed a fetal/perinatal myogenic state. In BAMs, spheroids promoted MYH positivity and established larger continuous MYH + structures. Transcriptional profiles of spheroid and single cell BAMs were broadly similar. Tetanic forces did likewise not differ between both conditions. Conclusion . hiPSC-derived myogenic spheroids advance MYH expression, but terminal maturation is constrained, likely due to their intrinsically isotropic nature. Within BAMs, spheroids enhance MYH + myotube formation, but do not overcome limitations in myoblast fusion. Incomplete spheroid outgrowth and poor control over their spatial distribution are important challenges for their integration. Future work should focus on improving hiPSC differentiation efficiency, implementing spheroids in earlier differentiation stages, and optimizing spheroid outgrowth and positioning, alongside incorporating remaining muscle components as fibroblasts and vascular cells. This will refine whether spheroid-based assembly can add value in specific biofabrication contexts.

works.title: Current Advances in Antioxidant Nanozymes for Liver Diseases
works.abstract: The liver with unique physiological functions is susceptible to oxidative stress (OS) damage from reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, further triggering various liver diseases. Compared with conventional pharmacological and surgical therapies, natural antioxidant enzymes represent promise for liver disease therapy due to high ROS scavenging and low immunogenicity. However, their clinical translation is limited by instability and complex preparation. Antioxidant nanozymes not only mimic natural enzymes, but possess advantages including simple structure, low cost and high stability. They have emerged as ideal therapeutic options for liver diseases by mitigating OS, modulating inflammation, and remodeling the pathological microenvironment. This review innovatively elucidates hepatic OS pathogenesis from a synergistic perspective, integrating indirect (inflammatory pathways) and direct (organelle stress, oxidase activation) ROS generation routes, thereby filling gaps in existing literature. Subsequently, we systematically summarize advances in five representative classes of nanomaterials: metal-, selenium-, carbon-, organic- and metal-organic frameworks (MOF)-based, and emphasize catalytic mechanisms and activity regulation strategies to guide the design of effective, low-toxicity antioxidant nanozymes. Furthermore, this review highlights recent progress of antioxidant nanozymes in typical liver diseases, including drug-induced liver injury, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury, liver fibrosis, and acute liver failure, alongside clinical translation bottlenecks. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for antioxidant nanozymes are outlined.

works.title: Dual-Enzyme-Driven Thermosensitive Hydrogel Triggers Disulfidptosis and Alleviates Hypoxia for Enhanced Osteosarcoma Radiosensitization
works.abstract: Osteosarcoma shows poor responsiveness to radiotherapy (RT), largely due to the efficient DNA damage repair capacity of tumor cells and the hypoxic tumor microenvironment. In addition, achieving adequate safe surgical margins after resection remains difficult, contributing to low long-term patient survival. Current clinical radiosensitization strategies are limited by insufficient tumor specificity and considerable systemic toxicity. In this study, we loaded glucose oxidase (GOx) and catalase (CAT) into a thermosensitive hydrogel to construct a local cascade catalytic system, termed FS-GC. The SLC7A11-mediated conversion of cystine to cysteine is highly dependent on glucose availability. GOx consumes glucose and depletes NADPH, increasing the NADP+/NADPH ratio and promoting cystine accumulation. This triggers filamentous actin contraction and downregulation of filamin A, thereby inhibiting DNA repair proteins and inducing disulfidptosis. Meanwhile, CAT converts H2O2 generated by GOx into oxygen to alleviate local hypoxia. FS-GC exhibits favorable biosafety, structural stability, and sustained enzyme release and degrades almost completely within 14 days. In vitro and in vivo results confirm that FS-GC suppresses DNA repair and relieves hypoxia through disulfidptosis and the dual catalytic activity of GOx and CAT, leading to significantly enhanced RT efficacy and inhibition of osteosarcoma progression.

works.title: Potentiated Skin Permeation and Antitumor Efficacy of Fulvestrant-Loaded High-Permeation Vesicles for Localized Breast Cancer Treatment
works.abstract: Fulvestrant (FLV) is a selective estrogen receptor degrader used for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Nevertheless, its delivery is limited by low aqueous solubility and repeated intramuscular administration. Considering these drawbacks, a high-permeation vesicle-in-gel system (HPV-gel) was explored as a localized transdermal approach for FLV and evaluated for its physicochemical, permeation, cellular, pharmacokinetic, antitumor, and safety performance. Accordingly, FLV/HPVs were prepared using soya phosphatidylcholine and a ternary permeation-enhancer combination of sodium oleate (SO), diethylene glycol monoethyl ether (DEGEE), and propylene glycol (PG). Enhancer proportions were optimized using a D-optimal mixture design based on vesicle size, PDI, and entrapment efficiency. The optimized composition contained 80% phospholipid and 20% of a permeation enhancer mixture, comprising SO, DEGEE, and PG in a ratio of 6:1.5:2.5. FLV/HPVs showed a particle size of 94.02 ± 1.10 nm, a PDI of 0.241 ± 0.029, a zeta potential of -38.6 ± 1.2 mV, an entrapment efficiency of 85.79 ± 3.72%, a practical drug loading of 8.58 ± 0.16%, and a deformability index of 1.62 ± 0.08. The optimized vesicles were incorporated into a 1.5% w/v Carbopol 934P gel and compared with FLV-gel and FLV/Lipo-gel with the same gel base and an equivalent FLV amount. FLV/HPVs-gel showed sustained drug release and increased FLV permeation by nearly 8-fold and 3-fold compared with FLV-gel and FLV/Lipo-gel, respectively, with higher intradermal retention and deeper dermal distribution. Following topical administration, FLV/HPVs-gel increased Cmax by ∼8.3- and ∼2-fold and AUC0-168 h by ∼8.1- and ∼2.6-fold compared with FLV-gel and FLV/Lipo-gel, respectively, while showing plasma concentration-time profile closer to FLV (i.m.). In 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, FLV/HPVs-gel showed the strongest tumor-suppressive effect, accompanied by greater intratumoral penetration, while biochemical parameters, major organ histology, TEWL, and skin histology indicated acceptable systemic and local safety. Overall, FLV/HPVs-gel improved skin permeation, drug exposure, and antitumor activity, suggesting its potential as a noninvasive transdermal approach for FLV in breast cancer therapy.

works.title: Quorum-Sensing-Mediated Extracellular Electron Transfer Enables Hydrogel Morphogenesis
works.abstract: Engineered living materials seek to capture the sensitivity, responsiveness, and programmable characteristics of biological systems. One emergent property of living systems is genetically driven spatial patterning, which controls cell differentiation and the development of complex multicellular organisms. Inspired by this capability, we use bacteria to spatially control material assembly. In our system, extracellular electron transfer (EET) flux from Shewanella oneidensis drives hydrogel synthesis via copper-catalyzed radical polymerization. We first construct a recombinant quorum-sensing system in S. oneidensis that allows for cell-cell communication between "sender" and "receiver" cells through an autoinducer. We then examine controlled gene expression and EET-driven chemical transformation in various synthetic consortia. Via diffusion through agarose, we examine 2D patterns of gene expression relative to localized sender cell populations and demonstrate controlled hydrogel crosslinking in predictable patterns. Finally, we apply computational methods and NOT logic in "receiver" cells toward more complex patterns of gene expression. Our results highlight the potential of bacteria to program material systems with life-like properties, including self-assembly, environmental responsiveness, and patterned differentiation.

works.title: Cytochalasin D-induced cytoskeletal remodeling with MYH9 enhances release of extracellular vesicles for therapeutic application
works.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold great potential as therapeutic vehicles, but their clinical application is limited by low production yields. Here, we explored whether the pharmacological disruption of the actin cytoskeleton using cytochalasin D (CytoD) could enhance EV release while maintaining properties essential for therapeutic use. We examined monocytic U937 cells and colorectal cancer SW480 cells, discovering that CytoD increased EV production by approximately 8.27-fold in U937 cells and 10.06-fold in SW480 cells, while largely preserving the size distribution and surface charge of the EVs. Density gradient ultracentrifugation and label-free quantitative proteomics revealed that CytoD not only increased overall EV release but also selectively remodeled EV proteins. Notably, CytoD-EVs retained lineage-associated membrane proteins such as LFA-1 and showed an enrichment of cytoskeleton-related regulators, particularly MYH9, as well as proteins involved in adhesion and membrane trafficking. We observed the recruitment of MYH9 to membrane blebs,and both pharmacological inhibition with blebbistatin and MYH9 knockdown suppressed EV release, indicating that actomyosin-dependent contractility stimulates EV shedding. Importantly, CytoD-EVs proved to be highly effective drug carriers that doxorubicin-loaded EVs efficiently delivered cargo to recipient cells and induced greater cytotoxicity than free doxorubicin at equivalent doses. Overall, these findings demonstrate that CytoD-induced cytoskeletal remodeling enhances EV production through MYH9-associated membrane dynamics while preserving their capacity for therapeutic delivery. Thus, our findings establish CytoD-induced EV biogenesis as a robust, scalable, and translationally applicable platform for advanced EV-based drug delivery systems.

works.title: Spontaneous phase separation-driven Janus hydrogel spatiotemporally orchestrates the fibrotic progression for functional tendon regeneration
Hybrid nanovesicle artificial antigen-presenting cells integrate endogenous tumor antigen display with senescence-mimetic erythrocyte membrane-directed splenic T-cell priming
An interpretable AI model decodes the rules of cell recruitment to specific destinations
Granular hydrogel bioink for macroporous pancreatic spheroid scaffolds
works.abstract: Cells positioned more than several hundred microns away from a vascular network experience insufficient oxygen and nutrient supply due to diffusion limitations, leading to compromised viability and impaired function. This challenge is especially relevant in large, engineered 3D constructs which exceed the diffusion limitation of 100 - 200 µm, resulting in necrotic cores. Granular hydrogels have emerged as a promising approach for tissue engineering due to their inherent porosity. Their interconnected pores can facilitate mass transport of oxygen and nutrients, and therefore support cellular function. In this work, we developed a facile method to prepare bioprintable granular hydrogel bioink containing microparticles with tunable diameters, that can form porous scaffolds with different pore sizes and porosities. The bioink remained shelf-stable for at least 60 days when stored at 4 °C, as determined by the melt temperature. The macroporous granular hydrogel scaffold has inherent void spaces between the hydrogel microparticles, in which spheroids can be embedded. Pancreatic spheroids incorporated into the scaffold showed improved viability compared to free spheroids, indicating the granular microenvironment supports spheroid survival. Furthermore, functional studies of embedded pancreatic spheroids with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) demonstrated preserved insulin secretion functionality. Our approach thus serves as a tunable platform for supporting the culture of functional spheroids and organoids, that has potential regenerative medicine applications in restoration of physiological functions when implanted.

works.title: Versatile polyacrylamide/gum hybrid hydrogels for tunable mechanics and high-fidelity 3D extrusion printing
works.abstract: Polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogels are widely used in biological research for their well-established and tunable mechanical properties, which can closely match native tissue stiffness, making them attractive for mechanobiology, biosensing and tissue engineering. However, extrusion-based 3D printing of PAM remains challenging due to the inherently low viscosity of precursor solutions. Existing strategies reach printable viscosities with rheology modifiers such as Laponite clays or protein-based microgels, but these additives strongly couple printability to final stiffness, substantially increasing the elastic modulus and compromising the soft, tunable character that makes PAM valuable. Here, we present a novel yet accessible one-pot strategy for extrusion-printable PAM hydrogels, using natural polysaccharide gums as a distinct class of rheology modifier. Unlike conventional additives, gums confer the shear-thinning and viscoelastic structure required for extrusion at low concentrations (2-4 w/v %), while preserving the established AM/BIS-stiffness relationship and allowing modulus to be tuned independently through monomer concentration. Tragacanth, xanthan, and guar gums were systematically evaluated across concentrations for their effects on ink rheology, print fidelity, and mechanics. High-fidelity printing was achieved at concentrations as low as 2 w/v % for guar and 3 w/v % for tragacanth and xanthan. Mechanical characterization reveals soft, tunable properties, with elastic moduli from 5 to 58 kPa across gum type and concentration, spanning a broad range of soft tissue stiffnesses. Guar and tragacanth in particular produced moduli statistically comparable to pure PAM, confirming minimal impact on network mechanics. Preliminary cytocompatibility assays confirm these hybrid hydrogels support MDCK I cell viability. We further demonstrate core-shell extrusion printing of PAM/gum hydrogels for the first time, using a sacrificial core to generate hollow, perfusable channels down to ~200 µm in diameter. Together, these results establish PAM/gum hydrogels as a printable, mechanically tunable ink platform, laying a materials-processing foundation for architecturally complex, channeled PAM-based constructs.

works.title: Correction to “An In Situ UV Cross-Linking Asymmetric Adhesive Hydrogel for Noncompressible Hemostasis and Postoperative Adhesion Prevention”
Photodynamic Cancer Therapy by an Oxygen Gas Carrier Consisting of PEGylated Carbon Nanohorn-Based Nanomaterials
works.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a promising approach for cancer treatment. However, PDT has been limited by oxygen (O2) availability in tumor tissues, particularly within hypoxic regions. A PEGylated nitrogen-doped carbon nanohorn (NCNH) has unique structural properties that encapsulate O2 and deliver it efficiently to tumor sites, overcoming the limitation of O2 availability. The O2 uptake on O2-loaded PEGylated NCNH nanocarriers was approximately 1.24 times higher than O2-loaded pristine NCNH and 0.80 times that of O2-loaded nanocarriers with additional O2 adsorbers of dendrimers (DEN) and fluorocarbons (F) named NCNH/DEN-F/F-PEG. Then, singlet oxygen was generated nearly proportionately to the O2 loading. However, on cellular uptake, PEGylated NCNH and NCNH/DEN-F/F-PEG had higher uptake (81.7% and 90.4%, respectively) than pristine NCNH (51.2%), implying the superior uptake ability of PEGylated carriers. From high singlet oxygen generation and the preferable cellular uptake, the decrease in cell viability of MCF-7 breast cancer cells, which were incubated with O2-loaded nanocarriers under light irradiation, occurred at the lowest concentration (IC50 = 9.6 µg/mL) for NCNH/DEN-F/F-PEG. This innovative strategy not only advances much production of singlet oxygen by accumulating O2 adsorber units but also facilitates the uptake of carriers into biological membranes by PEGylating, enhancing the therapeutic outcome and contributing to personalized and effective cancer therapies.

works.title: A Modular Glycoengineered Exosome Platform for Targeted Delivery via Chemoenzymatic Engineering of Surface Sialic Acids
works.abstract: Bovine milk-derived exosomes (mExos) are scalable, biocompatible nanocarriers well-suited for the cross-barrier transport and protection of labile nucleic acid therapeutics. However, achieving precise active targeting for cargo delivery remains challenging, as conventional surface functionalization methods often lack site-specificity, unintentionally altering native physicochemical properties or obscuring essential membrane interactions. Herein, we report a modular glycoengineering strategy that leverages the dense sialic acid coating on mExos to introduce versatile anchoring sites for targeting ligand modification via sequential chemoenzymatic remodeling. Specifically, the native terminal sialic acids on the mExo surface were enzymatically removed and replaced with azide-modified sialic acid analogs, which was achieved efficiently through an integrated multienzyme reaction. In principle, the resulting platform, mExo-N3, enables the glycan-selective conjugation of any dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO)-modified targeting ligands for targeted delivery, avoiding the limitations of random modifications. To validate this platform, we conjugated mExo-N3 with an anti-EGFR nanobody (7D12) and encapsulated a microRNA-21 inhibitor (miR-21i). The resulting mExo-7D12@miR-21i construct maintained colloidal stability and exhibited specific internalization by EGFR-positive cancer cells. Intracellular delivery of miR-21i restored the expression of tumor suppressors PTEN and PDCD4, inducing apoptosis and suppressing proliferation. Furthermore, in an A431 xenograft model, the targeted system achieved 58.3% tumor growth inhibition in vivo without evident systemic toxicity. By converting native glycans into functional anchoring sites, this approach provides a translatable framework for customizing exosomal delivery vectors into targeted therapeutics.

works.title: Functionalized Chinese Medicine-Derived Quercetin Carbon Dots for the Treatment of Osteoporosis
works.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) compound formulas are widely employed in the clinical management of osteoporosis; however, their principal bioactive constituents and primary molecular targets remain poorly characterized. Consequently, there is an urgent need for systematic functional exploration of TCM-derived chemicals. In this study, we applied a network pharmacology-based approach to screen four canonical TCM compound prescriptions for antiosteoporotic compounds, identifying a total of 20 candidate molecules. Among these, quercetin was selected as a lead compound for the synthesis of biologically active carbon dots (CDs), which were then integrated with mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) to construct a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanocarrier system. In vitro cellular assays demonstrated that both the quercetin-derived CDs and the drug-loaded nanocarriers exhibited excellent cytocompatibility, robust osteogenic-promoting activity, and potent osteoclast-inhibitory effects. Collectively, our findings underscore the utility of network pharmacology in identifying quercetin as a promising TCM-derived lead compound for osteoporosis intervention, and the rational functionalization strategy developed herein provides a valuable paradigm for advancing the therapeutic application of TCM-derived chemicals in bone metabolic disorders.

works.title: Piezoelectric electroporation potentiates high-frequency irreversible electroporation for enhanced prostate cancer eradication
Reprogramming tumor vasculature: Integrating normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip models
works.abstract: Abnormal tumor vasculature is a hallmark of the tumor microenvironment that promotes hypoxia, therapeutic resistance, and disease progression while limiting the delivery of anticancer therapy. Although early anti-angiogenic therapies were designed to starve tumors by eliminating their blood supply, excessive vessel pruning often aggravated hypoxia and selected for more aggressive phenotypes. These observations led to the concept of vascular normalization, whereby judicious modulation of angiogenic signaling transiently restores vessel structure and function, improving perfusion, oxygenation, drug delivery, and anti-tumor immunity. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms governing tumor vessel formation, maturation, and dysfunction, and examine therapeutic strategies aimed at normalizing the tumor vasculature. We further highlight the major challenges limiting clinical translation, including the transient and heterogeneous nature of the normalization window, adaptive resistance mechanisms, and the lack of robust tools for longitudinal monitoring.
