We then integrate vascular normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip platforms, examining how key features of the tumor microenvironment, including tissue architecture, extracellular matrix remodeling, hemodynamic forces, metabolic gradients, and multicellular interactions, can be recreated and quantitatively monitored. We critically evaluate how engineering design, biomaterial selection, vascularization strategies, perfusion, and integrated sensing influence the ability of these platforms to capture vascular normalization and therapeutic responses. By linking the hallmarks of vascular normalization to measurable on-chip phenotypes, vascularized tumor-on-chip systems provide controlled frameworks for investigating resistance mechanisms, optimizing treatment timing, and advancing precision oncology. However, challenges related to physiological fidelity, standardization, scalability, and clinical validation continue to limit their broader translation.

works.title: Mitochondria-rich cytochalasomes as an intravenously deliverable vesicle platform for ischemic heart disease
works.abstract: Poor organelle viability and rapid immune clearance limit mitochondrial transplantation for ischemic disease. Here, we engineer mitochondria-rich cytochalasomes (MRCs) as an intravenously deliverable vesicle platform. MRCs are generated through cytoskeletal remodeling in mesenchymal stem cells. They encapsulate functional mitochondria, protecting them from extracellular stressors and inheriting immunomodulatory proteins, which reduce macrophage phagocytosis by more than sixfold. Mechanistically, MRCs do not fuse with the host mitochondrial network but instead are trafficked to lysosomes and trigger protective autophagy-lysosomal response. In a murine myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) model, a single intravenous injection of MRCs reduced infarct size by 52% and preserved cardiac function for up to 28 days, whereas isolated mitochondria were ineffective. This work positions MRCs as a promising intravenously deliverable vesicle platform for ischemic heart disease and reveals a non-fusogenic mechanism.

works.title: Thermosensitive and tumor-targeted asparaginase fusion protein enables metabolic-immunotherapy for solid tumors
Bimetallic biomimetic catalytic STING sensitizer for coordinating innate and adaptive immune responses against biofilm infections
Self-assembly prodrugs for controlled singlet oxygen release and resistance modulation in deep-tumor photodynamic therapy
Dual Delivery from a Multilayer Buccal Film: Rational Design of a Combination Product for Localized Treatment of Oral Fibrosis
works.abstract: Oral submucous fibrosis (OSF) is a chronic, progressive, and potentially malignant disorder characterized by severe oral cavity remodeling. The condition is driven by a painful burning sensation and a pathognomonic restriction of mouth opening (trismus), severely diminishing patients' quality of life. Current clinical management represents a critical bottleneck in patient care, as conventional strategies rely heavily on painful intralesional injections or systemic regimens plagued by localized toxicity and poor compliance. Consequently, there is an urgent demand for localized, noninvasive, and patient-compliant delivery systems capable of sustaining therapeutic drug levels directly at the fibrotic site. To address this challenge, we developed, optimized, and characterized a multilayered buccal film ("sandwich" architecture) combining bupivacaine (Bupi) and pirfenidone (PFD) to achieve an immediate anesthetic effect followed by sustained antifibrotic action. A Design of Experiments (DoE) approach optimized both formulation composition and the critical process parameter (drying rate), yielding a fast-dissolving (FD) layer engineered for rapid Bupi release alongside a slow-dissolving (SD) layer tailored for prolonged PFD dissolution. The resulting monolithic system successfully immobilizes both therapeutics in a stable amorphous state, leveraging macromolecular free volume and modulated surface microtopography to regulate biphasic release kinetics. This work demonstrates the feasibility of engineering kinetically distinct, multilayered buccal films through rational design, providing a translationally viable therapeutic platform for localized management of oral fibrosis.

works.title: Correction to: “Extrusion-Stretched Multigrooved Conduits Loaded with Multiwalled Carbon Nanotubes for Efficient Peripheral Nerve Regeneration”
Self-Assembled Platelet-Derived Growth Factor-Mimetic Peptide@BG Hydrogel Promotes Wound Healing by Regulating Mitochondrial Function through the RhoA/Rock1/Drp1 Signaling Axis
works.abstract: Skin wound healing involves four overlapping phases, with angiogenesis and mitochondrial functional recovery being critical for effective repair. In this study, a platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF)-mimetic peptide hydrogel was constructed and combined with bioactive glass to form a PDGF-mimetic peptide@BG composite system, aiming to synergistically promote wound healing. The structural stability and morphology of the PDGF-mimetic peptide@BG were characterized using electron microscopy and spectroscopic techniques. Biocompatibility was assessed through in vitro cell experiments. A full-thickness skin defect model in mice was established, and wound healing, angiogenesis, and mitochondrial functional recovery were evaluated using histological staining, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. The involvement of the RhoA/Rock1/Drp1 signaling pathway in mitochondrial function improvement was investigated. The PDGF-mimetic peptide@BG was successfully prepared with stable structure. In vitro experiments demonstrated good biocompatibility and promotion of endothelial cell proliferation and migration. In vivo results confirmed that PDGF-mimetic peptide@BG accelerated wound healing in mice, enhanced granulation tissue formation and collagen deposition, and increased local blood flow and angiogenesis. Furthermore, the composite restored mitochondrial function, as evidenced by reduced ROS levels, elevated ATP and SOD activity, improved mitochondrial morphology, and downregulation of mitochondrial fission-related proteins. Mechanistic studies suggested that PDGF-mimetic peptide@BG may exert its reparative effects at least in part through inhibition of the RhoA/Rock1/Drp1 signaling pathway. This study suggests that the PDGF-mimetic peptide@BG significantly promotes tissue regeneration in a normal murine wound model by increasing wound blood flow, enhancing vascularization, accelerating mitochondrial repair, and improving its structure and function. These findings provide a preliminary foundation for further evaluation in clinically relevant impaired-healing models.

works.title: Organotypic vascularization improves maturation of human stem cell-derived islets and restores normoglycemia in diabetic mice
works.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells-derived pancreatic islet organoids (PIOs) hold promise for treating type 1 diabetes, but poor post-transplant survival due to inadequate vascularization remains a major challenge. Here, we generated vascularized PIOs (VPIOs) by co-culturing PIOs with blood vessel organoids (BVOs), resulting in integrated structures with BVOs-derived capillary networks that penetrate into the islet structures. These blood vessels structurally exhibit fenestrations characteristic of islet-specific endothelium and carry a molecular signature of organotypic vasculature. β cells within the VPIOs display partially enhanced maturation and greater resistance to hypoxia and endoplasmic reticulum stress. Following subcutaneous transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs exhibit markedly improved survival, establish vascular connections with the host circulation, and restore long-term normoglycemia. Our work presents a strategy for generating vascularized islet organoids that enhances β cell maturation and tissue-specific blood vessel specification in vitro and, critically, improves graft survival and function in vivo.

works.title: 3D-bioprinted dual-factor nerve conduits promote neurovascular co-regeneration via activation of the PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK pathways
Animal numbers are not a proxy for scientific strength
Towards physiologically relevant human tissue models
Engineering gut microbiome states overcomes hepatic accumulation of nanomedicines
Keeping psychedelics in mind
Skin fibroblast lineage tracing reveals layer-specific cooperation in wound repair
Female iPSC X chromosome inactivation erosion and its transcriptomic effects during CRISPR gene editing and neural differentiation
works.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), together with CRISPR editing, are commonly used for studying neurodevelopmental disorders. Female iPSCs gradually lose the expression of the noncoding X chromosome inactive-specific transcript (XIST), leading to random X chromosome inactivation (XCI) erosion that affects both X-linked and autosomal gene expression. However, the effects of CRISPR editing and neural differentiation on XCI erosion and how this may confound a real-world analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are poorly understood. Here, we analyzed hundreds of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) samples of CRISPR-edited iPSC lines for 66 genes and the matched single-neuron RNA-seq data. We found variable XCI in CRISPR-edited female iPSCs, which was largely preserved in iPSC-derived neurons and predominantly influenced X-linked genes. Mechanistically, XIST mediates allele-specific epigenetic regulation of both X-linked and autosomal genes, with the former showing stronger allele-specific expression (ASE) bias that affects neurodevelopmental genes. These results have significant implications in hiPSC-based modeling of neurodevelopmental disorders.

works.title: Donor-intrinsic regenerative potential outweighs histocompatibility in iPSC-derived skeletal muscle engraftment in nonhuman primates
works.abstract: Cell-based regenerative therapies represent a promising platform for muscular dystrophies, but the role of histocompatibility for muscle engraftment remains poorly defined. Given their close genetic relationship to humans, nonhuman primate (NHP) models provide an ideal system to investigate this question. Here, we generated myogenic progenitors from induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines derived from five major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-typed Mauritian-origin cynomolgus macaques (MCMs). Following extensive characterization, one iPSC clone from each donor was selected for transplantation across distinct MHC matching conditions, including fully matched, partially matched, and mismatched recipient-donor pairs. We found that variation in regenerative potential was primarily donor-intrinsic. Strikingly, fully mismatched donor-derived myogenic progenitors exhibiting high regenerative potential consistently outperformed partially and fully matched grafts across recipients. Our results suggest that, under clinically relevant immunosuppression, donor-intrinsic regenerative potential may outweigh histocompatibility as a determinant of early skeletal muscle engraftment, supporting the development of broadly applicable off-the-shelf allogeneic iPSC-based therapies for muscular dystrophies.

works.title: Microbiota-derived SCFAs modulate Socs36E-mediated feedback to regulate intestinal stem cell proliferation upon Atg4 loss in Drosophila
works.abstract: Microbial metabolites affect host physiology, but how they link genetic defects to abnormal stem cell behavior is unclear. In Drosophila, losing Atg4 in progenitors changes the gut microbiota and raises short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), such as acetate and propionate. These SCFAs increase intracellular acetyl-CoA, which boosts acetylation by inhibiting histone deacetylases (HDACs) and activating multiple histone acetyltransferases. Chromatin immunoprecipitation identifies Socs36E as a direct acetylation target. Socs36E upregulation serves as a feedback brake on EGFR signaling. However, this brake is too weak to stop sustained proliferation, causing intestinal stem cell overgrowth. These phenotypes are abolished in a germ-free niche and can be recapitulated by SCFA-producing bacteria. Our results support a model where niche-derived metabolites drive locus-specific acetylation of Socs36E, modulating a key homeostatic node and influencing stem cell fate decisions.

works.title: Programming brain endothelial identity: Transcription factor and genome engineering approaches to improve iPSC-derived BBB models
works.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain endothelial-like cells (iBECs) serve as important human relevant in vitro blood-brain barrier (BBB) models for evaluating central nervous system (CNS)-targeted therapies. However, conventional differentiation protocols often generate heterogeneous populations constrained by incomplete endothelial maturation. Overcoming these limitations requires precise control over developmental gene regulatory networks throughout differentiation. This review examines transcription factor-based forward reprogramming strategies designed to induce brain endothelial cell fate and prime BBB identity. Integrating these approaches with novel genome engineering tools enables the rational design of next generation BBB models with improved physiological fidelity and predictive power for CNS therapeutic discovery and validation.

works.title: Perinatal nicotine exposure disrupts hematopoietic stem cell development and elevates influenza severity in adulthood
works.abstract: Developmental exposures profoundly shape lifelong health by altering disease resilience later in life. One potential cause of increased disease susceptibility is an altered immune system, originating in epigenetically maladaptive hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Here, we establish perinatal nicotine exposure (PNE) as a mouse model of developmental maladaptive immunity, wherein early-life environmental insults permanently alter HSCs. We show that PNE selectively disrupts the establishment of HSCs and tissue-resident, but not circulating, immune cells. Remarkably, the specific decrease of HSCs and lung-resident immune cells persists into adulthood. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed durable molecular reprogramming of adult PNE HSCs, with inverse regulation of positive trained immunity signatures. Functionally, adult PNE offspring challenged with respiratory virus exhibit exacerbated immune maladaptation, marked by increased weight loss, deteriorated lung pathology, hyper-permeability of pulmonary vasculature, tissue-resident macrophage depletion, and exaggerated neutrophil recruitment. Together, our findings establish that PNE imprints durable maladaptive immunity involving changes in HSCs and their progeny, suggesting a hematopoietic origin for the PNE-induced respiratory vulnerability.

works.title: Osteoporosis treatment via programmed delivery of IRF5 siRNA to macrophages in bone tissue combined with ROS scavenging
works.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PO) is not merely a consequence of increased osteoclast activity. Estrogen deficiency induces oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization in bone tissue, thereby sustaining osteoclastogenic stimuli and pathological bone resorption. Interferon regulatory factor 5 (IRF5) is a key regulator of M1 polarization, and silencing its gene by small interfering RNA (siIRF5) may attenuate the pathogenesis of PO. However, selective delivery of siIRF5 to M1 macrophages within the osteoporotic bone microenvironment is challenging. Herein, we develop a nanomedicine, termed siP@WM, for programmed sequential targeting of bone tissue and macrophages. The siP@WM integrates a platinum nanozyme core with mesoporous silica shell loading siIRF5. The shell with enlarged pores (10–15 nm) provides effective siRNA encapsulation and programmable surface grafting of two kinds of poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) derivatives. The longer poly(aspartic acid)-terminated PEG chain promotes bone enrichment. ROS-triggered thioketal cleavage shortens this chain, reduces bone-matrix adhesion, and exposes the shorter folic acid-functionalized PEG chain to enhance M1 macrophage uptake. In vitro , siP@WM scavenges ROS, facilitates endosomal escape, achieves approximately 60% IRF5 knockdown, and promotes M2 polarization. In ovariectomized mice, systemic administration of siP@WM ameliorates bone loss, restores trabecular microarchitecture and mechanical strength, and shows no overt short-term toxicity in major organs. Transcriptomic and histological analyses support attenuated AP-1-associated inflammatory signaling, suppressed osteoclast differentiation, and modulated extracellular matrix remodeling. Together, programmed siIRF5 delivery to macrophages in bone tissue combined with ROS scavenging restores bone homeostasis and provides an adaptive biomaterial strategy for PO treatment.
